quest:1001.text: Buzzbox 411. Along Darkshore’s coast, Buzzbox 411 needs thresher eyes to return to service. This Alliance errand comes through an eccentric, intoxicated gnome inventor, Wizbang Cranktoggle, who works through a mechanical relay network. After you help repair Buzzbox 827 farther south, gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle’s voice crackles through the mechanical transmitter again. From somewhere safely out of sight, he directs adventurers north along Darkshore’s mist-laden beach to a damaged terminal called Buzzbox 411. His transmissions break with hiccups and muttered praise for crawler wine. He says local aquatic predators carry what his coastal apparatus needs to keep working. To restore Buzzbox 411, thresher eyes must be fed into its waiting hatch. Darkshore threshers, aggressive marine beasts, prowl the shallows off Auberdine, and their eyes have the properties Wizbang says are needed to recalibrate the device. The eyes jolt the apparatus back into operation, and the line opens for another assignment, delivered in an even slurrier voice.

quest:1002.text: Buzzbox 323. Wizbang Cranktoggle’s field research reaches Buzzbox 323, the third stop along Darkshore’s coast. You gather six Moonstalker fangs and place them in the machine north of Auberdine. Wizbang Cranktoggle’s voice crackles through the speaker after you operate Buzzbox 411 farther south. Heavy drinking muddles his directions, but he points you north of Auberdine, to Buzzbox 323 near a road bridge. His research calls for six Moonstalker fangs from the fierce hunters roaming Darkshore’s forests. Buzzbox 323 chatters with static and faint muttering before you begin. Place the requested fangs in its intake hopper, and the machine rattles violently, grinding the teeth into dust. Wizbang’s boozy voice returns through the transceiver to celebrate your delivery and point you toward the next machine in his scattered network.

quest:1003.text: Buzzbox 525. Along Darkshore’s coast, Buzzbox 525 waits for the last of Wizbang Cranktoggle’s strange requests. The gnome’s scattered machines call for animal remnants and ever stranger materials. After Buzzbox 323 is serviced, its rattling speakers carry Wizbang Cranktoggle’s garbled instructions. His words slur through drunken chuckles and rambling directions, sending his helpers far south along Darkshore’s main road. He asks them to hunt grizzled thistle bears and place four thick scalps in Buzzbox 525’s compartment. The machine is concealed behind a fence in the brush beside the road.

quest:102.text: Patrolling Westfall. Gnoll packs roam Westfall's grasslands, threatening the people who still live there. Captain Danuvin calls on volunteers from Sentinel Hill to hunt them, fearing they work with the thieves in the Deadmines. Sentinel Hill is Westfall's main defense, held by local volunteers rather than royal troops. With Stormwind sending no soldiers to protect the outer farmlands, the people formed the People's Militia. Captain Danuvin, once a farmer in Westfall, leads them and refuses to abandon his homeland. The militia depends on travelers who pass through to help hold its perimeter against the dangers gathering across the plains. Gnolls now threaten the refugees and squatters struggling to survive in Westfall. Danuvin's scouts believe the packs are working with bandits based in the Deadmines. He sends hunters to collect gnoll paws, hoping to curb the packs' growing patrols and break any cooperation between the beasts and the outlaws.

quest:103.text: Keeper of the Flame. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the coast. The spectral sailor seeks oil to keep the beacon burning after murlocs killed the living keepers, so ships can pass the reefs safely. Westfall Lighthouse stands on a rocky islet off the zone’s southwest shore, where its light once guided sailors through the Great Sea’s shallow waters. That duty ended when Old Murk-Eye led a murloc attack and killed the keeper and his family. Captain Grayson, a sailor who died in the waters by these rocks, now watches over the tower as a ghost. Death left him unable to stop the slaughter, but he will not let the lighthouse go dark. No living keeper remains to tend the flame, so Captain Grayson needs an unusual fuel. The rogue Harvest Watchers roaming Westfall’s abandoned farmlands carry flasks of machinery oil inside their rusted bodies. Grayson sends you ashore to recover the oil from these broken constructs. With it, the beacon can keep burning and guide other captains past the reefs.

quest:1061.text: The Spirits of Stonetalon. Unrest stirs among the spirits of Stonetalon, and Zor Lonetree sends Horde champions west to learn why. From Orgrimmar, they travel past the Crossroads and report directly to Seereth Stonebreak near Greatwood Vale. In Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree listens to the natural world and feels deep distress from the Stonetalon Mountains. The elemental spirits of its rocky peaks are furious as logging tears into their forests. Horde shamans hear that unrest and fear the devastation in the western highlands will upset Kalimdor's spiritual balance. The Venture Company, an unscrupulous goblin syndicate, is cutting timber in Greatwood Vale. Its commercial crews use aggressive machinery, saws, and muscle to butcher the ancient woodland instead of harvesting sustainably. The Horde sent Seereth Stonebreak, a young shaman, to watch the forest from the frontier and rally defenders against the ravagers.

quest:109.text: Report to Gryan Stoutmantle. Westfall needs fighters, and Report to Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to answer the call. The crown leaves the outer farmlands to fend for themselves, so local defenders gather under Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Westfall calls for skilled fighters from across the river. Brigands, gnolls, and hostile harvest golems are driving the farmlands into chaos. With no royal battalions answering, local volunteers must defend the realm. The road leads you to Gryan Stoutmantle in the stone tower atop Sentinel Hill. He leads the People's Militia, a force of farmers, retired veterans, and mercenaries formed in response to royal inaction. The farmlands face a bitter guerrilla war against lawlessness.

quest:1097.text: Elmore's Task. Smith Argus sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind to help Grimand Elmore. The dwarven weaponsmith needs help with a delivery bound for his kin in Khaz Modan, and Argus trusts you to make the journey. In Goldshire, blacksmith Smith Argus watches for travelers he can trust with work beyond clearing wolves and kobolds. Grimand Elmore, a skilled dwarven weaponsmith in Stormwind, has asked for help with a delivery to his kin in Khaz Modan. Argus sees you as fit for the journey and sends you toward the city gates to answer Elmore's call. Stormwind and Ironforge depend on open trade and goodwill to keep both realms supplied and united. Argus says Elwynn Forest needs defenders, but honoring promises to the dwarves matters too. In northeastern Stormwind, the Dwarven District leads you to Elmore's shop, where a journey beyond the forest begins.

quest:1099.text: Goblins Win!. In Thousand Needles, a goblin race ticket pays off when the goblins come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The goblin race ticket is the stub that counts when the goblins win. Hold on to it, and a goblin prize box is yours once the result is in. The gnome ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

quest:111.text: Speak with Gramma. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks Gramma Stonefield's help to meet Maybell Maclure. Their families' bitter feud keeps the young lovers apart, and Tommy Joe hopes his grandmother can find a way for them to see each other. Tommy Joe Stonefield and Maybell Maclure keep their romance secret from their feuding families. The Stonefields and Maclures have fought over their farms for years, making their neighboring homesteads hostile ground. Tommy Joe wants to meet Maybell without provoking violence between their kin, so he turns to his grandmother for help. Gramma Stonefield stays indoors, but she knows the feud well. She understands that the families cannot truly unite while their bad blood remains. Still, she will not let their grudge crush young love. Rather than urge caution, Gramma begins looking for small chances to bring Tommy Joe and Maybell together.

quest:112.text: Collecting Kelp. In Goldshire, Maybell Maclure seeks a way to visit Tommy Joe Stonefield unseen. William Pestle needs rare crystal kelp to brew an invisibility liquor for her. The feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families keeps Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield from meeting openly. Maybell wants to see her beloved without provoking an armed clash between their kin, so she seeks a way to cross the valley unseen. William Pestle, an herbalist and apothecary at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, plans to brew an invisibility liquor. The rare ingredients he needs are not in the inn's cupboards. Crystal kelp is the catalyst William Pestle needs for his brew. The fronds usually grow far out in saltwater oceans, but tribal murlocs have carried stashes inland to their crude camps along Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. Their peculiar instincts have led them to haul the marine plants to the freshwater shore. You need to recover enough fronds from the murlocs before returning to Goldshire with them.

quest:114.text: The Escape. Maybell Maclure waits for a way to slip away from her family and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. You bring her William Pestle's Invisibility Liquor, brewed from crystal kelp gathered across the region. The Maclures and Stonefields have feuded for generations, leaving no room for courtship. Gramma Stonefield turns to William Pestle, an alchemist in the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. With crystal kelp from nearby lakes, Pestle brews Invisibility Liquor strong enough to hide Maybell's escape from the Maclure homestead.

quest:1141.text: The Family and the Fishing Pole. Gubber Blump and his heirloom Fishing Pole await a catch on Auberdine's docks. Hostile murlocs keep the town's small fishing boats ashore, so Gubber seeks help catching native Darkshore grouper from the coast. Gubber Blump takes pride in a family known for its skill with a fishing line. Night elves make up most of Auberdine, though dwarves and gnomes have settled around its docks and port. Gubber spends his days gazing over the Veiled Sea instead of digging into stone, hoping to bring in the local catch. Darkshore grouper thrive along the coast and make versatile food, but they can put up a lively fight on the line. Local fishermen usually row small boats into deeper waters to catch them. Now aggressive murlocs prowl the coast, and small boats no longer go out. Gubber fears the creatures are eating the local fish, so he asks travelers to fish from shore. Gubber gives a Blump Family Fishing Pole to anyone who brings him a hearty catch. He believes anyone who can land a batch of feisty groupers is worthy of his family's legendary anglers, including his cousin Graun Blump. For Gubber, handing over a family rod is the highest mark of respect.

quest:117.text: Thunderbrew. In Westfall, Grimbooze Thunderbrew is gathering what he needs for his next batch. Fresh hops keep his ale from turning thick as stew, and he shares kegs with those who help. Grimbooze Thunderbrew keeps his family's brewing tradition alive far from Dun Morogh. Even across Westfall's turbulent plains, he insists on the right ingredients: without proper hops, his current brew may turn into thick stew instead of refreshing ale. Grimbooze celebrates hops, barley, yeast, and malt in cheerful rhymes. With fresh hops, he finishes the fermentation on the spot. Those who supply him receive whole kegs of Thunderbrew Lager, a brew known for its forceful taste.

quest:1174.text: Gnomes Win!. In Thousand Needles, a gnome race ticket pays off when the gnomes come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The gnome race ticket is the stub that counts when the gnomes win. Hold on to it, and a gnome prize box is yours once the result is in. The goblin ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

quest:119.text: Return to Verner. You carry fifty freshly forged horseshoes from Goldshire back to Lakeshire. Smith Argus has finished the order, and Verner Osgood is waiting across the border in Redridge. Smith Argus has forged fifty horseshoes for Lakeshire, and you carry them east from Goldshire. Redridge faces supply shortages and gnoll attacks. The iron shoes help keep horses and draft animals working on its rugged mountain roads. Verner Osgood is relieved when the horseshoes arrive, but Smith Argus has attached a bill to the crate. Verner is annoyed that the Goldshire smith expects payment. Redridge faces pressing dangers, leaving little time to argue over the charge.

quest:12.text: The People's Militia. At Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle tests your mettle for the People's Militia. Stormwind's throne is distracted, and its army is absent, so local volunteers defend Westfall from the Defias Brotherhood. You begin by driving outlaws from the northern fields and mines. Westfall once fed Stormwind, but outlaws, vagrants, and thieves now overrun the region. With the capital sending no royal soldiers to patrol the countryside, Gryan Stoutmantle organized the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill as a local defense force. He calls for decisive action to reclaim Westfall. Anyone seeking the militia's badge must prove they can fight and will protect innocent settlers. Before Stoutmantle trusts new recruits with deeper operations, he sends them against Defias forces near northern homesteads. Defias Trappers and Smugglers work openly near Jangolode Mine, Molsen Farm, and Furlbrow's Pumpkin Patch, pillaging stores and ambushing travelers. You can disrupt their foraging by driving them out, while showing Stoutmantle's scouts that you have the grit for a long fight against crime.

quest:120.text: Messenger to Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire is desperate for military aid as gnolls and Blackrock orcs encircle the town. Unable to spare garrison troops, he dispatches an adventurer to carry 'The State of Lakeshire' directly to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind City. Lakeshire stands on the brink of collapse. Gnoll packs contest every road, Blackrock orcs raid from the north, and the local guardsmen are stretched beyond their limits. Magistrate Solomon cannot afford to send fighting men on a days-long ride to the capital, leaving an independent traveler to carry his official plea for regular troops to the city gates. Delivering the magistrate's report brings an adventurer face-to-face with General Marcus Jonathan, commander of Stormwind's defense. While Jonathan respects Solomon's leadership and acknowledges the urgency, army protocol prevents him from mobilizing without a royal directive. The defense of Redridge must await formal consultation with the young King Anduin and the regency council.

quest:121.text: Messenger to Stormwind. You carry General Marcus Jonathan's reply from Stormwind to Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten the town. The capital offers no troops, leaving the settlement to face danger while Stormwind's leaders delay. You brought Magistrate Solomon's plea for reinforcements to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind. Now you carry his preliminary reply back to Redridge while he waits for approval from the throne. Without royal authorization, the General cannot commit the army. Lakeshire's citizens remain without city guards, and each day brings the settlement closer to falling under the Blackrock clan.

quest:123.text: The Collector. An intercepted dispatch from gnoll raiders in Elwynn Forest lays out when gold shipments leave the abandoned mines. It is addressed to a figure called 'The Collector' and points to an organized operation near Stormwind's garrison. Riverpaw gnoll packs in western Elwynn Forest carry more than furs and crude weapons. Among them, a parchment called the Gold Pickup Schedule lays out dates and times for gold taken from local mines. The intercepted note directs each shipment to an overseer identified only as 'The Collector.' Marshal Dughan hears the news at the Lion's Pride Inn and learns that gold is still being mined and moved. Official mines across Elwynn have been closed for months because of gnoll attacks, kobold infestations, and roaming bandits. Gnolls carrying shipping schedules point to an organized criminal network stealing the kingdom's wealth.

quest:13.text: The People's Militia. Across Westfall, The People's Militia faces a growing Defias threat. Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteers now confront thieves who have moved beyond highway robbery to ransack Moonbrook and the Gold Coast Quarry, and the Militia calls for harsher retaliation. Defias attacks have grown from petty banditry on the roads into a wider threat. Defias Looters and Pillagers, who hurl fire, have overrun Westfall's economic centers. They occupy Moonbrook, strip the Alexston Farmstead, and have taken control of the Gold Coast Quarry. Gryan Stoutmantle sees the danger: if the brigands hold these places, Westfall may become impossible to reclaim without a formal royal army. Stormwind has sent Gryan Stoutmantle no soldiers or supplies, so he calls on the Holy Light and the resolve of Westfall's remaining farmers. The Militia's war of attrition depends on volunteers carrying the fight into Defias strongholds. Driving out the looters will deny the Brotherhood resources and show fearful residents that defenders still fight for Westfall's peace and prosperity.

quest:132.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood is building a network beyond banditry. Wiley the Black sends word of its ties to gnolls, kobolds, and goblins. Gryan Stoutmantle needs this intelligence to measure the full reach of the conspiracy choking Westfall. Wiley the Black says telling what he knows about the Defias could cost him his life. Along the edges of Redridge and Westfall, he has caught wind of an operation far greater than highway robbery. His sealed note describes how the Brotherhood has coordinated groups that are usually hostile to one another across the countryside. Wiley warns that the Defias has drawn an alarming network around itself. The red-masked outlaws have enlisted gnoll packs, kobold diggers, and goblin engineers instead of working alone. Together, their brutal muscle, burrowing labor, and mechanical cunning point to an enterprise beyond what the People's Militia first expected. Gryan Stoutmantle has little love for Wiley and openly laments that he did not leave the rogue to rot when he had the chance. Yet Westfall cannot afford pride. With Stormwind ignoring pleas for military aid, the People's Militia must take useful intelligence wherever it can find it.

quest:1338.text: Stormpike's Order. In Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike is arranging a shield from Furen Longbeard. The armorsmith works far south in Stormwind City, so Stormpike asks a traveler to carry his order there. Mountaineer Stormpike wants a new shield, and he trusts only Furen Longbeard to forge it. The mountaineer is willing to pay well to place the commission in the smith’s hands, though Loch Modan and Stormwind City lie far apart. Stormpike wonders why Furen works so far from Ironforge and the Great Forge, where many dwarves make their home. He suspects Stormwind’s humans pay the smith a king’s ransom. When the order reaches Furen at his anvil, the armorsmith takes pride in hearing from the prestigious Stormpike clan and eagerly prepares to forge the shield.

quest:135.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's troubles reach Stormwind. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to deliver Wiley's Note to Master Mathias Shaw, suspecting a link between the Defias and the old Stonemasons Guild. A mention of the Stonemasons in Wiley's communications catches Gryan Stoutmantle's attention. The builders rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War, but the guild has long been thought scattered or dissolved. If the Defias Brotherhood shares ties with them, Westfall's rural insurgency is more than a disorganized band of outlaws. From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle cannot confirm his suspicions. He sends you to Master Mathias Shaw, head of Stormwind's covert intelligence wing, SI:7. Shaw works from the Barracks in Old Town, gathering whispers and secrets from across the realm. He may be able to untangle the Defias Brotherhood's origins.

quest:1358.text: Sample for Helbrim. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim awaits a wolf heart from across the sea. Apothecary Zinge sends it from the Undercity to support the Forsaken's research in central Kalimdor. Apothecary Zinge sends a Wolf Heart Sample from the Undercity to Apothecary Helbrim in the Barrens. The Royal Apothecary Society's experiments reach beyond the ruins of Lordaeron. After Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine sent tainted organs, Zinge sought to extend their research across the world. Now a courier carries the sample overseas to Helbrim, an alchemist stationed in the Barrens' dry savanna. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim studies how Kalimdor's native beasts react to compounds from the Plaguelands. The wolf heart could show how those toxins affect local creatures. Helbrim believes that dissecting and testing it alongside them will help the Forsaken master poisons and unnatural afflictions.

quest:136.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A battered parchment map sets Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure in motion along Westfall's coast. The hunt begins with a search of the shoreline for the late captain's personal footlocker, then leads toward his hidden plunder across the region. Shipwrecks and the restless spirits of drowned sailors mark Westfall's western coast. Captain Sanders, an old seafarer, met a watery grave there. He left cryptic instructions so his hard-won fortune would not be lost to the Great Sea or taken by scavengers. A determined adventurer can retrace the trail he left behind.

quest:138.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. In Westfall, Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure sends you inland after a clue found by the shore. The trail leads east from the coast toward a barrel near ruined stonework. Captain Sanders sends you inland after the first cipher is solved. The clue points away from the shore and up the rocky bluffs, toward Westfall's main roads. An old chimney among roadside ruins marks the next stop. A discarded barrel nearby hides another message, and the ruined farmstead gives Sanders a landmark for the trail.

quest:139.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A broken barrel on Westfall's western shore holds Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure clue. It sends you north toward an old jug beside a coastal windmill, another step along the late pirate's trail to his hidden riches. Captain Sanders scattered his directions along Westfall's western shore. Each clue leads only to the next container, never straight to the prize. You have to follow the trail from one barrel, chest, or jug to another across the bluffs to reach his plunder. From the broken barrel, the parchment points due north toward the sea cliffs. Beside an isolated windmill on the bluffs, an abandoned jug holds the next clue. Murlocs and Defias scavengers roam coastal Westfall, so the way north carries danger.

quest:140.text: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A whiskey-soaked clue sends Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure hunt west from Westfall's shore. The trail leads out across the Great Sea, away from the mainland's troubles, to a remote islet. Captain Sanders scattered clues along Westfall's coast for any adventurer bold enough to follow them. The last parchment came from the dregs of his favorite whiskey jug and gives the final bearing. The captain's words are clear: head west to the water's edge, then swim out into the waves.

quest:141.text: The Defias Brotherhood. Mathias Shaw sends a confidential report from Stormwind to Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Shaw has investigated the former Stonemasons Guild to help Stoutmantle uncover the origins of the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:143.text: Messenger to Westfall. Messenger to Westfall is an Alliance errand carrying an urgent plea from Magistrate Solomon in Redridge across Elwynn to Westfall. Facing total abandonment by the Stormwind military, Lakeshire's leadership seeks mutual aid from Gryan Stoutmantle's newly formed People's Militia. Magistrate Solomon finds Lakeshire in a desperate situation. The Redridge Mountains are besieged by Blackrock orcs and gnolls, yet the Stormwind Army has failed to arrive in force. Recognizing that Lakeshire cannot survive on town guards and irregulars alone, Solomon writes a formal plea for assistance. With regular royal reserves nowhere in sight, he turns his eyes west, having heard word of a citizen defense group forming beyond Elwynn Forest. The intended recipient of the dispatch is Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran commander who has begun rallying volunteer fighters under the banner of the People's Militia. By sending a courier directly across the kingdom, Solomon hopes that Westfall's organized volunteers might spare troops to reinforce Lakeshire's borders until the Crown's armies finally mobilize. However, as messengers soon discover, Westfall is mired in its own catastrophic struggles against the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:144.text: Messenger to Westfall. A letter from Westfall brings Magistrate Solomon a hard answer in Lakeshire. He asked Gryan Stoutmantle for soldiers to defend Redridge, but Westfall has been left to face its own troubles. Magistrate Solomon faces growing troubles in the Redridge Mountains without Stormwind's royal garrison. He looks to the southern frontier for help and writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall. Solomon hopes the volunteers at Sentinel Hill can spare fighters to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. He does not know how hard pressed the western plains are. Gryan Stoutmantle refuses, though the answer weighs heavily on him. Westfall is fighting the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls because the House of Nobles and the crown have abandoned the kingdom's breadbasket. The People's Militia formed so the people could survive. Its ranks lose good men each day, and Stoutmantle cannot spare a single fighter for Redridge.

quest:1462.text: Earth Sapta. Earth Sapta is a replenishment ritual offered by Seer Ravenfeather in Camp Narache. Young shaman undertaking their initiation to commune with the spirits of the stone require this draught to open their inner sight. Should a novice lose or spill their prepared brew before finishing their rite, the seer prepares another to ensure their trial may continue. The path of the shaman begins with attuning the mortal senses to forces beyond physical sight. To perceive the elemental spirits of the land, an initiate must ingest a potent ritual brew known as a sapta. Infused with natural essences bound to the element of stone and soil, the Earth Sapta lifts the veil between the physical realm and the spiritual plane, allowing a novice to commune directly with the earth elementals of Mulgore. The spiritual arts demand discipline, but seasoned seers recognize that young initiates often falter or misplace sacred reagents while braving the wilds. Seer Ravenfeather keeps a steady vigil at Camp Narache, ensuring that any pupil who loses their brew before their communion at the stone monument can renew their preparation. With quiet patience, she provides another vessel so the novice may face the spirits unbroken.

quest:1463.text: Earth Sapta. In the Valley of Trials, an initiate who loses the Earth Sapta can ask Canaga Earthcaller for another. The replacement gives the young shaman a chance to commune with the spirits of the land, along with a warning to guard sacred draughts carefully. A misplaced Earth Sapta can interrupt an initiate's communion with the spirits of stone and soil. Prepared through specific rituals, the elemental brew thins the veil between the physical realm and the spirits. When an initiate loses or spills it while traveling through Durotar, Canaga Earthcaller prepares another in good faith, but warns the novice to guard sacred gifts with greater care. Canaga Earthcaller watches over fledgling shamans emerging from the Den in the Valley of Trials. He understands that young orcs and trolls are prone to the chaos of early trials, but stresses that elemental spirits do not take kindly to negligence. Accepting a second sapta offers a small lesson in humility: power granted by the earth must be guarded and respected.

quest:147.text: Manhunt. Marshal Dughan sends you after a Defias bagman called the Collector in Elwynn Forest. The Collector works from the overrun Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and sends stolen gold from the forest's mines into the Brotherhood's coffers. Marshal Dughan sends you to Brackwell Pumpkin Patch after Elwynn's gnolls are found carrying a schedule for gold pickups. Defias bandits and gnolls have taken over the once quiet homestead. The Collector hides among its overgrown vines, skimming ore from the kingdom's mines and arranging shipments for the growing rebellion.

quest:1470.text: Piercing the Veil. Piercing the Veil is an introductory warlock trial given by Venya Marthand in Deathknell. It tests a freshly risen warlock's resolve by directing them to collect skulls from nearby mindless skeletons. Completing the task earns the novice the knowledge required to summon and bind an imp minion. Newly awakened Forsaken warlocks begin their journey in Deathknell under the instruction of Venya Marthand. She teaches that true strength lies not in raw brute force, but in knowledge and the precise mastery of chaotic powers. To prove they possess the focus and capability required to pierce the veil between worlds and subjugate nether beings, novices are dispatched to harvest the skulls of restless Rattlecage Skeletons roaming near Deathknell's abandoned smithy. Once the skeletal remains are secured, Venya considers the initiate ready to step beyond simple dark spells. The recovered materials serve as a rite of passage, demonstrating that the novice can overcome mindless undead and withstand the bleak realities of their craft. In return, Venya imparts the rituals needed to bend an imp to the summoner's command, warning that despite the demon's diminutive stature, its cunning and fire will make it a dangerous ally.

quest:1471.text: The Binding. The Binding is the culminating rite for Forsaken warlocks seeking to command a voidwalker. In the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Carendin Halgar requires initiates to summon, conquer, and permanently subjugate a creature of the Void. Unlike minor imps, which are easily coerced into pacts with dark magic, creatures of the Void despise reality and possess formidable physical might. To earn the right to summon a voidwalker, an aspiring warlock in the Undercity must prove total mastery over it. In the shadowed enclave of the Magic Quarter, the Forsaken mentor Carendin Halgar provides the mystic runes required to tear a voidwalker from the Nether into the physical realm. The ritual takes place within the glowing summoning circle etched beneath the mentor's dais. Once the runes are activated, an unbound voidwalker materializes in fury. Subduing it is not an exercise in diplomacy; the summoner must break the entity through sheer arcane force and raw will. Only when the entity is thoroughly crushed does Carendin reveal the true formula of summoning, binding the creature's essence to the practitioner indefinitely.

quest:1473.text: Creature of the Void. Creature of the Void is a pivotal rite of passage for Forsaken warlocks, tasking them with recovering a lost arcane text from the Scarlet Crusade. To learn how to summon and bind a chaotic voidwalker, an initiate must venture west into Tirisfal Glades and retrieve Egalin's Grimoire from hostile zealots. Within the dark alcoves of the Temple of the Damned in the Undercity, Carendin Halgar oversees the development of rising Forsaken summoners. When an acolyte proves competent enough to wield power beyond petty imps, Halgar directs them toward binding a creature forged from pure shadow and chaos: the voidwalker. Rather than relying on simple instinct, Forsaken practitioners base their summons on the meticulous research of Egalin, Halgar's own former master, who first penned the rituals necessary to subjugate these monstrous denizens of the void. Mastery of the voidwalker cannot be achieved without Egalin's Grimoire, which contains the precise methods for channeling such volatile magic. However, the precious tome was stolen by an agent of the Scarlet Crusade—a zealot named Perrine stationed in an outpost tower to the west. While Perrine and his crusaders likely viewed the grimoire as mere blasphemous contraband to confiscate and hoard, recovering it is essential if the Forsaken are to secure the ritual secrets before attempting to tear open the veil.

quest:1478.text: Halgar's Summons. Halgar's Summons is a formal directive given to rising Forsaken warlocks who have reached a critical threshold in their dark craft. Master Carendin Halgar requires their presence in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity to begin rigorous advanced training. Answering his call sets the stage for summoning and binding dangerous entities from the Nether. When a warlock operating around Brill or the Tirisfal wilderness demonstrates adequate control over basic fel energies, word reaches the deeper subterranean halls of the Undercity. Senior practitioners such as Ageron Kargal serve as talent spotters, relaying notices to those who show genuine promise. To be summoned by Carendin Halgar is both a rare privilege and a perilous undertaking, indicating that basic imps and petty curses no longer suffice for the practitioner's education. Halgar oversees warlock rites from the shadowed reaches of the Magic Quarter, situated near the sinister altar known as the Temple of the Damned. Forsaken darkcasters operate without the squeamish moral restrictions of the living, yet even they demand rigorous discipline when dabbling in planar summonings. Halgar does not tolerate hesitation or sentimentality; his summons expects immediate deference and complete readiness to confront the hostile horrors of the Twisting Nether.

quest:1485.text: Vile Familiars. Near the Den, Vile Familiars threaten every warlock who seeks the power of demons. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength against them and bring back their heads. This is the humble, dangerous first step toward mastering fel power under the Horde’s watchful eyes. Warlocks live uneasily within Thrall’s new Horde. Demonic corruption and blood pacts once brought ruin to the orcs, leaving deep scars and distrust. Fel magic is tolerated in Durotar, but its practitioners are neither loved nor welcomed. Many warlocks live in seclusion, practicing in shadowed places like the Den, away from prying eyes. There, they teach the few initiates daring enough to follow their path. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength before he teaches you the dangerous rites for bending an imp to your will. Vile Familiars skulk near a cave northeast of the Den and hurl bolts of flame at those who approach. Slay these lesser demons and bring back their heads to show you can overcome the fiery creatures you hope to control. Only then can you face the danger of the magic you seek to command.

quest:1492.text: Wharfmaster Dizzywig. At Ratchet's pier, a crate of alchemy supplies waits for passage across the sea. Wharfmaster Dizzywig arranges its journey to the Old World aboard a ship bound for Blackwater Cove. A crate of potions and reagents waits at the Barrens port, bound for colleagues in the Old World. Caravans that might have carried it have already departed, so you are asked to take the secure shipment to Ratchet's water's edge. The port offers a route across the Great Sea between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Wharfmaster Dizzywig handles cargo on Ratchet's wooden piers. He tracks shipments in ledgers and manifests, then finds space aboard vessels sailing east across the Great Sea. This crate is booked for a ship bound for Blackwater Cove.

quest:1498.text: Path of Defense. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek prepares young Horde warriors to defend those who cannot defend themselves. He sends them to Thunder Ridge to prove their endurance against its electric beasts. At the Far Watch Post, Uzzek teaches young warriors that defense is part of the Horde's duty. The post lies on the border between the Barrens and Durotar. Uzzek says a warrior's highest calling is to stand between danger and those unable to defend themselves, taking the blows so the Horde can endure. Uzzek sends the novices to Thunder Ridge, north across the Southfury River in Durotar, to test their stamina and resolve. Thunder lizards and lightning hides roam the canyon. The initiates must survive the beasts' jolts and harvest their singed scales to show they have the fortitude to hold the front line.

quest:1499.text: Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Ruzan sends warlock initiates against vile familiars. After you slay them, you report to Zureetha Fargaze, who oversees the effort to curb the Burning Blade. Warriors and scouts in the Valley of Trials answer directly to Zureetha Fargaze, who sends them to curb the Burning Blade Coven. Warlock initiates first answer to Ruzan, their shadowy mentor. He demands proof that you can master lesser demons before sending you back to aid the Horde's defense. Your work serves both the warlocks and the safety of the Den. Zureetha Fargaze watches the northern cavern above the Valley of Trials. Vile familiars hide within, the weakest pets of the Burning Blade cultists. Their presence in the sacred training grounds insults the orcs and threatens the Valley. When you report your success, you show that those who practice fel magic remain ready to defend Durotar from corruption.

quest:15.text: Investigate Echo Ridge. Marshal McBride sends recruits north as kobolds gather at Echo Ridge Mine. The mine supplies ore and raw materials to Northshire Abbey and the Stormwind guard, and the growing threat puts both at risk. After early skirmishes with scattered vermin around Northshire's forested edge, scouts report a more organized threat. Kobolds have gathered in force at Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride sends you north to face the workers at the entrance and learn how deeply they have settled in. Echo Ridge Mine supplies ore and raw materials to the Northshire brotherhood and the Stormwind guard stationed there. Kobolds have seized the tunnels, halting extraction and exposing the strain on local defenses. McBride asks you to cull ten workers, but the infestation runs deeper into the shafts than a surface patrol can reach.

quest:1501.text: Creature of the Void. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye sends a young warlock after the stolen Tablet of Verga. The rogue Burning Blade cultists took it to their cavern at Skull Rock, and its runes are needed to summon a voidwalker. Gan'rul Bloodeye trains Horde warlocks in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. Thrall's new realm regards fel magic with deep wariness because of the orcish clans' dark history. Gan'rul says few true warlocks remain in the Horde, but their perilous skills are essential to its survival. To serve the Warchief, an initiate must learn more than the chaotic fire of an imp; they must command beings of pure shadow and endurance. The runes needed to summon a voidwalker are inscribed on the Tablet of Verga. The Burning Blade, a fanatical shadow cult, stole the relic and hides in a cavern at Skull Rock, right beneath the Warchief's nose. Gan'rul sends you into the cultists' den to recover the tablet and strike a bloody blow against the renegades who stain the name of all practicing warlocks.

quest:1502.text: Thun'grim Firegaze. Atop Thorn Hill, Thun'grim Firegaze keeps to a reclusive life and a solitary forge. After their first lessons in defense, Horde warriors cross the Barrens to find him and seek steel fit for their growing skill. After you show skill in the defensive arts under veteran trainers like Uzzek, you are sent to sharpen your fighting with suitable steel. Ordinary armories can carry a frontline fighter only so far. True mastery calls for a personal weapon from a smith of renown. In the Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze is that smith, an aging orc who has left settlement life behind to keep an isolated forge high above the plains. Thun'grim Firegaze lives atop Thorn Hill, a jagged rise east of the Crossroads where wild raptors and hostile quilboar roam. He spends his solitary hours shaping metal, far from the protection of town walls. Decades of gazing into blistering forge flames have ruined his eyesight, though his instincts remain sharp. When you climb the heights and disturb his solitude, Firegaze knows why: a warrior has come seeking forged steel.

quest:1503.text: Forged Steel. Thun'grim Firegaze waits in the eastern Barrens for the steel stolen from his camp. He offers to forge a weapon for the warrior who brings it back. Thun'grim Firegaze keeps a smithy in the eastern Barrens, far from Orgrimmar. Years at the forge have dimmed his sight. The nearby Razormane quilboar used that weakness to steal an iron chest from his camp. Some snorted and made noise on one side to draw his gaze while others slipped in from the other and carried off his forged steel bars. Thun'grim is angry at the theft, but doubts the Razormanes can use the steel. Quilboar craft with stone, tusks, and thorny roots, not refined metal. The heavy chest remains near a broken wagon in their camp, untouched and useless to them. For Thun'grim, its steel is the stock he needs to forge weapons for young Horde warriors.

quest:1504.text: The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation ritual in Orgrimmar for young Horde warlocks seeking command over a voidwalker. Under the direction of Gan'rul Bloodeye, the petitioner inscribes glyphs from the Tablet of Verga within Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle to call forth, subdue, and perpetually enslave a creature of the Void. For an initiate warlock lurking in the dark tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow, summoning an imp is merely child's play. Subduing a voidwalker is the first true test of willpower and arcane dominance. Warlocks do not form polite pacts or commune with these otherworldly horrors; they wrest them across dimensions through raw force and bind them in eternal servitude. Gan'rul Bloodeye demands that the initiate draw upon the glyphs transcribed from the Tablet of Verga, calling the monstrosity directly into Neeru Fireblade's ritual circle to break it in single combat. Overcoming the entity in physical and magical combat is only half the battle. As Gan'rul Bloodeye warns, a bound voidwalker never truly accepts its enslavement. Though it serves its master as a durable, shadowy bulwark in battle, it perpetually searches for lapses in concentration. A warlock must maintain an unwavering mental grip over their servant, for the moment discipline falters, the voidwalker will happily consume the soul of the one who bound it.

quest:1506.text: Gan'rul's Summons. Gan'rul's Summons is an urgent call delivered to young Horde warlocks by Ophek in Razor Hill. Senior warlock Gan'rul Bloodeye requires their immediate presence in the Cleft of Shadow to advance their training. It marks the first step toward mastering the dark art of summoning a voidwalker. Novice warlocks operating in Durotar do not remain unnoticed for long. Once a practitioner demonstrates sufficient mastery over their initial imp, word reaches the deeper subterranean recesses of Orgrimmar. Ophek, stationed out in Durotar, acts as a messenger for the senior dark casters, intercepting warlocks with an urgent demand to drop whatever they are doing and report to the Cleft of Shadow. Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the training of nascent orc warlocks within the Horde. Operating out of the hidden caverns beneath Orgrimmar, he maintains a delicate balance between honing lethal fel power and keeping such dangerous arts shielded from the disapproving gaze of the Warchief. When Bloodeye calls an apprentice to his circle, it signals that simple fire spells and imps are no longer enough; it is time to bind a creature from the Twisting Nether.

quest:151.text: Poor Old Blanchy. Verna Furlbrow waits beside the road in Westfall with her stranded family and starving mare. Their wagon broke during an attempt to escape, leaving Old Blanchy exhausted. Verna asks you to gather oats from nearby abandoned farmsteads and feed the old horse. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow are stranded beside Westfall's main road. Bandits and rogue mechanical harvest golems have driven families like theirs from their homes. As the Furlbrows tried to haul their belongings to safety, their wagon broke down, leaving them marooned in open country. Old Blanchy has plowed and hauled for the Furlbrow family across many seasons. Now exhausted from pulling their overloaded cart and starved by the delay, the gentle mare is fading fast. Verna asks you to search nearby overrun farmsteads for sacks of oats, where hostile threshers and gnoll scavengers threaten. The grain could give the faithful animal a decent meal.

quest:1516.text: Call of Earth. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller sets novice Horde shamans a test of endurance and patience. They hunt felstalkers to prepare a ritual sapta. A shaman begins by learning to bond with each element. For orcs and trolls, that path starts with earth, the bedrock of life, endurance, and patience. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller guides new shamans and teaches them that earth demands respect and steadfastness before it grants protection. The Burning Blade cult festers in ravines north of the Valley of Trials. Its dark magic summons felstalkers, corrupt hounds from beyond this plane. Hunting them tests whether a shaman can defend the land from unnatural decay. Canaga uses their hooves to brew an Earth Sapta, a sacred draft that opens mortal eyes to the elemental plane.

quest:1517.text: Call of Earth. At Spirit Rock, Canaga Earthcaller guides young shaman through their first communion with the elements. They drink an Earth Sapta on sacred ground to see the Minor Manifestation of Earth. A sapta is a mystical draught known to only a few shaman masters. Made with elemental magic, it bridges mortal perception and the spiritual plane, granting Sapta Sight to the strong-willed. Because it binds the drinker's spirit directly to an element, tradition forbids drinking it outside consecrated holy ground. To commune with earth, you leave the Valley of Trials and climb the Hidden Path into Durotar's southern crags. Spirit Rock waits at the trail's end, an elevated sanctuary overlooking the rugged wasteland. Drink the sapta there, and you can perceive what ordinary eyes cannot: an elemental presence among the stone. The Minor Manifestation of Earth asks no bloodshed or submission. It asks only that you stand humbly before the world. Fire, water, and air bear turbulent, volatile, often chaotic spirits, while earth teaches steadiness. Mountains offer endurance, and plains teach boundless patience.

quest:1518.text: Call of Earth. In Durotar, a young shaman communes with a manifestation of the earth spirit. The initiate returns to Canaga Earthcaller with rough quartz and receives a first elemental totem. A novice shaman seeks communion with the earth through patience and humility, not brute strength. The Minor Manifestation of Earth grants the initiate a piece of rough quartz. The small stone proves the spirit has accepted the initiate’s pledge and remains a seed of power. You complete the trial by bringing the quartz to Canaga Earthcaller in the Valley of Trials. Canaga shapes it into an Earth Totem, the focus through which you channel the ground’s steadfast protection and strength. The rite begins your path through the four elemental disciplines and lays the foundation for a lifetime of communion with the natural world.

quest:152.text: The Coast Isn't Clear. Along Westfall's western shore, shipwrecked sailors face murloc tribes on the beaches. Captain Grayson at the Westfall Lighthouse calls for help clearing the coast so survivors can reach land safely. Westfall's western coast has claimed countless ships. Reefs, sudden squalls, and jagged rocks break vessels against the shoals. Survivors may cling to wreckage and crawl ashore, hoping for rescue. But murloc tribes control the beaches and show no mercy to castaways. Captain Grayson tends the Westfall Lighthouse from a lonely outcropping southwest of the mainland. Death has bound him to the post, yet he remains watchful over passing ships and sailors in need. Murlocs make the shore deadly, from Coastrunners in the north to Tidehunters, Warriors, and Oracles in the south. Grayson calls on travelers to clear the coastline.

quest:1520.text: Call of Earth. This sacred rite marks a tauren shaman's spiritual attunement to the element of earth. By drinking an Earth Sapta at a holy rock east of Camp Narache, initiates peer beyond physical senses to commune directly with a Minor Manifestation of Earth. A sapta is a carefully concocted ceremonial potion crafted by shamanic elders to bind an initiate's mortal spirit directly to a primal element. Prepared with ancestral magic, only a select few among the tauren preserve the secrets of its brewing. When imbibed at a designated sacred site, the draught expands the imbiber's mind, piercing the veil between the physical realm and the spiritual plane so the elements can be witnessed in their raw form. East of Camp Narache stands Kodo Rock, a looming stone pillar that serves as a holy sanctuary. Consuming the sapta here reveals the Minor Manifestation of Earth awaiting the pilgrim. Unlike the volatile, fiery, or raging aspects of nature encountered later along the shaman's path, the spirit of earth asks only that the initiate approach in quiet humility, granting the mountain's enduring strength and the plains' calm patience to all who honor the land.

quest:1521.text: Call of Earth. This rite concludes a young tauren shaman's initial communion with the spirits of the land in Mulgore. After drinking the Sapta of Earth and speaking directly with a spirit manifestation, the initiate receives a fragment of raw stone to bring home. Returning to Camp Narache marks the fledgling mystic's formal bond with the first of the four elements. Upon communing with the Minor Manifestation of Earth atop the crags near Red Cloud Mesa, the spirit yields a simple Rough Quartz. Though plain in appearance, the stone represents an elemental pact and the endurance of stone itself. The spirit reminds the young shaman that patience and strength are the core virtues demanded by the earth, promising that mutual respect will grant harmony with the land. Returning to Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather uses the gifted quartz to fashion the shaman's very first Earth Totem. Far more than a decorative symbol of status, the totem serves as a permanent physical and spiritual anchor. Through this carved focus, the initiate channels the grounding, protective magic of the earth itself, taking the first true step along the fourfold elemental path.

quest:1524.text: Call of Fire. In the Barrens, an aspiring shaman begins the second trial in the search for communion with fire. Kranal Fiss sends the initiate across the Southfury River to a secluded mountaintop shrine in Durotar, carrying the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame. Kranal Fiss entrusts the shaman with the Torch of the Dormant Flame. Raw mystical strength alone cannot meet fire’s demands; the trial calls for temperance, focus, and respect. The torch is both ritual instrument and proof to the shrine’s keeper that the bearer has been judged ready to attempt the trial. The shrine lies across the Southfury River, among Durotar’s southern crags. A weathered stone carved with a fire rune marks an obscure path that climbs toward one of the region’s highest peaks. At the summit, the Shrine of the Dormant Flame is watched by Telf Joolam, a troll hermit. He turns away curious travelers and treasure hunters, keeping the sacred brazier from ordinary eyes until a petitioner arrives with the unlit torch.

quest:1525.text: Call of Fire. Telf Joolam sends a shaman across Durotar and the eastern Barrens for a Fire Sapta's ingredients. The draught prepares an initiate to perceive and speak with fire spirits. A Fire Sapta opens a shaman’s senses to the Eternal Flame. Like the draught for earth, it lets a shaman see and speak with spirits hidden from mortal sight. Telf Joolam sends initiates across Durotar and into the eastern Barrens to gather ingredients bound to heat and flame. Razormane quilboar spellcasters in the eastern Barrens carry fire tar, made in their earthy rituals. Burning Blade cultists carry the other needed ingredient in Dustwind Cave, in the ravines northeast of Razor Hill. The cultists use fire for destruction and demonic chaos, while the reagents in their pouches hold a natural tie to the element.

quest:1526.text: Call of Fire. Atop Durotar's peaks, a shaman faces the trial that attunes them to fire. Telf Joolam guides the initiate to drink fire sapta, confront a Minor Manifestation of Fire, and claim its glowing ember to light the ceremonial torch. Fire spirits hide from untrained eyes on Durotar's summit. To see them, you drink fire sapta, a draught made from reagents gathered across the barrens and coast. It sharpens your senses to the unseen, revealing minor spirits and manifestations among the summit crags. A Minor Manifestation of Fire waits atop the mountain. Once the sapta takes hold, the spirit knows you can see it and awaits your challenge. Fire answers strength and decisive action, so you strike without delay. The longer the fight lasts, the more fiercely the elemental fire burns.

quest:153.text: Red Leather Bandanas. At Sentinel Hill, Red Leather Bandanas mark the fight against the Defias Brotherhood. Scout Galiaan offers a reward for the red cloth masks worn by the outlaws, as the People's Militia struggles to track them across Westfall. Across Westfall, the red bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. The gang draws cutpurses, looters, and traitors from many walks of life, but its members rally beneath the same crimson sign. Scout Galiaan and the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill collect the bandanas as proof that bandits have fallen. The cloth also helps them follow the Defias as their fronts shift across the countryside. Stormwind has denied Westfall proper military support, so the People's Militia depends on seasoned observers like Scout Galiaan to chart Defias activity. Galiaan watches outlaw patrols from Sentinel Hill. Passing adventurers and militia volunteers take on the dangerous work of bringing down the highwaymen who have driven honest farmers from their land.

quest:155.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the People's Militia seeks the Defias Brotherhood's hidden base. A turncoat agrees to guide Alliance champions there in exchange for protection. The road passes through Moonbrook, where Edwin VanCleef's inner sanctum lies hidden. Gryan Stoutmantle's fight against the Defias Brotherhood reaches a turning point when a captured brigand agrees to talk. His former brothers may execute or assassinate him, so the Defias Traitor bargains with the People's Militia. Escort him safely through hostile territory, and he will reveal where Edwin VanCleef and his ringleaders hide. The thieves' network silences those who speak out, and the turncoat needs armed protection along the road.

quest:1579.text: Gaffer Jacks. In Auberdine, Wizbang Cranktoggle needs his lost gaffer jacks back. The gnome inventor tossed a box of hardware into the sea during his voyage from Ironforge, and anglers can search for it along Darkshore's coast. Wizbang Cranktoggle crossed the Great Sea from Ironforge to find quiet in Darkshore. The gnome inventor drank too much on the voyage. Leaning over the rail in a drunken haze, he lost a crate of specialized metal parts called gaffer jacks in the water near Auberdine. Wizbang says gaffer jacks are essential precision tools. Without them, he cannot properly tune his stintle pegs or continue his delicate tinkering. Unwilling to wade into the cold surf himself, he asks local anglers to cast along Darkshore's shore and fish up the scattered parts.

quest:1580.text: Electropellers. In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle asks anglers to recover his lost electropellers. He lost the prototype parts in freshwater streams after a mishap with an explosive duck decoy. Wizbang Cranktoggle spends an evening searching inland Darkshore for a place to test his latest invention. The gnome tinkerer, stationed in Auberdine, has built a self-propelled, exploding duck decoy. After drinking too much, he blacks out and wakes hours later back in town with singed hair and an empty pack. His bag of electropellers has fallen into one of the coastal rivers. Wizbang asks local fishermen to dredge Darkshore's freshwater streams because he does not want to brave the wilds himself. Anglers fishing the Wildbend River and Cliffspring River can snag the buoyant metal parts alongside local fish. With the components recovered, the gnome can resume his erratic waterfowl experiments.

quest:1581.text: Elixirs for the Bladeleafs. Syral Bladeleaf seeks help keeping her family’s busy trade supplied in Dolanaar. Her husband spends nearly all his time brewing, and fresh elixirs could ease his workload while earning the brewer uncommon herbs. Dolanaar draws travelers, sentinels, and druids moving through Teldrassil. Syral Bladeleaf and her husband have built a flourishing herb and alchemy trade to serve them. Demand keeps her husband bent over vials and cauldrons for nearly all his hours, leaving the couple little time together. Syral turns to passing herbalists and brewers to ease her husband’s workload. She asks for Elixirs of Lion's Strength and Minor Defense, offering freshly gathered, uncommon herbs in exchange. For a fledgling alchemist practicing beneath the Great Tree, the exchange brings a bundle of herbs and a chance to turn common forest flora into coveted regional flora.

quest:1582.text: Moonglow Vest. In Darnassus, Lotherias needs leather gear for young adventurers setting out across Kalimdor. She offers the pattern for a Moonglow Vest in return for shipments of embossed leather goods. In Darnassus, leatherworkers work to outfit sentinels and young scouts. Night elves and allied wanderers leave Teldrassil for the wilds of Kalimdor, where sturdy armor is in demand. Lotherias is among the master leatherworkers supplying them with gear. Lotherias asks apprentices to bring matched embossed gloves, boots, and cloaks as proof of their skill. Those who meet her order earn her trust, and she teaches them a night elf pattern for the Moonglow Vest, made to protect while allowing free movement.

quest:1598.text: The Stolen Tome. In Northshire Valley, a novice human warlock is sent to recover a forbidden tome and prove their skill. Drusilla La Salle hopes to claim Powers of the Void from the Defias, whose camp lies in the vineyards. Warlocks in Stormwind's lands hide their craft and keep prying eyes from their research. Northshire Abbey guards forbidden grimoires in its archives. Drusilla La Salle, the warlock mentor on the abbey grounds, covets Powers of the Void but cannot risk suspicion from the clerics and paladins by entering the library's protected wing herself. An abbey novice joins the Defias Brotherhood and steals several valuable texts on his way out. He flees to the Northshire Vineyards and takes refuge around the Defias campsite. The thieves stash their prize in a field tent, unaware of the danger in the book's dark arts. Recovering the tome tests a novice warlock's nerve and opens the way to darker knowledge. Braving the bandit camp and returning the text satisfies Drusilla's ambition and proves the pupil is ready. She rewards the pupil with the dark rites to summon and bind an imp, the first demon an apprentice learns to command.

quest:1599.text: Beginnings. Beginnings is a rite of passage for fledgling Alliance warlocks starting in Dun Morogh. Under the begrudging tutelage of Alamar Grimm, novices are dispatched to harvest magical feather charms from nearby Frostmane troll novices to prove their competence before mastering the art of summoning an imp. Within the safe haven of Anvilmar, dark magic is not openly celebrated, but it is tolerated out of necessity. Alamar Grimm, an established warlock, conducts his occult research in relative discretion. When new practitioners show raw promise, Grimm is asked by unnamed parties who have taken an interest in the recruit to step away from his studies and assess the recruits personally. Before granting a novice the secrets to enslaving lesser demons, Grimm requires practical proof of both physical endurance and magical affinity. Nearby Frostmane troll novices, gathering in a cave southwest of Anvilmar, carry primitive feather charms infused with subtle primal magics. Harvesting these charms proves the aspiring warlock can conquer a magical adversary, while also providing Grimm with curious specimens for his ongoing research. Returning with the charms satisfies Grimm that the novice has sufficient will to survive. The trial culminates in teaching the summoning of the imp, the warlock's most foundational minion. Grimm offers a stern warning alongside the ritual: despite their diminutive stature, imps wield chaotic fire magic that can easily overpower an undisciplined master.

quest:16.text: Give Gerard a Drink. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works long days in the fields and needs fresh spring water. He trades apples for water brought by passing travelers. Elwynn Forest's farms supply grain, fruit, and vegetables to Stormwind's townsfolk and garrisons. Tending crops under the open sky is hot, demanding work. Gerard Tiller spends long days in the dirt at the Maclure Vineyards, keeping pests away and managing the harvest. With little time to return to town wells, he relies on passing recruits to bring clean spring water so he can keep working. Gerard trades provisions instead of coin. Travelers with extra flasks of Refreshing Spring Water can exchange them for fresh apples from the orchard. The kingdom stretches its resources to maintain order and feed its army, so direct barter between smallholders and recruits remains a practical way to get by in rural Elwynn.

quest:1638.text: A Warrior's Training. In Goldshire, A Warrior's Training sends young warriors to Stormwind for lessons in battlefield endurance. Lyria Du Lac directs them to the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Old Town, where veteran Harry Burlguard offers seasoned instruction. After aspiring fighters show reliable command of the fundamentals against threats across Elwynn Forest, their trainers see little more for Goldshire drillmasters to teach. Lyria Du Lac sends recruits into Stormwind, toward the gritty district of Old Town. Veteran fighters gather there to share combat experience far from the royal garrison’s rigid ways. Harry Burlguard, an aged battle veteran, keeps his quarters at the Pig and Whistle Tavern. He tests a warrior’s mettle with tavern grit and practical stamina instead of parade-ground drills. Before teaching defensive maneuvers that help soldiers survive dangerous campaigns, Harry expects new arrivals to match his appetite for drink and face local brawlers in the tavern.

quest:1639.text: Bartleby the Drunk. In the Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby the Drunk faces a test set by Harry Burlguard. An aspiring Alliance warrior must take Bartleby's prized mug before Harry will teach deeper combat skills. Harry Burlguard asks for proof of a novice's backbone before teaching deeper combat skills in the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Across the room, Bartleby nurses his drinks at the far end of the counter. Harry wants you to take the man's mug, knowing Bartleby would rather fight than surrender his ale. The challenge puts a warrior's resolve to the test. Soldiers, laborers, and rough locals fill the Pig and Whistle, where polished manners count for little. Bartleby mocks newcomers as too prissy for a tavern scuffle instead of answering politely. The exchange leads to a brawl on the floorboards, where a warrior's training in Stormwind begins with a test of basic barroom fighting.

quest:1640.text: Beat Bartleby. In Stormwind, Bartleby guards the mug a young warrior must claim. The instructors send recruits to face him in a bare-knuckle fight and earn the vessel for their training. Stormwind's warrior instructors expect recruits to face combat without excuses or grand ceremony. As part of their formal training, young warriors must retrieve a particular mug from Bartleby, a notorious drunkard who lounges in the city. He scoffs at polite requests and swears no one will take his prized drinkware without prying it from his cold, dead fingers. For a fledgling warrior, words soon give way to a fistfight. Bartleby boasts that he will fight to the death, but a thorough thrashing is enough to sober him. Once beaten, his bravado gives way to bruised admiration. He recognizes that his opponent is tougher than they appear and yields peacefully, letting the victor claim the mug and complete the trial at the training hall.

quest:1641.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides young paladins through a solemn rite. Under Duthorian Rall's care in the Cathedral of Light, you face teachings on virtue, devotion, and the duties that come with the Holy Light. Duthorian Rall guides those who answer the paladin's calling in the Cathedral of Light. Early training teaches martial discipline and the order's rites, but advancement asks for a deeper commitment to the spirit. The trials ask you to look beyond battle and weigh the moral duties of a paladin. Stormwind faces dangers within its borders and beyond, and its people need defenders who understand that duty. Receiving the Book of Divinity binds you to service and self-sacrifice. Duthorian asks you to study the holy text and learn what the Light demands of its defenders. Its lessons prepare paladins to oppose the Scourge's creeping horrors and protect common folk. Righteous power must answer to virtue and compassion.

quest:1645.text: The Tome of Divinity. The Tome of Divinity marks an essential milestone in a dwarven paladin's training within Ironforge. Bestowed by Tiza Battleforge in the Hall of Mysteries, this holy text begins a trials-based journey meant to test an initiate's devotion to the Light and their readiness to defend Azeroth against dark forces like the Scourge. Paladin mentors across the eastern kingdoms direct promising initiates to Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries once they demonstrate mastery of martial and spiritual fundamentals. Under the watchful eye of Tiza Battleforge, young dwarven paladins are introduced to the solemn principles that separate a simple warrior from an ordained champion of the Holy Light. Taking up this task represents a conscious pledge toward lifelong self-sacrifice, duty, and spiritual discipline. Accepting this charge places a Book of Divinity into the hands of the novice. This text outlines the expectations, virtues, and spiritual tenets required to wield sacred energies effectively against wicked threats. Studying its teachings is merely the introductory step; the scripture serves as a foundational guide before the initiate is sent forth across Khaz Modan and beyond to embody its lessons in real acts of faith.

quest:1665.text: Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, Bartleby's Mug marks a young warrior's trial of grit. After besting Bartleby in the Pig and Whistle Tavern, you claim his drinking mug for your trainer, Harry Burlguard. Harry Burlguard tests young warriors with a brawl in Old Town. He asks you to take down Bartleby, a stubborn drunk at the bar of the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Once subdued, Bartleby reluctantly gives up his prized drinking mug, but first takes one final swig to drain the dregs. Returning the mug to Harry Burlguard completes your novice trial. Burlguard sees that you can persuade through sheer force and recognizes your readiness for defensive mastery. He points you onward to further battlefield instruction with Marshal Haggard, a seasoned veteran in Elwynn Forest.

quest:1666.text: Marshal Haggard. At Eastvale, Marshal Haggard keeps the arms he gathered over a lifetime of service. Harry Burlguard sends novice warriors from Stormwind City to meet the retired marshal and seek better weapons. Stormwind's novice warriors need more than skill to face danger beyond the city. Harry Burlguard sends promising fighters east through Elwynn Forest to find Marshal Haggard, a retired officer who served the realm for years. Haggard gathered a personal armory over a lifetime in the field, and his home near the Eastvale Logging Camp holds weapons for young warriors seeking better arms. Marshal Haggard lives in a secluded manor near the Eastvale Logging Camp. Years of service have weakened his failing sight, and he sometimes mistakes approaching travelers for prowling riverpaw gnolls. Though age keeps him in this quiet corner of eastern Elwynn, Stormwind's guards and trainers still respect the old marshal.

quest:1667.text: Dead-tooth Jack. A stolen badge puts Marshal Haggard's authority in Defias hands. The retired officer lives in eastern Elwynn Forest, where Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into surrendering his official insignia. Jack wore a Stormwind tabard in the dark and posed as Marshal Dughan. Haggard needs the badge back before the Defias Brotherhood can use it to impersonate Stormwind officials. Marshal Haggard lives in an isolated cottage on Elwynn's eastern ridges. One night, a figure in a Stormwind tabard approached, claiming official business and asking for Haggard's old marshal's badge. Believing he was handing it to a fellow officer, Haggard complied. The stranger laughed in his face and vanished into the woods. The thief was a Defias rogue called Dead-tooth Jack. Marshal Haggard has retired, but his old badge still carries the legal weight of Stormwind. Defias bandits are creeping across Elwynn, Westfall, and Redridge, and the badge could help them pass guard checkpoints, redirect patrols, or take command of supplies. Jack retreated to a camp to the south and left the badge locked in a strongbox. Haggard needs it recovered before the Defias can cause serious harm.

quest:1679.text: Muren Stormpike. Muren Stormpike is an introductory quest for developing Alliance warriors, given once a recruit proves their basic mettle in Dun Morogh. Directed by Granis Swiftaxe in Kharanos, the young fighter travels into the mountain city of Ironforge to seek formal instruction in martial discipline. Meeting Muren marks the beginning of deeper training in tactical stances and dwarven military traditions. After cutting their teeth against local threats in the snowy valleys of Dun Morogh, warrior novices catch the eye of Granis Swiftaxe in Kharanos. Recognizing that crude skirmishing can only take a brawler so far, Swiftaxe sends promising fighters to the heart of dwarven martial prowess: the Military Ward of Ironforge. There, within the echoing halls of the forge-city, senior combatants oversee the formal schooling of those bound for battle. Upon reaching the Hall of Arms, recruits are introduced to Muren Stormpike, a seasoned veteran of a storied dwarven clan. Muren cares little for tavern tales and demands proof that his new charges can withstand real combat. Reporting to him opens the pathway toward mastering the defensive arts, learning to absorb and control enemy aggression, and earning well-crafted iron armaments fit for true front-line duty.

quest:1681.text: Ironband's Compound. Ironforge smith Tormus Deepforge seeks vengeance for his mentor, Sturgy Ironband, whose remote teaching outpost in eastern Dun Morogh fell to a sudden and bloody assault. The slaughter followed the arrival of a rare umbral ore shipment, which immediately drew the violent attention of the Dark Iron dwarves. Sturgy Ironband was revered across Ironforge as an unmatched instructor of the smithing craft. From his secluded compound south of Helm's Bed Lake, he instructed promising pupils far from the crowded anvils of the Great Forge. That peaceful enterprise ended abruptly when one of his students acquired an unfamiliar mineral dubbed umbral ore. Intrigued by its properties, Ironband resolved to experiment with the sample, entirely unaware that possessing it had marked his school for ruin. Shortly after the umbral ore reached the compound, hostile Dark Iron dwarves launched a ruthless surprise attack against the outpost. The assailants showed no mercy, slaughtering Sturgy Ironband and every apprentice under his care before occupying the grounds. Tormus Deepforge, one of Ironband's surviving proteges based in the capital, refuses to let the massacre stand, dispatching Alliance travelers to avenge his teacher and recover the cursed ore that brought destruction to the encampment.

quest:1683.text: Vorlus Vilehoof. In Darnassus, young night elf warriors face a trial set by Elanaria. They must hunt a satyr who has defiled a hidden moonwell near the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Elanaria asks you to prove your dedication and discipline before she teaches advanced martial techniques. She needs more than words from those who defend Kalimdor. A guardian must face corruption and cleanse the sacred boughs of Teldrassil. Your trial leads to Vorlus Vilehoof, a satyr hiding at a moonwell in the mountains southeast of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Satyrs were once ancient betrayers, twisted by demonic influence, and they hate sacred Kaldorei relics. Vorlus bathes in the moonwell, fouling its blessed waters and mocking the grace of Elune.

quest:1685.text: Gakin's Summons. A summons delivered to promising Alliance warlocks by Remen Marcot on behalf of Gakin the Darkbinder. It directs fledgling practitioners down into the crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter to begin their next stage of dark occult training. Demonology is strictly outlawed across the civilized districts of Stormwind, yet dark arts persist right under the noses of the city guard. When a warlock displays sufficient proficiency with their introductory imps, word quietly travels to senior practitioners. Remen Marcot delivers the message with deliberate discretion, urging initiates to keep the meeting place quiet and head into the shadowy recesses beneath the Mage Quarter. Behind the modest facade of the Slaughtered Lamb tavern lies a network of damp cellars and hidden catacombs. Here, shielded from prying Kirin Tor mages and the Cathedral's inquisitors, Gakin the Darkbinder oversees the instruction of Stormwind's warlocks. The summons serves as the gateway to commanding a voidwalker, a rite requiring dangerous stolen reagents and perilous summoning circles.

quest:1686.text: The Shade of Elura. At Auberdine, Elura's shade guards a sunken ship and its Elunite ore. Elanaria sends young night elf warriors into the waters to lay the captain to rest and recover her medallion and ore for a weapon forged by Smith Mathiel. Long ago, a ship carrying rare Elunite ore struck jagged coastal rocks near the Auberdine lighthouse and sank. The captain, Elura, cursed her own soul in despair and out of unwavering duty. Bound to the wreck beneath the waves, her shade guards the lost cargo from anyone who would disturb it. Elanaria sends young night elf warriors into Darkshore's surf to defeat Elura, recover her medallion, and salvage the ore. They need both the medallion and ore to put the captain to rest and bring the metal to Smith Mathiel's forge. The work tests their martial skill and respect for the fallen, and provides the ore for a crafted weapon.

quest:1688.text: Surena Caledon. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin seeks his former pupil and a bloodstone choker. He sends an aspiring warlock after Surena Caledon, who betrayed him to join the Defias Brotherhood. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novices the forbidden arts of fel summoning. He once took a young woman named Surena Caledon as his pupil. He admired her natural magical talent and her beauty. Surena left her studies and Gakin's favor, then fled Stormwind with her lover, Erlan Drudgemoor, to join the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:1689.text: The Binding. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder puts a novice warlock through a final trial. With his recovered Bloodstone Choker, you draw a voidwalker into a hidden circle and force it to submit. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, forgotten catacombs run beyond the watchful gaze of the Silver Hand and Kirin Tor magistrates. Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novice warlocks that dark magic demands more than channeling power; they must also dominate otherworldly beings. You have recovered Gakin's stolen Bloodstone Choker from Surena Caledon. Now he asks you to call a voidwalker into the summoning circle beneath the tavern. A voidwalker will not bargain with you. The power in the Bloodstone Choker opens a rift and draws the shadow creature into the mortal world. You must batter it with magic and force until its will breaks, proving you can command it. Once defeated, the voidwalker's essence binds to you, giving you a durable, shadowy protector that can endure punishment in the battles ahead.

quest:1692.text: Smith Mathiel. In Darnassus, sacred ore is on its way to the forge. After you recover elunite from the shipwreck off Auberdine, Elanaria sends you to Mathiel to have it shaped into a weapon for the Kaldorei. Elanaria sends you across Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace with the elunite ore you recovered from the haunted shipwreck off Auberdine. The warrior trainer packs it in a sturdy case and directs you to Mathiel, one of the capital's finest smiths. He can shape the metal into a weapon worthy of your calling. Mathiel treats smithing as a craft of devotion. Elunite bears the sacred blessing of Elune, the Moon Goddess, and he accepts the case as an honor. He will shape the holy metal into arms to defend the young boughs of Teldrassil.

quest:1693.text: Weapons of Elunite. In Darnassus, Weapons of Elunite brings a young warrior's early rite of passage to its close. After recovering ore blessed by Elune, you bring it to Mathiel to forge arms for a defender of Kalimdor. Night elf warriors defend Teldrassil and the kaldorei people. Promising young warriors gather elunite, a mineral blessed by the Moon Goddess, rather than relying on mundane steel alone. Its ore calls for a smith skilled in metalcraft and mindful of Elune's gift. Smith Mathiel works in Darnassus, shaping blessed elunite into weapons of war. He considers the work an honor, not routine metalcraft. When you bring him the ore, he fashions arms to suit your style and rewards your service with weapons blessed by your goddess.

quest:170.text: A New Threat. A New Threat is an early combat assignment issued by Balir Frosthammer in Coldridge Valley. Dwarven mountaineers have been caught off-guard by a sudden surge of troggs bursting out across Dun Morogh, threatening local settlements and camps. Coldridge Valley was long regarded as a protected haven for young dwarven warriors and mountaineers training in Dun Morogh.
