That peace shattered when subterranean Rockjaw troggs began clawing their way to the surface in startling numbers. Reports quickly reached Anvilmar that troggs were swarming the frozen lake and surrounding foothills, disrupting daily patrols and cutting off vital supply routes through the valley pass. The crisis peaked when the creatures mounted a coordinated assault on a dwarven encampment to the west, forcing the mountaineers to retreat and abandon their posts. Shorthanded and unable to spare full battle regiments from Ironforge, Balir Frosthammer has turned to newly recruited adventurers to cut through the Rockjaw ranks and secure the hills before the beasts push straight to Anvilmar's doorstep.

quest:1715.text: The Slaughtered Lamb. This errand directs novice gnome warlocks out of Ironforge to seek advanced instruction in human lands. With King Magni Bronzebeard keeping a vigilant watch on dark practitioners within the dwarven mountain, mentors must rely on Stormwind's hidden networks to complete their disciples' training. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, aspiring warlocks in Khaz Modan studied under their own tinker-mages and demonic scholars deep within the techno-city. The disaster that drove the gnomes into exile scattered those institutions. The surviving practitioners found themselves cramped into Ironforge's gloomy, subterranean caverns, operating under the distrustful eye of King Magni Bronzebeard and the dwarven guard. Unable to practice demonic arts openly or cultivate dangerous rituals in such tight quarters, senior instructors like Lago Blackwrench have little choice but to send their students away. The destination for these expatriate students is the Slaughtered Lamb, an unassuming tavern nestled in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Beneath its taproom, concealed behind twisting stone passages and descending stairs, lies a subterranean sanctum where human warlocks gather in shadows. Overseen by seasoned summoners like Gakin the Darkbinder, the cove provides the space and dark paraphernalia required to teach novices how to summon and bind minor demons without drawing the immediate wrath of city marshals. While Stormwind's coven welcomes capable hands, the influx of refugee novices creates friction. Human mentors already walk a knife's edge to avoid detection from the city's paladins and authorities. Gakin and his colleagues find their clandestine sanctuary increasingly crowded by practitioners sent south from Khaz Modan. The steady stream of dwarven-mountain traffic risks blowing the lid on their discreet operation, yet neither side possesses an easier alternative.

quest:176.text: Wanted: "Hogger". Wanted: "Hogger" is an Alliance bounty posted outside Goldshire for the head of a massive, savage gnoll chieftain. Hogger prowls the southwestern woods of Elwynn Forest and has violently thwarted every attempt by the local authorities to bring him down. While Elwynn Forest struggles with banditry and kobold infestations, the gnoll tribes in the south have grown bolder and more organized under the brute leadership of Hogger. Towering over typical Riverpaw gnolls, Hogger has established camp near the Forest's Edge, ambushing travelers and overpowering the local militia patrols sent to subdue him. With the Stormwind Army stretched thin and unable to spare regular forces to police the outskirts of the capital, Marshal Dughan took the unusual step of posting an open bounty on the beast. Taking down Hogger requires venture into deeply hostile gnoll territory, and his ferocity has earned him a reputation as the deadliest threat facing novice adventurers in Elwynn.

quest:179.text: Dwarven Outfitters. Dwarven Outfitters is an introductory survival task in Coldridge Valley offered by Sten Stoutarm. In exchange for culling local wolves and gathering their tough meat for winter rations, fresh recruits are rewarded with sturdy gloves to ward off frostbite in Dun Morogh's biting cold. The high mountain pass of Coldridge Valley is brutally cold, and unprepared travelers quickly learn that standard kit is no match for the elements. Standing outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm offers a straightforward frontier bargain to new recruits: venture into the snowy drifts, hunt down the prowling wolves, and bring back cuts of tough meat to help supply the outpost. In return, he provides proper cold-weather gloves to ensure young adventurers keep all ten fingers. While wolves represent a perpetual hazard to dwarven scouts and fledgling gnomes training in the valley, they are also a vital resource. Their meat sustains the garrison stationed at Anvilmar, and culling their numbers keeps the paths between the local encampments somewhat safer. Stoutarm's arrangement serves a double purpose—testing a recruit's ability to handle the local wildlife while stockpiling food for the bitter nights ahead.

quest:18.text: Brotherhood of Thieves. Deputy Willem sends recruits across Northshire's eastern river to face the Defias Brotherhood. Their red burlap bandanas give Stormwind its first tangible evidence of the brigands' organized presence in the valley. Northshire Valley has long been a safe haven in Elwynn Forest, guarded by Stormwind and used to train recruits and Clerics of the Holy Light. Recently, discipline along its perimeter has frayed. Vagrants and thieves have crossed the eastern river, lurking near the woods and making small camps close to the abbey. Deputy Willem maintains local order, but the guards cannot spare the manpower to watch every corner of the valley without volunteers. These outlaws are coordinated and wear matching attire. They call themselves the Defias Brotherhood, and their red burlap bandanas mark their allegiance. Deputy Willem sends recruits to drive back the brigands and recover their masks, hoping to curb their advance and learn how deeply the Defias have reached into the kingdom's heartland.

quest:1818.text: Speak with Dillinger. Speak with Dillinger is a Horde military directive issued in Brill. Austil de Mon, the warrior trainer at the Gallows' End Tavern, dispatches able-bodied fighters to Deathguard Dillinger at the west end of the village to take on a hazardous combat mission in service of Lady Sylvanas. Within the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, the warrior trainer Austil de Mon keeps a watchful eye out for promising combatants willing to serve the Dark Lady. When the Deathguards require capable hands, de Mon directs unproven adventurers out of the tavern and into the field. Deathguard Dillinger, who oversees security on the western edges of Brill, has requested someone with martial competence for an urgent task. Brill sits squarely on the front line of Tirisfal Glades, where the Forsaken must constantly prove their martial dominance against hostile threats. Dillinger's post near the village graveyard puts him in prime position to manage local incursions. For the young warrior, reporting to Dillinger is more than a simple errand: it is a formal test of combat prowess and political loyalty to the newly forged Forsaken nation.

quest:1819.text: Ulag the Cleaver. Ulag the Cleaver is a rite of passage for young Forsaken warriors in Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Dillinger tasks you with releasing and executing an enslaved Scourge warrior bound inside a northern mausoleum, testing your martial resolve and earning the respect of the Deathguard. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the Forsaken managed to capture a peculiar undead warrior who named himself Ulag the Cleaver. While Ulag possessed a conscious, lucid mind, his spirit remained inextricably dominated by the psychic thrall of the Lich King. Seeking to understand how the Scourge binds free will, the Forsaken kept him restrained under a magical seal beneath a mausoleum north of Brill, hoping to break the entity's spiritual chains. All efforts to sever Ulag from the Lich King's mental grip ended in failure. Recognizing that true freedom could only come through destruction, Deathguard Dillinger repurposed the captive as a trial of combat for rising Forsaken warriors. By disturbing the skull stone trigger outside the crypt, a warrior breaks the protective wards, releases Ulag from his imprisonment, and grants him release at the edge of an axe.

quest:182.text: The Troll Cave. Assigned by the mountaineer Grelin Whitebeard, this mission dispatches adventurers to cull young Frostmane trolls gathering in the southern caves of Coldridge Valley. With the Ironforge Senate preoccupied by an escalating trogg crisis, lone scouts and willing recruits must handle border skirmishes before the trolls establish a permanent foothold. While Ironforge's regular forces are consumed with repelling rock-jawed trogg incursions across the snowfields, the southern approaches cannot be left unguarded. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were deployed by the mountain authorities to assess whether the native ice trolls posed an immediate danger to the heartland. Perched on a bluff overlooking the frozen valley, Grelin maintains a solitary watch on their movements. Grelin's reconnaissance revealed that the local Frostmane clan had begun settling in a deep cave along the southern ridgeline of Coldridge Valley. Believing full military mobilization would be an unnecessary waste of dwarven manpower, the scout favored hiring capable local volunteers to cull the aggressive whelps. Thinning their young fighters serves to disrupt their encampment before the Frostmane can mount coordinated raids against nearby dwarven homesteads.

quest:1820.text: Speak with Coleman. Speak with Coleman is a transitional task in Tirisfal Glades offered to champions who have proven their worth against the Scourge. Deathguard Dillinger directs capable warriors from the town square to the local tavern to assist Coleman Farthing with personal and factional vendettas. After assisting in the containment of severe local threats—such as laying to rest dangerous Scourge remnants like Ulag the Cleaver—adventurers earn the personal trust of Deathguard Dillinger. As one of the sentinels watching the roads into Brill, Dillinger judges who is capable of handling more than routine perimeter patrols and points capable fighters toward citizens in need of specialized service. Not every conflict in Tirisfal Glades is fought on high command orders from the Undercity. Across the ruined kingdom of Lordaeron, surviving undead carry deep grudges tied to the lands, families, and fortunes they left behind. Coleman Farthing bides his time within the Gallow's End Tavern, seeking an instrument of vengeance to strike back at the threats lingering near former settlements like the Agamand Mills.

quest:1821.text: Agamand Heirlooms. Coleman Farthing tasks adventurers with plundering the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern end of Agamand Mills. Driven by bitter resentment over his mortal demise, he seeks to strip his former masters of their ancestral weapons and erase their final remnants of dignity. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Coleman Farthing served the wealthy and influential Agamand family at their expansive mills in Tirisfal Glades. Whatever occurred during the fall of their estate, Farthing blames his former lords entirely for his death. Now raised into undeath among the Forsaken, he views the Agamands' downfall with spiteful satisfaction, rejoicing that the once-proud dynasty has been reduced to mindless minions enslaved to the Lich King. To completely extinguish what remains of the family's prestige, Farthing sends adventurers into the Agamand Family Crypt nestled beneath the northern bluffs of the mills. Within its haunted stone halls, the restive dead wander alongside lingering Scourge. Farthing demands the extraction of four storied relics—the Agamand family sword, axe, dagger, and mace—ensuring their bloodline's legacy is stripped of every remaining shred of honor.

quest:183.text: The Boar Hunter. The Boar Hunter is an early errand given by the dwarf hunter Talin Keeneye in Coldridge Valley. A surge in the local crag boar population has made the woods overly dangerous, and young recruits are tasked with culling the aggressive beasts so seasoned hunters can track in peace. Coldridge Valley is typically a quiet, protected training ground for young mountaineers and scholars of Ironforge. However, the wildlife often grows restless and overabundant in the harsh winter climate. Talin Keeneye, a veteran hunter stationed outside Anvilmar, notices that the aggressive small crag boars have multiplied so rapidly that they pose a genuine threat to anyone wandering the snow-covered trails. Hunting is a cornerstone of dwarven life, providing meat, hide, and essential fieldcraft practice. Yet when game becomes a nuisance that attacks on sight, culling is required to restore balance. By trimming the crag boar numbers across the valley slopes, young adventurers prove their combat readiness while giving local hunters room to pursue their sport without getting overwhelmed.

quest:184.text: Furlbrow's Deed. The Furlbrows flee their farm as Defias bandits carry their land grant through Elwynn Forest. Returning the deed to Farmer Furlbrow near the Westfall border preserves the couple’s claim to their stolen homestead. Defias bandits in Elwynn carry a land deed signed by Theodore and Verna Furlbrow. A crude note on its back says they drove the elderly farmer from his property, then carried the document across the river into Elwynn to copy it and forge claims to other seized land. The note says the Furlbrows were stranded just over the border, beside the road, after their wagon broke. The Defias have driven dozens of families from their ancestral land in Westfall. With Stormwind’s army absent and the realm’s resources strained, the Brotherhood uses force and false claims to seize the kingdom’s breadbasket. Theodore and Verna are leaving their farm for safety, but their lawful deed preserves their claim if order ever returns to the province.

quest:1858.text: The Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, Therzok tests rogues seeking a place in the Shattered Hand. He asks them to open Tazan's recovered satchel with a key taken from an unwitting accomplice. After retrieving Tazan's locked satchel, you find it useless without the key. The Shattered Hand demands skill, not brute force against the complex lock. Therzok sends you to Gamon, a tauren drunkard who frequents Orgrimmar's tavern. Gamon is easily distracted and once helped Tazan, making him a fitting mark for quiet theft. Take the key from Gamon without alerting the tavern, then open the satchel and claim Tazan's logbook. Bring the stolen contents to Therzok in the Cleft of Shadow to meet the Shattered Hand's standards. A clean job earns you formal recognition as one of its operatives.

quest:1859.text: Therzok. In Orgrimmar, Therzok waits for a promising rogue from Durotar. Kaplak has seen your skill with violence and stealth and sends you to the Cleft of Shadow to meet a Shattered Hand operative. Kaplak draws promising young rogues aside when they begin making a name for themselves in Durotar. The new Horde honors Thrall, but not all its servants fight openly beneath his banner. Word of a fighter skilled in violence and stealth, willing to bend the rules of open warfare, reaches the underground guild in Orgrimmar. Kaplak sends you beneath Orgrimmar's red stone cliffs to the Cleft of Shadow. Therzok waits in its gloom, out of sight of the city's grunts. There, lone cutpurses and ambushers are brought into the Shattered Hand, the Horde's covert network of daggers in the dark.

quest:1860.text: Speak with Jennea. In Goldshire, Zaldimar Wefhellt sends novice mages to Stormwind for further instruction. He directs apprentices who have advanced beyond basic training in Elwynn Forest to Jennea Cannon in the Wizard's Sanctum. Zaldimar Wefhellt sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind City as your training advances. Your time learning elementary spells from local tutors in Elwynn's hamlets has run its course. In the Mage Quarter, the Wizard's Sanctum is where the kingdom's senior mages pursue arcane study and instruction. They coordinate magical matters across the realm. Zaldimar says your report concerns the security of Elwynn Forest and Stormwind, not only your studies. In Stormwind, you report to Jennea Cannon, a mage who oversees local assignments. She is cautious about sharing grand secrets with a newly arrived apprentice, but your report begins your service to the wizarding order.

quest:1861.text: Mirror Lake. Novice Alliance mages in Stormwind's Mage Quarter are sent to sample Mirror Lake's waters for magical contamination. Jennea Cannon sends them southwest of the city gates to test the waterfall spray. Azeroth's arcane currents were shaken by conflicts from the opening of the Dark Portal through the Third War and the battle at Mount Hyjal. Those shocks tore ancient currents from their stable channels. In Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, magi like Jennea Cannon watch the changes closely. They fear that displaced arcane power could reach the wilderness and corrupt local ecosystems. Mirror Lake lies beneath the cliffs southwest of the Stormwind gates and is a primary natural reservoir fed by mountain falls. The surrounding countryside depends on its waters. Jennea sends novice mages with a glass flask to the waterfall's base, where they collect fresh spray. The Sanctum can then use scrying and reagent tests to learn whether wild magic is seeping into the public water supply.

quest:1879.text: Speak with Bink. "Speak with Bink" is an Alliance summons directing novice mages from Dun Morogh to the capital city of Ironforge. Dispatched by Magis Sparkmantle, the call sends promising spellcasters to assist Bink, an arcane researcher working out of the Hall of Mysteries. Novice mages training in the cold crags of Dun Morogh eventually catch the eye of Magis Sparkmantle. Recognizing when an apprentice has outgrown the rudimentary exercises around Kharanos, Sparkmantle passes along word from his colleague, Bink. The request is specific and uncompromising: Bink requires an arcane specialist and refuses to trust the matter to anyone who cannot wield magic. The assignment carries young mages into Ironforge's Mystic Ward, where scholars, priests, and arcanists convene beneath the soaring stone vaults of the Hall of Mysteries. Here Bink conducts her studies, evaluating arriving apprentices with sharp-eyed scrutiny. In her view, raw potential is merely a beginning; an undisciplined spellcaster quickly becomes a hazard rather than an asset in arcane matters.

quest:1881.text: Speak with Anastasia. Speak with Anastasia is an introductory summons directing promising Forsaken mages to Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity. Dispatched by mage trainer Cain Firesong, the young caster is called to the Magic Quarter to undertake critical work for the magi of the Forsaken. This brief summons sets the stage for investigations out into the blighted lands of Tirisfal Glades. As nascent spellcasters hone their early talents under the guidance of Cain Firesong in Brill, they are soon directed into the capital. The mages of the Forsaken maintain a dedicated enclave within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, organizing both arcane scholarship and strategic defensive efforts across Lordaeron. Cain Firesong acts as an evaluator, filtering out mere novices and sending those who demonstrate genuine talent directly to senior practitioners who require capable field hands. Anastasia Hartwell stands among the prominent mage instructors within the Undercity. Rather than leaving promising students to study trivial incantations in safety, she wastes little time pressing them into service for the Forsaken's territorial and practical interests. Answering her summons is both a rite of passage for arcane practitioners and an induction into the shadowy, pragmatic magical pursuits that define the post-Scourge undead.

quest:1882.text: The Balnir Farmstead. "The Balnir Farmstead" is an early rite of passage for young Forsaken mages, directed by Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity's Mage Quarter. Initiates are sent to eastern Tirisfal Glades to gather snapdragons from an abandoned farmstead sitting dangerously close to the border of the Plaguelands. The floral samples serve as barometers for the encroaching magical corruption spreading from the Scourge-blighted east. While the Royal Apothecary Society frequently studies the effects of necromancy and decay, the mages of the Forsaken maintain their own watchful eye on the borderlands. Anastasia Hartwell tasks novice spellcasters with travelling to the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades. Snapdragons native to the farm's gardens are naturally sensitive to shifting magical currents, absorbing ambient energies from the soil and atmosphere. By examining these blooms, arcane scholars in the Undercity can measure whether the corruptive contagion of the Lich King's domain has seeped past the bulwark into Tirisfal proper. The Balnir Farmstead sits near the fringes of the glades, uncomfortably near the blight-scarred wilderness of the Western Plaguelands. The Forsaken recognize that the Lich King's plague is an unruly and destructive power that actively rots the land itself. Although the Forsaken harness their own dark arts, uncontained Scourge corruption threatens their territorial borders and security. Anastasia intends to pass the gathered snapdragons along to the apothecaries, uniting arcane observation with alchemical investigation to defend Lordaeron's reclaimed heartland.

quest:1885.text: Mennet Carkad. Mennet Carkad is an introductory rogue quest in the Undercity that brings promising operatives into the fold of the Deathstalkers. Directed by Marion Call, aspiring assassins are summoned to report directly to Mennet Carkad deep within the Rogues' Quarter. Within the dark corridors of the Undercity, word travels quietly among the Forsaken's covert operatives. When a scout or assassin catches the eye of the higher leadership, an invitation is issued. Marion Call passes down word that Mennet Carkad, a prominent figure among the rogue handlers, has taken personal notice. Given the lethal reputation of the Forsaken intelligence apparatus, ignoring such a directive is not considered a viable option. Mennet Carkad waits in the shadowy alcoves of the Rogues' Quarter, watching over recruits and evaluating their readiness. Those who heed his call are not simply joining an ordinary guild of thieves; they are being tested for entry into the Deathstalkers, the dreaded espionage and assassination arm of the Forsaken. Swift obedience is merely the first baseline test for anyone seeking to serve the Dark Lady from the shadows.

quest:1886.text: The Deathstalkers. This task marks the trial for initiates seeking entry into the Deathstalkers, the covert and lethal arm answering to Lord Varimathras in the Undercity. Assigned by Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter, the mission demands ruthless initiative to intercept a traveling messenger. Completing it opens the door to deeper clandestine schemes within the Forsaken realm. The Deathstalkers do not admit just anyone into their ranks. Operating directly under dreadlord Varimathras, this secretive order acts as both the secret police and elite assassination corps of the Forsaken. To earn their notice, a hopeful agent must demonstrate cunning, discretion, and an unhesitating willingness to eliminate targets. In the shadowy corners of the Rogues' Quarter, handler Mennet Carkad sets an initiation trial designed to weed out the weak or overscrupulous.

quest:1898.text: The Deathstalkers. This covert assignment sends an undercover operative into the Undercity's shadowy underbelly to interrogate an unwitting conspirator. Acting under orders handed down from Lord Varimathras, you pose as an expected messenger to uncover treason within the Forsaken's own capital. The Deathstalkers do not merely eliminate external threats to the Forsaken; they maintain a ruthless vigil over their own citizens. Acting on suspicions harbored by Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker Mennet Carkad sets an infiltration plan in motion. Armed with a forged or acquired letter of introduction belonging to Astor Hadren, you are tasked with slipping past the suspicions of a local merchant named Andron Gant.

quest:1899.text: The Deathstalkers. This errand continues the Deathstalkers' deception of the informant Andron Gant in the Undercity. Still believing you are the messenger he was expecting, Gant hands over a ledger meant for his secret contacts, and the operative delivers it instead to Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter. The exchange marks the transition from simple inquiries to deeper, more covert operations on behalf of the Forsaken state. The Deathstalkers do not rely solely on brute force or shadow magic; their operations depend heavily on mundane ledgers, recorded names, and meticulous surveillance. Andron Gant, operating out of the Undercity, hands over a personal ledger crammed with intelligence, believing it bound for the mysterious employers he secretly serves. Taken in by the operative's disguise, Gant even asks that the same courier be sent in the future, never suspecting that his ledger is headed straight to the Deathstalkers.

quest:1941.text: Manaweave Robe. In Stormwind, Wynne Larson presents the Manaweave Robe as a proud showcase for her family’s shop. She has woven the enchanted garment from fine materials for a commission that is now complete. Larson Clothiers serves spellcasters in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter with garments made to channel volatile energies. Fine magical robes call for rare materials, careful needlework, and threadwork that holds through mystic resonance. Wynne Larson takes pride in each piece that leaves her shop, where every robe worn into the field carries the Larson name. The manaweave robe offers comfort, mobility, and practical resilience for travel through contested lands. Once the needed components are delivered, Wynne Larson weaves the final stitch herself and presents the finished garment as a fine example of Larson tailoring, meant to draw admiration and spread the shop’s name across the kingdom.

quest:1961.text: Gathering Materials. Gathering Materials is a rite of passage for aspiring Horde mages training in the Undercity. Assigned by Anastasia Hartwell, the task sends apprentices into Silverpine Forest to claim arcane gems from the wizards of Dalaran, assembling the components needed to weave their first true mage's robes. Within the arcane cloisters of the Magic Quarter, novice mages must prove their mastery over more than just raw incantations. To earn their first true robes—a formal mantle marking their station and personal worth—initiates are directed by Anastasia Hartwell to harvest the raw components required for enchanted weave: a bolt of simple linen and a set of potent Dalaran mana gems. The mana gems cannot simply be purchased or manifested; they must be torn from Dalaran mages stationed across Silverpine Forest, particularly near Ambermill. Anastasia Hartwell remarks with cold detachment that while Dalaran's arcane philosophies mirror their own, sentimental hesitation has no place in the Undercity. In the eyes of the Forsaken, if those living wizards lack the strength to defend their relics, they forfeit both their treasures and their lives. Once gathered, the cloth and gems are delivered to Josef Gregorian, a tailor residing in the Magic Quarter. While Gregorian readily admits he lacks the magical talent to gauge the pristine quality of Dalaran's enchanted stones, he possesses the rare artisan skill needed to weave their raw power directly into the fabric of the robes.

quest:1963.text: The Shattered Hand. Therzok tests rogues in Orgrimmar who seek entry to the secretive Shattered Hand. Their trial sends them after Tazan, a troll smuggler, and his locked satchel. The Shattered Hand works from the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. The order of assassins and thieves follows old orcish traditions. Warchief Thrall rules the young Horde with honor, diplomacy, and caution, but the Shattered Hand's leaders believe restraint weakens their people. They seek to restore martial supremacy through covert violence, using knives and poison when a battlefield charge may fail.

quest:1978.text: The Deathstalkers. This errand marks the formal induction of a capable operative into the ranks of the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken order of assassins and spies. Tasked with delivering Andron's Ledger directly to the dreadlord Varimathras, the courier brings proof of the Syndicate's covert activities to the highest tier of Undercity leadership. After unearthing incriminating records from Andron Gant, Mennet Carkad officially welcomes the operative into the Deathstalkers. The organization serves as Lady Sylvanas's eyes, ears, and daggers throughout Lordaeron, relying on intelligence networks, ruthless efficiency, and stealth to eliminate threats before they surface. Gaining formal recognition within the order is a major milestone for any aspiring rogue or scout in the Undercity. Because of the sensitive nature of the intelligence, the ledger is delivered directly to Varimathras in the Royal Quarter of the Undercity. The nathrezim commander oversees Forsaken tactical intelligence under Sylvanas Windrunner. Pleased with the Deathstalkers' initiative, Varimathras welcomes the operative's demonstrated capability, noting that his intelligence division can always make use of someone who delivers results.

quest:21.text: Skirmish at Echo Ridge. In Northshire Valley, recruits strike at kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride ordered the attack after scouts found the mine overrun. Marshal McBride sends recruits against the kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Scouts found the mine overrun, and the garrison fears the creatures will strengthen their hold if left alone. The kobolds dig through the tunnels, gather stolen resources, and multiply. Recruits must thin their numbers to protect Northshire Valley, with its farms and spiritual retreat. New recruits are sent into the mine because the Stormwind Army is stretched thin. Garrison forces guard the southern borders, while unrest is rumored across Elwynn. Officers like McBride must call on willing hands. A recruit who proves reliable at Echo Ridge earns the army’s respect and is ready for more difficult work elsewhere in the kingdom.

quest:2118.text: Plagued Lands. Corruption is spreading through Darkshore, where Tharnariun Treetender hopes to save the afflicted wildlife. He asks travelers to calm a rabid thistle bear with an enchanted relic and bring it back alive. A creeping sickness twists Darkshore’s beasts into maddened, aggressive versions of themselves. Thistle bears suffer most, their rabid frenzy threatening travelers and the coast’s fragile balance. Night elf sentinels often answer with steel, while druids seek to understand the sickness and heal its cause. Tharnariun Treetender refuses to kill the corrupted beasts without first trying to save them. He made a trap called Tharnariun’s Hope. Set on the forest floor, its soothing light briefly calms a raging thistle bear. Pacified, the bear follows the traveler back to Tharnariun’s outpost for study.

quest:2138.text: Cleansing of the Infected. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender faces a hard choice over the infected thistle bears. His attempt to cure one has failed, and he asks you to kill the rabid beasts before they harm other creatures or spread the sickness. Tharnariun Treetender has searched for a remedy to the sickness spreading through Darkshore's wildlife. He tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the thistle bears remain diseased and violent. Now he asks you to put them down. He fears they will maul other creatures and carry the sickness farther into the ancient woodlands.

quest:2139.text: Tharnariun's Hope. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turning point. After travelers put down infected beasts across the woodlands, he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of Auberdine. After the Third War, an unnatural rabid sickness began afflicting Darkshore's wild creatures. Tharnariun Treetender, stationed in Auberdine, spent days asking travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. But killing rabid thistle bears treated only a symptom. Tharnariun decided the source among the local bears had to be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother. After the Den Mother's death, Tharnariun offers profound thanks, though melancholy shadows his words. For the kaldorei, raising weapons against woodland creatures is agonizing. Dark forces press against their new home, and many despair or seek shelter. The defenders of Auberdine accept the heavy moral burden of protecting their wilderness.

quest:2159.text: Dolanaar Delivery. Travelers leave Shadowglen with a parcel of herbs bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius, occupied with the druids, asks them to carry it south, marking their first venture beyond the sheltered glade. Porthannius asks travelers heading south from Shadowglen to carry a bundle of freshly harvested herbs along the forest path. He is occupied with pressing business alongside the druids tending the glade, and cannot leave to handle the errand himself. The bundle goes south as young adventurers prepare to leave the training grounds for the wider reaches of Teldrassil. The southern road from Shadowglen leads to Dolanaar, a foremost night elf settlement on Teldrassil's great boughs. Innkeeper Keldamyr oversees hospitality, rest, and supplies for wanderers, sentinels, and druids. When he receives the herbs on Porthannius's behalf, he urges young adventurers to rest their minds and spirits before facing the corruption spreading across the world tree.

quest:2160.text: Supplies to Tannok. Supplies to Tannok is an errand entrusted to fledgling adventurers departing Coldridge Valley through the dangerous mountain pass into greater Dun Morogh. The gnome tinkerer Hands Springsprocket sends a crate of needed provisions to Tannok Frosthammer at the Thunderbrew Distillery inn in Kharanos, bypassing the trogg-infested trails that have severed routine trade. Coldridge Valley is traditionally the proving ground and sanctuary for young Ironforge dwarves and exiled Gnomeregan survivors, but recent events have strained its connection to the rest of Dun Morogh. Trogg incursions have overrun Coldridge Pass, leaving the mountain defile perilous to cross. Mountaineers are spread thin guarding settlements and defensive perimeters, delaying scheduled supply escorts for days on end. Hands Springsprocket, a gnome waiting by the mouth of Coldridge Pass, found himself saddled with a crate of vital inn supplies meant for Kharanos without any safe way to deliver it personally. Recognizing that hearty adventurers are already preparing to brave the perilous pass, he enlists outward-bound travelers to carry the cargo to Tannok Frosthammer, the assistant at the bustling Thunderbrew inn. Reaching Kharanos marks an adventurer's entry into the broader world of Dun Morogh. Tannok Frosthammer eagerly receives the delivery, noting that word from Anvilmar has been scarce ever since the troggs disrupted travel through the pass. Delivering the goods restores a fragile line of communication and trade between the two isolated dwarf communities.

quest:2161.text: A Peon's Burden. Ukor waits on the trail outside the Valley of Trials with a load he cannot carry home. The recruits in the red canyon refused his provisions, and now he asks travelers to return them to Razor Hill. Ukor set out from Razor Hill with provisions for the fresh recruits training in the red canyon. He believed they needed the food, but the taskmasters turned him away. They keep supplies lean because they believe meager rations teach young Horde warriors discipline and endurance. Innkeeper Grosk later explains that this hardship is part of their training. Ukor reached the pass, but fears the return trip across Durotar. Scorpids, venomous spiders, and prowling boars haunt the rocky trail. He has no weapons or armor, and lacks the fighting spirit expected of an orcish grunt. Waiting along the path, he asks travelers leaving the proving grounds to carry his heavy provisions back to the inn in Razor Hill.

quest:2178.text: Easy Strider Living. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong offers to share her strider stew recipe with hunters who bring her foreststrider meat. Auberdine's coastal folk make use of the wildlife around them. Alanndarian Nightsong has her own recipe for hearty strider stew, made from the tall foreststriders that roam Darkshore's woods. She asks you to hunt the birds and bring back their meat before she shares her cooking. Foreststriders range through the woodlands and beaches north and south of Auberdine. Their sharp beaks and quick tempers make them dangerous when provoked, but their meat makes a rich stew. Bring fresh meat to Alanndarian, and she will share her recipe.

quest:218.text: The Stolen Journal. The Stolen Journal is an early Alliance quest in Dun Morogh where Grelin Whitebeard tasks adventurers with entering the troll cave in Coldridge Valley to reclaim his stolen notebook. To recover it, you must defeat the formidable troll leader Grik'nir the Cold. Reclaiming the journal allows Grelin to finalize his appraisal of the troll threat within Coldridge Valley. Grelin Whitebeard has been observing the Frostmane trolls encroaching on Coldridge Valley, keeping detailed notes on their habits and sudden aggression. During the unrest, an unusually imposing troll made off with his personal journal and retreated into the depths of their den. For Grelin, the loss is not merely sentimental; the notebook contains the bulk of his reconnaissance, leaving his official assessment stalled until it is recovered from the cavern. The brute responsible for taking the journal is Grik'nir the Cold, a powerful Frostmane troll marked with distinctive body and facial paint who holds court in the heart of the valley's troll cave. Slaying Grik'nir breaks the immediate local leadership of the cave's trolls and secures Grelin's journal. With the leader dispatched, Grelin feels confident enough to report that the valley's troll situation is manageable, sending his finished findings on to his brother Senir.

quest:22.text: Goretusk Liver Pie. At the Saldean Farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean prepares a pie amid hard times. Bandits have ravaged the breadbasket of the kingdom, and local homesteaders hunt aggressive boars to feed their families. Westfall was once Stormwind's fertile breadbasket, but hard times have fallen on the land. Neglected roads, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields make daily life a struggle for the few settlers who remain. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works to keep a sense of home despite the dangers around her. A traditional meat pie offers one of the few modest comforts for homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life. Goretusks roam Westfall's plains in great numbers, their tough hides and vicious tusks making them dangerous. They threaten lone farmhands, yet provide vital meat to families cut off from regular trade. Salma's recipe calls for crushed rosemary, minced garlic, chopped dill, and simmering gravy. With careful preparation, the pungent organs of these hardy beasts become a rich, savory meal.

quest:2205.text: Seek out SI: 7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends new rogues toward SI: 7. A sealed package carried to Stormwind City brings them before Master Mathias Shaw, who leads the crown's covert intelligence network. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, rogue trainer Keryn Sylvius wastes no time praising newcomers. She thinks fresh initiates look more like cheese delivery hands than covert agents, yet gives them a sealed delivery for the capital. The trip tests their reliability as couriers and quietly vets scouts for wider service to the realm. SI: 7 works from the southeastern corner of Old Town in Stormwind City. The worn district holds the command center of Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7, where Master Mathias Shaw oversees the kingdom's covert operations. Shaw receives the package with dry skepticism and judges whether the traveler has the grit for real espionage.

quest:2206.text: Snatch and Grab. Master Mathias Shaw sends agents to Jerod's Landing for shipping intelligence. The Defias Brotherhood uses the river dock to move supplies in secret. Master Mathias Shaw tests aspiring operatives who seek a place in Stormwind's covert intelligence wing. He asks for finesse and stealth, not brute force. SI:7 agents take down key figures quietly and recover important papers without drawing the realm into open scandal. Each new operative must prove they can work unseen. Jerod's Landing lies on the river in southern Elwynn, south of Goldshire and just east of the Maclure Vineyards. The Defias Brotherhood seized the once-quiet dock and made it an illicit route. Smuggled arms, supplies, and contraband cross the water from Redridge toward Westfall, beyond the reach of royal road patrols. Master Mathias Shaw warns agents that capture, compromise, or death leaves them without the Crown's support. Stormwind and its spymasters will deny knowing they ever existed. Recovering the Defias Dockmaster's schedule gives SI:7 proof of the Brotherhood's supply lines while keeping Stormwind's official involvement hidden.

quest:224.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. Mountaineer Cobbleflint guards the southern tower in the Valley of Kings, desperately seeking aid against the encroaching Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's military stretched thin across distant fronts, the defense of Loch Modan's southern passes falls to passing Alliance volunteers. The massive dwarven monuments carved into the mountains of the Valley of Kings loom over a garrison under severe strain. Mountaineer Cobbleflint and his fellow guards stationed at the southern watchtower face an ever-growing invasion of troggs erupting from the rock. With much of King Magni Bronzebeard's regular army dispatched abroad to support Alliance commitments, the home front relies heavily on local patrols and hired blades to prevent the province from being overrun. The subterranean threat originates within Stonesplinter Valley, a craggy ravine carving into the southern peaks of Loch Modan. Troggs and their scouts have burrowed surface-ward in massive numbers, carving out fortified camps along the valley floor. Left unchecked, their scouting parties threaten the critical roads connecting Loch Modan to the southern passes, forcing the Mountaineers to wage a continuous war of attrition.

quest:2242.text: Destiny Calls. Syurna sends you to learn what Sethir the Ancient knows of Teldrassil's corruption. The satyr waits near the Oracle Glade, beyond the reach of those who tried force or diplomacy. Teldrassil's growing sickness troubles the night elf leaders in Darnassus. Syurna, the rogue trainer, needs someone subtle; armed patrols have died trying to reach Sethir the Ancient. The satyr roosts on a remote bough near the Oracle Glade and has turned away force and diplomacy alike. To learn what he knows, you need to enter his lair and take his personal possessions.

quest:2259.text: Erion Shadewhisper. Jannok Breezesong sends promising rogues from Teldrassil to Darnassus. At the Cenarion Enclave, Erion Shadewhisper points them toward work beyond the forests. Jannok Breezesong sends you from Teldrassil to find Erion Shadewhisper in Darnassus. You need not worry about being sent to the exacting trainer Syurna. Erion waits in the Cenarion Enclave, where he handles work that calls for a quieter touch. Erion Shadewhisper marks a change for rogues in night elf lands. Teldrassil's forests can no longer contain your duties. Erion sends capable hands into a wider, more dangerous world, toward work across the sea.

quest:2260.text: Erion's Behest. Across the Great Sea, Erion's Behest carries a summons to promising night elf rogues in Darnassus. Erion Shadewhisper sees their growing skill in stealth and sends them to Stormwind City to report to Stormwind Intelligence. Night elf rogues in Teldrassil's shadow train under mentors such as Erion Shadewhisper. When one shows exceptional talent, word reaches beyond the World Tree. Through Erion, Stormwind Intelligence, known as SI:7, invites the rogue across the Great Sea to the human capital. The journey leads from northern Kalimdor through the docks of Darkshore or the Wetlands to Stormwind City. In the capital, you make your way to SI:7 headquarters in Old Town and report to Renzik "The Shiv." He assesses newcomers and opens the way to advanced espionage, poison mastery, and covert operations for the Alliance.

quest:2281.text: Redridge Rendezvous. Promising Alliance rogues are sent east from Stormwind’s intelligence headquarters to train in Lakeshire. SI:7 wants them ready for dangerous field work under seasoned operatives. Renzik 'The Shiv', SI:7’s second-in-command in Stormwind, warns that untrained rogues rarely survive dangerous operations. Sending raw recruits into hostile territory brings casualties instead of intelligence. SI:7 sends promising agents east to the Redridge Mountains, where they train under Lucius, stationed among Lakeshire’s docks. Lakeshire offers an ideal ground for clandestine training. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs threaten the frontier town, while its piers give Lucius cover to test a rogue’s stealth, reflexes, and lockpicking without attracting townspeople or guards.

quest:2300.text: SI:7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends promising young rogues toward Stormwind's hidden ranks. Recruits report to Renzik "The Shiv" in Old Town, where they enter Master Mathias Shaw's service. Keryn Sylvius watches local recruits from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. When a rogue proves cunning and capable against the growing Defias threat, Sylvius passes along a message from headquarters. The order is plain: report to Renzik "The Shiv" without delay. The recruit leaves Elwynn's fields for the covert heart of Stormwind. Behind an unassuming barracks in Old Town, SI:7 keeps its headquarters. Master Mathias Shaw commands the agency, whose work includes covert operations, reconnaissance, and assassination across the kingdom and beyond. Renzik "The Shiv," Shaw's sharp-tongued second-in-command, assesses promising agents before sending them into dangerous work beyond the reach of the kingdom's formal military.

quest:233.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery is a simple courier task entrusted to recruits by Sten Stoutarm at Anvilmar. With mountain passes often choked with snow and troggs pressing nearby, carrying fresh correspondence out to the camps along the frozen lake keeps the valley's isolated defenders connected. Life in Coldridge Valley is secluded even in the calmest of seasons. When winter couriers successfully navigate the mountain pass with mail from the rest of Dun Morogh, the missives pile up quickly at Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm, busy managing local supply concerns and security, relies on wandering recruits to carry these bundles down the western road rather than letting vital tidings languish in the hall. The intended recipient, Talin Keeneye, keeps watch by the frozen lake to the west, observing trogg movements and dangerous wildlife. Even out in the cold, word from Ironforge and surrounding outposts remains precious. However, mail sorting under harsh mountain conditions is rarely flawless, and letters bound for different scouts often travel together in a single bundle.

quest:234.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. This errand completes a courier run across the snowy drifts of Coldridge Valley. Passing the dispatch from mountaineer Talin Keeneye down the southeastern road ensures that Grelin Whitebeard stays connected to the dwarven capital. Even in an isolated basin like Coldridge Valley, news and formal correspondence must travel. While Anvilmar serves as the administrative heart of the valley, field scouts and sentries stationed along the trails rely on foot couriers to relay dispatches between the high passes and Ironforge. Grelin Whitebeard maintains a small camp down the road to the southeast of Talin Keeneye's post. Enduring freezing drifts and constant trogg harassment, veteran mountaineers stationed at these remote watchpoints depend on regular missives to stay informed of broader affairs across Dun Morogh and the kingdom beyond.

quest:2378.text: Find the Shattered Hand. In Orgrimmar, the Shattered Hand awaits a promising Forsaken rogue from Tirisfal Glades. The Deathstalkers send the initiate across the sea to Durotar to learn specialized arts from the clan. Mennet Carkad has seen a rogue prove their worth in Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken train their own covert order, the Deathstalkers, and their alliance with the Horde opens a path to learn darker arts. He directs promising rogues to seek the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar, joining Lordaeron’s undead operatives with Kalimdor’s orcish assassins. The journey ends beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, where warlocks, rogues, and demon-binders work out of sight. Shenthul, a Shattered Hand trainer, awaits there. The gruff troll judges the newly arrived undead agent with harsh skepticism. Reputation alone will not satisfy him; he wants to see whether the envoy has real cunning or has wasted the voyage across the Great Sea.

quest:2379.text: Zando'zan. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, promising rogues begin training with the Shattered Hand. Trainer Shenthul sends his chosen initiate to meet Zando'zan and enter the Horde's covert ranks. Orgrimmar's rulers know brute strength cannot win every war. Beneath the city, the Cleft of Shadow houses the Shattered Hand, a covert guild that handles espionage, sabotage, and theft for the Horde. When rogue trainer Shenthul sees promise in an initiate, he sends them to report to Zando'zan for dedicated operative training. Zando'zan does not grant respect to every inexperienced rogue who enters the cavern. Meeting him marks a formal initiation into the finer clandestine arts, beginning with stealth, subterfuge, and thievery. His training bridges the distance between rough street cutpurses and organized intelligence operatives, preparing rogues for fieldwork beyond the safety of the capital's red canyon walls.

quest:2380.text: To Orgrimmar!. Kaplak sends a young rogue from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There, you are to find Shenthul in the Cleft of Shadow and enter the Shattered Hand's network. Kaplak sends you north from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Your budding skills have caught the notice of more prominent handlers, though they remain unpolished. The red crags of Durotar are behind you as you make for the capital.

quest:2381.text: Plundering the Plunderers. Wrenix the Wretched sends new Shattered Hand rogues against the Southsea Freebooters near Ratchet. Aboard the Tide Razor, they face pirates, locked strongboxes, and a dangerous guardian before claiming the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin contact in Ratchet, tests aspiring Shattered Hand operatives. He sends rogues south along the Barrens coast to a cove where the Tide Razor lies at anchor, crewed by Southsea Freebooters. They must board without being seen, enter the pirates’ den where cutpurses train, pick the strongboxes in the hold, and bring back the plunder.

quest:2382.text: Wrenix of Ratchet. In Orgrimmar, Wrenix of Ratchet draws Horde rogues toward a goblin port far to the south. Zando'zan sends them to aid Wrenix the Wretched, a disreputable goblin in Ratchet. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the rogue guild works out of winding crevices, largely unseen. Zando'zan, a troll who speaks in wild ramblings, greets operatives with ominous portents. His visions include Warchief Thrall struck down by poison and blade. He gives no explanation for the prophecy, and quickly sends agents south to the port town of Ratchet in the Barrens. Ratchet lies on the Barrens coast, east of the Crossroads. Scoundrels, mercenaries, and tinkerers gather in the neutral port, where Wrenix the Wretched makes his home. Wrenix has little patience for Zando'zan's eccentric ways. He says the troll's earlier recruits met grim ends in the bay, among its hungry predators.

quest:239.text: Westbrook Garrison Needs Help!. Marshal Dughan sends available adventurers west to Westbrook Garrison, the outpost at Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Stormwind's army is stretched thin across the kingdom, while Deputy Rainer and his guards face growing pressure from Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves without regular reinforcements. Westbrook Garrison guards the western edge of Elwynn Forest, where settled woodland meets Westfall's troubled plains. Gnoll warbands and bandits grow bolder along the waterways and western roads, and the small garrison has asked for more men. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's administration have no Stormwind soldiers to spare. Local commanders must hire traveling mercenaries and wandering adventurers. Deputy Rainer and his men face the Riverpaw gnolls, whose raiding parties harass travelers and nearby homesteads. The pack operates in the borderlands between Elwynn and Westfall. With Stormwind distracted by political and military troubles, the gnolls press deeper into inhabited territory. Westbrook Garrison guards against their unchecked advance into the heart of the forest.

quest:2399.text: The Sprouted Fronds. At Denalan's garden by Lake Al'Ameth, the planted frond has taken root and sprouted. Travelers can see the new growth among the garden beds. You find Denalan's garden near Lake Al'Ameth, where the botanist studies Teldrassil's peculiar plants. After a shimmering frond is planted, new fronds rise from the soil in his planter, ready to be gathered and examined. Teldrassil is young and vast, and its plant life grows quickly. Night elf herbalists find that growth fascinating and troubling. The shimmering fronds and their offshoots show how quickly life takes hold on the World Tree's boughs, though its vitality can be hard to predict.

quest:2438.text: The Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot asks you to recover a cherished heirloom from his abandoned home in Starbreeze Village. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druid warden, gave him the Emerald Dreamcatcher, which he left behind when corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the settlement. Recovering it keeps its gentle nature magic from falling into foul hands. Gaerolas Talvethren gave Tallonkai a rare druidic talisman. The warden watches over the sleeping druids within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Crafted to channel the serene currents of the Emerald Dream, the amulet draws on that pure spiritual energy to bring peace and fortune to its bearer. Such gifts go only to a trusted few whose lives are bound to the forest's care. Starbreeze Village was peaceful until the Gnarlpine furbolgs succumbed to violent madness. They drove the villagers from their ancestral homes. During the fearful flight, Tallonkai left his most treasured possession hidden inside his dresser in the village's southeastern quarter. He could not reclaim it on his own.

quest:2459.text: Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot in Dolanaar sends you after a stolen emerald in northern Teldrassil. The jewel was pried from his damaged heirloom dreamcatcher by Gnarlpine furbolgs north of Starbreeze Village, and now hangs from their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot felt relief when the dreamcatcher recovered from the corrupted wilds came back to him, then dismay at its ruined state. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, its emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame. Night elves spoke of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village, fallen under the influence of a furbolg leader named Ferocitas the Dream Eater. He wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. In Ferocitas's clutches, the sacred gem was useless and perverse, so Tallonkai sent defenders to take it back. The Gnarlpine furbolgs in Teldrassil's northern reaches were once peaceful neighbors. Corruption seeping into the World Tree drove them into frenzy and madness. Their mystics once practiced harmonious nature rites, but began drawing on distorted magical energies. Travelers can track down Ferocitas by cutting through the mystics guarding his woodland enclave. The jewel can then be returned to Tallonkai, so his dreamcatcher may be made whole and balance restored to the woods.

quest:2498.text: Return to Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Return to Denalan carries Rellian's alarming news to the botanist studying corruption in Teldrassil. After examining the mossy tumors on timberlings, you head south to help Denalan with his discovery. Rellian Greenspyre studies the mossy tumors afflicting Teldrassil's timberlings when urgent word arrives from his colleague Denalan. At his camp beside Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan has finally isolated the cause of these unnatural growths on the forest's nature spirits. Rellian recognizes the gravity of this discovery and sends you south at once to lend a hand.

quest:2499.text: Oakenscowl. Along Lake Al'Ameth, blight spreads from a corrupted timberling called Oakenscowl. Denalan asks you to end the threat. The maddened creature dwells in a cave on the lake's southern bank. Timberlings tend the boughs of Teldrassil, and Oakenscowl once led them. Now corruption runs through the world tree, reaching humble wildlife and ancient protectors alike. A massive growth swells across Oakenscowl's bark, driving the timberling mad. Where it once guarded the forest, blight now takes hold. Oakenscowl hides in a cavern on Lake Al'Ameth's southern shore. Its presence poisons the nearby water and woodland beasts. Denalan cannot face the creature alone, so he seeks its destruction to cut off the corruption and study the strange growth afflicting the lake's spirits.

quest:2518.text: Tears of the Moon. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora mourns Lady Sathrah's madness. Once cherished by Elune, the great spider has become dangerous, and the Sisterhood seeks to end her suffering and recover her sacred spinnerets. In Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Sathrah was once blessed by Elune. Beneath the night sky, she wove delicate silver webs that caught the evening mist on Teldrassil's boughs. The Sisterhood of Elune gathered and kept the shimmering dew from those webs, which held healing powers for their sacred ministrations.

quest:2519.text: The Temple of the Moon. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne calls for aid to a suffering ancient creature in Teldrassil. The Sisterhood of Elune needs help, and this is the opening call to a solemn ritual of mercy. Sister Aquinne asks for help in the Temple Gardens. As a devoted servant of Elune, she speaks for her order: a venerable forest creature is suffering, and the Sisters cannot attend to it alone. Sister Aquinne sends you southeast to the Temple of the Moon. Priestess A'moora coordinates the rituals and practical duties needed to address Teldrassil's troubled wildlife, preparing allies to carry out a sorrowful act of mercy.

quest:2520.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice gives a fallen creature's spirit a final rite. You carry Lady Sathrah's spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters, where the Priesthood seeks to cleanse her soul of corruption. Priestess A'moora asks you to perform a final rite after Lady Sathrah is slain. The great spider fell to the dark madness spreading across Teldrassil, which twisted her peaceful nature into mindless aggression. The Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence, not treat her death as a simple culling. You place her silvery spinnerets in the fountain at the heart of the Temple of the Moon. Its consecrated waters wash away the corruption and grant her release.

quest:2541.text: The Sleeping Druid. Oben Rageclaw lies asleep in Ban'ethil Barrow Den, but his spirit is caught in the Emerald Dream. Gnarlpine shamans have drawn it from his body and set his flesh moving through the den. Night elf druids sleep in barrow dens across Kalimdor while their spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Their bodies rest in stone alcoves, safe through centuries of slumber. Teldrassil's corruption has driven the Gnarlpine furbolgs to desperate savagery. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans found a way to breach Oben Rageclaw's sacred rest and draw his living spirit from his sleeping body.

quest:2561.text: Druid of the Claw. Oben Rageclaw’s spirit waits in the barrows beneath Teldrassil, unable to rest. The Gnarlpine furbolgs have bound his body with a dark enchantment, and you can break that bond by destroying his soulless shell. Oben Rageclaw was resting in the barrows beneath Teldrassil when the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs laid a voodoo enchantment over his sleeping body. The magic tore his spirit from his mortal flesh and trapped it in the Emerald Dream. Now his spirit lingers nearby, unable to rest or reclaim his body.

quest:26.text: A Lesson to Learn. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends young druids from Darnassus to Moonglade to learn the ways of water. There, they meet an elder of the Cenarion Circle and begin training in their aquatic aspect. Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides young night elf druids as they practice among Darnassus’s boughs. When an initiate shows a firm bond with nature and readiness for greater responsibility, Mathrengyl sends them toward mastery of the waters. Cenarius’s gifts demand focus, and learning to cross the depths without drowning calls for guidance from the Cenarion Circle’s elders. The initiate leaves Darnassus for Moonglade, an ancient sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze waits as an elder mentor of the Cenarion Circle. Starblaze judges whether young shapeshifters are ready for the trials that lead to aquatic form. Mastering water takes both physical resilience and mental resolve.

quest:267.text: The Trogg Threat. The Trogg Threat is an Alliance quest issued by Captain Rugelfuss at the Southern Gate of Loch Modan. With the local Ironforge Reserve called away to support Alliance battlefronts, the remaining defenders are stretched thin against the hostile trogg tribes in the hills. Adventurers are tasked with culling the troggs and returning with their stone teeth to relieve pressure on the mountain pass. The defensive line guarding the southern approach into Loch Modan is in a precarious state. The regular dwarven mountaineers and Ironforge Reserve regiments have been dispatched to reinforce broader Alliance war fronts, leaving Captain Rugelfuss and a skeleton garrison stationed at the southern guard tower. Constrained by strict orders not to abandon the gate, Rugelfuss cannot mount an active offensive into the highlands, leaving nearby settlers and travelers vulnerable to ambushes. Troggs residing in the surrounding crags pose an escalating danger to Khaz Modan. Left unchecked, their numbers swell quickly, threatening to overrun dwarven outposts. To buy time and thin the menace, Rugelfuss calls upon wandering adventurers to assault the troggs directly in their hillside warrens and present severed stone teeth as physical confirmation of the deed.

quest:2751.text: Barbaric Battlements. In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks someone to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks an aspiring smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge. Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar under the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, and he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk of ending, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward. Orokk will not share his secrets with an untested smith. He asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp beast claws as proof of basic skill at the anvil. To him, blacksmithing is no idle luxury: its highest honor is armor and steel stained with enemy blood. Meeting his demands may persuade the old smith that the Omosh legacy can live on through an apprentice, and earn a chance to learn more of the craft.

quest:2753.text: Trampled Under Foot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh puts smiths through an advanced blacksmithing trial. Forging green iron armor tests their endurance and teaches them to make heavy iron boots, with the Omosh bloodline's secret techniques at stake. Orokk Omosh trains armorsmiths in Orgrimmar through hard physical trials. He sees metalworking as more than heating ore and shaping it; the work honors his ancestral clan and tests a smith's endurance. This is the third trial in his chain, and repeated crafting of tempered green iron armor is meant to build muscle and discipline. Smiths who bring Orokk the requested green iron gear earn rare praise from the gruff armorsmith. He compares an artisan who endures the work to his grandfather, Chief Gorokk of Omosh. In exchange for the armor, Orokk teaches the ancestral design for sturdy iron boots, made so Horde warriors can crush their enemies beneath their heels.

quest:2755.text: Joys of Omosh. After an adventurer's great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith brushes off his tears as soot, then performs the Omosh dance of joy to pass down an unusual piece of family heritage. Near Orgrimmar's scorching forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. The burly blacksmith has received great help from you, and the kindness overwhelms him. He stubbornly blames a stray bit of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping. Before you part, Orokk says he must share one last secret of the Omosh family. He performs the vigorous, exhausting Omosh dance of joy for his apprentice, then teaches the apprentice to strike with an iron fist.

quest:282.text: Senir's Observations. Having gathered vital intelligence on local threats in Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard entrusts you with carrying his findings to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, out in Kharanos. However, leaving the sheltered valley requires passing through a tunnel recently overrun by hostile troggs, guarded by Mountaineer Thalos. Grelin Whitebeard spent considerable effort documenting the troll activity stirring around Coldridge Valley. When his journal was pilfered and subsequently recovered, it became clear that the collected intelligence was far too critical to trust to an inexperienced apprentice. Looking to bypass intermediate hands, Grelin selects a seasoned adventurer to convey his report directly to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, who conducts operations outside the valley in Kharanos. Leaving Coldridge Valley is no longer a simple trek down the main road. The eastern tunnel connecting the valley to the wider snowy plateau of Dun Morogh has been violently overrun by burrowing troggs. To prevent unwary civilians from wandering into a deathtrap, the Ironforge guard has stationed Mountaineer Thalos just outside the passage. Only travelers carrying urgent, official business are granted leave to push past the sentry post and brave the subterranean gauntlet.

quest:287.text: Frostmane Hold. Frostmane Hold is an Alliance recon mission assigned by Senir Whitebeard in Kharanos. Having tracked the hostile Frostmane trolls to their heavily guarded cavern stronghold near Iceflow Lake, Senir enlists adventurous scouts to brave the interior, eliminate their headhunters, and supply vital intel for his scouting reports. Stationed in Kharanos, mountaineer and scout Senir Whitebeard was tasked with monitoring the encroaching Frostmane troll threat across Dun Morogh. While he successfully traced the aggressive tribes back to their primary cavern dwelling southwest of Brewnall Village, the sheer volume of armed trolls gave him pause. Reluctant to step foot inside alone and falling severely behind on his official reports, Senir hires passing adventurers to venture into the icy recesses on his behalf. The stronghold sits carved into the western peaks overlooking Iceflow Lake, a freezing redoubt packed with hostile ice trolls. To fulfill Senir's mission, scouts must fight their way deep through the subterranean tunnels, cull the fierce Frostmane Headhunters stationed along the ledges, and map the interior layout. Surviving the delve provides the critical intelligence Senir requires to finalize his findings for Ironforge's military commanders.

quest:291.text: The Reports. Carry Senir Whitebeard's report on the Frostmane trolls from Kharanos to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Senir warns that the senator is sour and asks you not to mention who helped gather the information. After daring reconnaissance deep inside Frostmane Hold, Senir Whitebeard drafts an urgent report detailing the growing troll threat facing Dun Morogh. Stationed out of Kharanos, the mountaineer needs a courier to deliver these intelligence findings directly to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Eager to preserve his own reputation in the eyes of the government, Whitebeard cheerfully advises his runner not to mention who actually did the hazardous legwork out in the snowy crags.

quest:2950.text: Nogg's Ring Redo. In Orgrimmar, Nogg works to improve a ring recovered from Gnomeregan. He asks for rare materials and information about Dark Iron dwarves, eager to prove goblin craft superior to gnomish design. You bring a cleaned gold ring from Gnomeregan to Nogg's workshop in the Valley of Honor. The goblin engineer takes one look at its modest gnomish craft and offers a bargain. Bring raw materials and a modest fee, and he will add an intricate lattice of silver and moss agate to the band, meant to amplify the magic within it.

quest:2997.text: Tome of Divinity. The Tome of Divinity is an introductory summons calling young dwarven paladins from their field duties in Dun Morogh to the mountain city of Ironforge. Dispatched by Azar Stronghammer, the initiate is directed to seek guidance from Tiza Battleforge high in the Hall of Mysteries. It marks the formal beginning of a paladin's deeper trials in service to the Holy Light. While dwarven initiates begin their training protecting the snowbound villages and roads of Dun Morogh, martial prowess alone does not make a paladin. Azar Stronghammer recognizes when a defender has grown ready for deeper spiritual instruction. Rather than continuing standard martial drills, he sends promising candidates into the heart of Ironforge to begin their true initiation under the city's revered holy elders. The summons directs the initiate to the Mystic Ward, climbing into the quiet chambers of the Hall of Mysteries. There, surrounded by sacred relics and solemn study, stands Tiza Battleforge. As one of the most respected dwarven champions of the Light, she tests incoming paladins on their readiness to embrace self-sacrifice, mercy, and the heavy moral duties of their holy calling.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. A summons bearing the Tome of Divinity calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Answering Brother Wilhelm's call begins the sacred trials needed to master resurrection through the Holy Light. Novice paladins in Elwynn Forest spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows martial discipline and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. Leaders of the paladins take note of promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind and report straight to the kingdom's spiritual heart. In Cathedral Square, Stormwind's Cathedral of Light is the supreme sanctuary of the kingdom's priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Duthorian Rall resides there and oversees those sworn to the Order. Beneath its soaring vaulted ceilings, high-ranking paladins set formal trials from the Tome of Divinity before each initiate. The challenges test compassion, fortitude, and a willingness to sacrifice.

quest:2999.text: Tome of Divinity. Tome of Divinity is a rite of passage quest offered to young dwarven paladins serving in Dun Morogh. Directed by Brandur Ironhammer, the paladin trainer in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, an initiate is sent upstairs to speak with the respected paladin trainer Tiza Battleforge. It marks the transition from basic martial training into the deeper spiritual duties and sacred vows of the Holy Light. While novice paladins spend their early days defending Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls, their duties eventually call for deeper devotion. Brandur Ironhammer, recognizing that an initiate has proven their martial discipline, advises them to take a break from their work in the snowy passes and seek guidance upstairs in his own Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge. There, senior paladins oversee the spiritual maturation of the order. Tiza Battleforge stands as one of the most revered paladins among the Ironforge dwarves. It is her responsibility to instruct initiates on the true burdens of the Light, moving past simple swordplay and hammer swings to teach compassion, justice, and self-sacrifice. Seeking her out begins the formal study of the Tome of Divinity, a sacred process aimed at granting a paladin the ability to resurrect the fallen.

quest:3000.text: Tome of Divinity. This errand directs dwarven paladins wandering abroad to return home to Ironforge to further their sacred calling. Offered by Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker in Stormwind, it points fledgling champions toward Tiza Battleforge, one of the most respected instructors in the Hall of Mysteries. Returning home marks the beginning of their formal trials with the Tome of Divinity. While dwarven paladins frequently aid the kingdom of Stormwind and venture throughout human territories, their spiritual and martial roots remain anchored in Khaz Modan. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker, recognizing when a dwarf's training in the field has progressed enough, advises them to return to the heart of Ironforge. There, their own people oversee the profound spiritual obligations expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand. Upon returning to the mountainous capital, the paladin is directed to the Mystic Ward. Deep within the Hall of Mysteries, atop its upper level, resides Tiza Battleforge. She serves as a venerated mentor to the younger generation of dwarven paladins, preparing them to shoulder the burden of the Holy Light through the sacred trials recorded in the Tome of Divinity.

quest:3065.text: Simple Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a marked parchment sends you to Frang after you prove yourself against local beasts. The warrior trainer waits outside the Den. After you prove you can face the Mottled Boars, Gornek hands you a parchment marked specifically for you. Durotar is harsh, and the Horde quickly gives its fighters guidance. The parchment directs you to Frang, the veteran warrior trainer outside the Den. Frang shelters in the shade outside the Den and watches recruits arrive from the red scrubland. With a seasoned eye, he judges each new arrival before teaching the fundamentals, whether with a heavy axe or a spear. He prepares each recruit to defend the young Horde's fragile settlements.

quest:308.text: Distracting Jarven. Down in the cellar of Thunderbrew Distillery, guard Jarven Thunderbrew finds himself surrounded by barrels he is forbidden to touch. Craving a taste of the family craft, he asks a passing adventurer for a mug of Thunder Ale to help sharpen his wits on duty. Jarven Thunderbrew is tasked with keeping watch over the deep stores of Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Despite being surrounded by the finest stout in Dun Morogh, he works under strict family orders not to dip into the stock while on guard. The temptation proves too much, prompting him to enlist passing travelers to fetch him a pint of potent Thunder Ale from the taps upstairs. Jarven insists that a good drink will only hone his senses and bolster his watch. Whether indulging a guard on duty is wise remains an open question, but among the hardy dwarves of Dun Morogh, few can fault a Thunderbrew for wanting a taste of his own kin's world-famous brew.

quest:3082.text: Etched Tablet. Gornek sends a carved tablet to hunters in the Valley of Trials. It bears Jen'shan's mark and calls them to begin training in the wilderness. Gornek brings novice hunters a carved tablet after they prove themselves against the boars near the Den. The stone bears Jen'shan's mark. She is a skilled troll huntswoman stationed nearby, and the message shows that seasoned hunters have noticed the young recruit's grit. The lesson now moves beyond surviving the local dangers and toward disciplined training in the wild. Jen'shan teaches that orcs and trolls have a long history within the Horde. Orcs brought renowned traditions of warriors and shamans, while the Darkspear trolls carried ancient skills in stalking, tracking, and survival. Those skills helped the orcs endure life on Azeroth. As Jen'shan trains new hunters, the two peoples continue to share what they know, bound by respect for the hunt.

quest:3083.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives a coded summons to aspiring rogues. It sends them to Rwag in the Den, where rogue instruction meets the Shattered Hand. Gornek gives an Encrypted Tablet to each initiate who proves their mettle against the local wildlife. Its message is written in cipher, a fitting test and precaution for those trained in stealth, poison, and subterfuge. The summons directs the recruit into the Den to meet Rwag, who trains the Horde’s rogues, thieves, and cutpurses. Inside the Den, initiates find Rwag, an agent aligned with the Shattered Hand. He tells new rogues the guild will not dictate their every breath, but the Hand holds him accountable if an apprentice fails to perform. The fledgling Horde is surrounded by foes and relies heavily on silent scouts and agile cutpurses to gather intelligence and eliminate threats from the shadows.

quest:3084.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, new shamans receive a summons from Shikrik. It calls promising initiates to formal training in the spirits and the elements: earth, fire, water, and air. Gornek gives fledgling shamans a carved stone tablet after they prove their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials. Its runes carry an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer. The summons tells each initiate they are ready to look beyond physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world. Shamanism holds a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. Shikrik teaches that shamans draw power from the four elements and strength from ancestral spirits. They follow Warchief Thrall's example as spiritual guides and sources of wisdom for their communities. Across Durotar, they protect the settlements taking root.

quest:3085.text: Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a message from Ken'jai reaches young priests after their first test. The tablet calls them to learn how Darkspear priests commune with the spirits. After you prove yourself against the boars under Gornek's watch, he gives you an inscribed stone called the Hallowed Tablet. Its message bears Ken'jai's mark. The Darkspear mystic waits outside the Den, where he watches over newcomers drawn to faith and spiritual magic. Darkspear priests among the Horde seek communion with spirits and loa, unlike human and dwarven priests who follow the Holy Light across the sea.
