Ken'jai welcomes you to Durotar and teaches that your power grows through spiritual discipline. He will instruct you in greater rites as your bond with the spirits matures.

quest:3086.text: Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a Glyphic Tablet sends young Horde mages to Mai'ah. Gornek passes it to them after they prove their strength, and the troll trainer waits outside the Den. You have proved your strength against the Valley of Trials' wildlife, and Gornek gives you an inscribed tablet. Mai'ah, the valley's mage trainer, sent it. She asks you to find her by the Den's entrance when you are ready to begin your arcane studies. Mai'ah speaks plainly about the power mages wield and the danger that comes with it. She warns that their greatest threat is magic's unseen pull toward corruption, not rival warriors or enemy races. Humility and patience matter, she says, because unchecked sorcery can make a mage believe they have mastered more than they have.

quest:3087.text: Etched Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Etched Parchment calls a young hunter to Jen'shan. Gornek delivers it after the initiate's first blooding, opening the way to wilderness training in Durotar. After proving themselves against mottled boars, hunters in the Valley of Trials receive an etched parchment from Gornek. Jen'shan, a skilled Darkspear hunter, sent the note after watching new arrivals from the edges of the encampment. It welcomes the initiate to formal training and recognizes the instincts needed to master Durotar's untamed beasts and harsh land. Reporting to Jen'shan marks the move from recruit to dedicated stalker. She warns that hunting is no easier than the arcane arts or ancestral shamanism. Mastering Durotar's predators, maintaining ranged weapons, and surviving on unforgiving land all demand discipline. Jen'shan sends her apprentices to aid the valley's other inhabitants and test their abilities before returning to learn more advanced survival techniques.

quest:3088.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment sends proven novice orc rogues into the Den. Its cipher points them to Rwag, an agent of the Shattered Hand. Gornek passes the coded parchment to novice orcs who have proved themselves against the local wildlife. Other trainers recruit pupils openly in the clearing, but rogue instructor Rwag sends his summons by cipher. The message directs you beyond the sunlit camp and deep into the cavern called the Den. Inside the Den, you find Rwag keeping watch among the rock. Warlocks lurk deeper in the cave, and he tells you he watches recruits for the Shattered Hand. While orcish society prizes open honor and glory in battle, the Shattered Hand works as the Horde's hidden network of spies, cutthroats, and gatherers of intelligence.

quest:3089.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. At the Valley of Trials, a rune-marked summons calls new shamans to Shikrik. Gornek delivers the parchment, which begins their formal training in communion with spirits and elements. After proving their survival skills against local wildlife, new orc shamans receive a rune-inscribed parchment from Gornek, overseer of the Valley of Trials. Its mystical writing comes from Shikrik, the valley's shaman trainer, who asks to meet the newly arrived initiate. Meeting Shikrik begins a shaman's sacred duty to the Horde. She teaches that shamans serve as conduits for ancestral spirits and wielders of elemental wrath. Under her guidance, new shamans learn to channel spiritual energies, mend wounds, and call upon Kalimdor's natural forces.

quest:3092.text: Etched Note. The Etched Note is a formal summons directed to promising young tauren hunters in Camp Narache. Delivered on behalf of the trainer Lanka Farshot, the message calls the novice forward to begin mastering the practical and spiritual arts of the wild. While training amidst the bluffs of Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren showing an aptitude for marksmanship and tracking are passed an etched message. Handed down through Grull Hawkwind, the note carries word that Lanka Farshot has taken notice of the youth's bloodline and raw capability, urging them to formalize their study beneath his watchful eye. To the Shu'halo, a hunter is far more than a simple scout or warrior. Hunters sustain the tribes through their quarry, protect nomadic encampments, and live in close balance with the beasts of Kalimdor. By calling the novice into training, Lanka sets the groundwork for mastering weapons, understanding the creatures of Mulgore, and eventually undertaking the ancient art of taming wild companions.

quest:3094.text: Verdant Note. The Verdant Note is a formal summons delivered to promising young tauren in the Red Cloud Mesa. Entrusted by Grull Hawkwind, the message bids budding protectors of the wilds to seek out the druidic mentor Gart Mistrunner at Camp Narache. Young tauren stepping into their responsibilities on the Red Cloud Mesa are quickly singled out for their natural gifts. Grull Hawkwind passes along this missive on behalf of a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner. The note acts as an invitation into the ancient fold of tauren druidism, calling the initiate away from basic village errands to heed the whispering balance of the plains. Upon answering the summons, Gart Mistrunner warns the fledgling druid that ancestral and natural spirits have grown restless across Mulgore. Tauren druids are tasked to act as living avatars of nature, keeping harmony with the will of the Earthmother regardless of distant rivalries. While night elves also practice druidic arts, Gart cautions that their pride blinds them to the tauren's own deep-seated bond with the natural realm.

quest:3096.text: Encrypted Scroll. The Encrypted Scroll is a discreet summons delivered to freshly awakened Forsaken rogues in Deathknell. Passed along by Shadow Priest Sarvis, the cipher directs the recruit to David Trias, a rogue mentor operating quietly out of the local inn. While newly raised Forsaken battle mindless zombies in the cemetery, the settlement's leadership takes note of those with particular inclinations toward stealth and subterfuge. Shadow Priest Sarvis passes this sealed parchment to promising scouts once their initial readiness is proven. Stamped with the discreet seal of David Trias, it serves as an early introduction to the shadowy network operating beneath the Forsaken hierarchy. David Trias watches the crossroads and inn of Deathknell, scouting prospects for future clandestine operations. Rather than seeking common thieves or reckless cutpurses, the Forsaken require disciplined covert operatives to serve the fledgling kingdom. Trias hints that capable rogues may eventually catch the eye of the Shadowstalkers, a dedicated cadre within the Forsaken who prize cunning, precision, and absolute loyalty to the Dark Lady.

quest:3097.text: Hallowed Scroll. The Hallowed Scroll is an introductory summons directed to newly awoken Forsaken priests in Deathknell. Handed over by Shadow Priest Sarvis, the missive calls the novice to Dark Cleric Duesten inside the shattered village chapel to learn how the undead wield faith after death. As newly awakened undead stagger from the graves of Deathknell, their minds are often reeling from the trauma of the plague, death, and sudden liberation from the Lich King's grip. For those who were once devout followers of the Holy Light in life, confusion runs exceptionally deep. While fledgling undead battle the mindless Scourge haunting the settlement's perimeter, Shadow Priest Sarvis intercepts incoming messages. Bearing the mark of Dark Cleric Duesten, the hallowed scroll bids newly risen priests to abandon their wandering and report to the desecrated town chapel. Upon delivering the scroll, a novice encounters the harsh theology of Forsaken priesthood. Dark Cleric Duesten pulls no punches: the Holy Light abandoned them in death, ancestral spirits are hollow tales, and planar demons have no interest in their plight. Instead, Forsaken clergy teach that sheer willpower and radical self-reliance are the only true sources of salvation. Under Duesten's tutelage, newly risen practitioners learn to channel both divine discipline and shadow, wielding power not out of devotion to distant gods, but out of absolute conviction in their own survival.

quest:3098.text: Glyphic Scroll. The Glyphic Scroll is an official summons delivered to newly awakened Forsaken mages in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of the mage trainer Isabella, the parchment directs promising practitioners of the arcane to seek her out in the desecrated village church to hone their volatile powers. When a freshly raised Forsaken demonstrates an affinity for arcane magic while culling mindless Scourge around Deathknell, they quickly catch the attention of their elders. Delivered by hand, the Glyphic Scroll is marked with the arcane sigil of Isabella, the local mage instructor. It bids the newly risen practitioner to report to her station within the ruined church, recognizing that unregulated magical aptitude poses as much danger to the Forsaken as it does to their enemies. Within the ruined chapel of Deathknell, Isabella instructs fledglings that death has not exempted them from the perils of the arcane. While mortality has stripped away their physical frailties, the volatile pull and corrupting nature of magic linger just as fiercely. For the Forsaken, pursuing arcane dominance is not merely an intellectual pursuit, but an instrument of survival and vengeance—a means to reclaim their destiny and obliterate any who challenge their fragile reclamation of Lordaeron.

quest:310.text: Bitter Rivals. Bitter Rivals is an early Alliance quest in Dun Morogh born from the fierce competition between two proud dwarven brewing families. Marleth Barleybrew sends an adventurer to infiltrate the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos and tamper with their rival's stock. Few things in Khaz Modan stir passions as quickly as a pint of ale. The Barleybrews have long bristled under the shadow of the famed Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. While Marleth Barleybrew begrudgingly concedes that Thunderbrew craft is respectable, she cannot stomach the notion that it is the only renowned vintage in Dun Morogh. To shake up the local palate, she devises a plan to swap a cask of Thunder Ale with her own fiery concoction, Barleybrew Scalder. Carrying out the scheme requires slipping directly beneath the noses of Kharanos patrons. Beneath the kitchen of the distillery lies the basement storeroom where aging casks await tapping. Because the Thunderbrews keep a guard posted near their most prized reserve, a would-be saboteur must find a way to lure the watchman away before secretly substituting the barrels.

quest:3103.text: Hallowed Letter. The Hallowed Letter is a formal summons given to promising young priests by Marshal McBride on behalf of Northshire Abbey's resident trainer, Priestess Anetta. It marks the start of a fledgling priest's formal mentorship in the tenets of the Holy Light amidst a troubled and vulnerable world. After proving their mettle against the kobold camps around Northshire, novitiate priests are handed a missive bearing the sacred seal of Priestess Anetta. Delivered through Marshal McBride, the letter serves as an invitation to begin serious study of the Holy Light within the abbey's quiet halls. When presented with the letter, Priestess Anetta impresses upon her new pupil the grim state of the realm. Lingering threats from the Burning Legion cast long shadows across Azeroth, while the continents struggle with fresh wounds and unrest. In her eyes, taking up the mantle of a priest is not merely an academic devotion, but an urgent moral responsibility to bring healing and solace to a suffering world.

quest:3104.text: Glyphic Letter. A sealed summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley, sent by Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, Northshire's resident mage trainer, wrote it. He watches new recruits arriving at the abbey for signs of magical discipline and talent. Northshire Abbey has long been a sanctuary of the Holy Light, but Stormwind's dangers call for practitioners of every discipline. The letter brings you upstairs to Khelden Bremen. He offers no easy praise. Instead, he warns that mastering arcane power means defying natural limits, earning both profound respect and deep fear from ordinary folk.

quest:3105.text: Tainted Letter. At Northshire, Tainted Letter calls novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards for instruction in the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle entrusts it to Marshal McBride, who delivers it to her recruits. Novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride after proving themselves against the kobold menace. While priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, warlocks must tread carefully. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter, which directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties. Drusilla warns that warlocks walk a precarious path under the watchful eyes of Stormwind's guards, whom she calls 'pathetic mundanes.' Drawing power from the Twisting Nether and communing with demons always risk corruption. She counsels patience, prudence, and firm self-control when handling those dark energies, but says caution must not extinguish a warlock's ambition.

quest:3106.text: Simple Rune. Simple Rune is an introductory task given to novice dwarven warriors in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm on behalf of the warrior trainer Thran Khorman, it directs fresh recruits inside Anvilmar to begin their martial training. As young recruits clear pests and prove their grit around Coldridge Valley, veteran scouts keep a watchful eye out for promising fighters. Sten Stoutarm delivers an inscribed stone—a simple rune—handed off to him by Thran Khorman. This summons calls martial hopefuls from the snowy valley paths into the warm forge-hall of Anvilmar to formally pledge themselves to the warrior's trade. Reporting to Thran offers an immediate glimpse into the harsh realities facing modern Dun Morogh. The veteran trainer speaks frankly about the kingdom's shifting landscape: displaced gnomes seeking refuge after catastrophic explosions destroyed Gnomeregan, fellow dwarves wielding foreign arcane arts or taking up human devotion to the Holy Light, and an ever-present menace of subterranean troggs clawing at the mountain borders. In Thran's eyes, solid martial discipline remains the bedrock required to withstand it all.

quest:3107.text: Consecrated Rune. The Consecrated Rune is an introductory summons delivered to fledgling dwarven paladins in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm on behalf of Bromos Grummner, it marks an initiate's formal induction into the Knights of the Silver Hand. While novice adventurers clear out troggs and wolves around Coldridge Valley, the local leaders keep a close eye on those who display a gift for divine martial prowess. Sten Stoutarm delivers this inscribed rune to young paladins, instructing them to seek out Bromos Grummner inside the warmth of Anvilmar. It serves as both an invitation and an official notice that raw potential must now be tempered with discipline. Though the Knights of the Silver Hand originated among the humans of Lordaeron, Ironforge dwarves embraced the philosophy of the Holy Light with fierce devotion. Bromos Grummner welcomes initiates into the brotherhood, reminding them that dwarven paladins now share the solemn duty of protecting Azeroth. Grounded in sacrifice, tradition, and martial virtue, the order demands that recruits take up hammer and faith in equal measure.

quest:3108.text: Etched Rune. The Etched Rune is a written summons delivered to novice dwarven hunters assisting the guard in Coldridge Valley. Passed on by Sten Stoutarm, the inscribed stone directs fledgling trackers to seek out Thorgas Grimson inside Anvilmar to formally begin their martial and wilderness training. While helping Sten Stoutarm deal with nearby threats around Coldridge Valley, promising dwarven hunters are handed an inscribed stone tablet known as the Etched Rune. Rather than delivering spoken orders or simple parchment, dwarven mentors favor carved runes to impart formal missives. The rune instructs the recipient to take stock of their early work and present themselves indoors at Anvilmar for deeper instruction in the art of the hunt. Presenting the rune to Thorgas Grimson marks a hunter's entry into formal discipline. Thorgas stresses that mountaineering and survival in Khaz Modan demand deep respect for the harsh environment: reading tracks in bitter snowdrifts, maintaining one's weapon and ammunition, and understanding the wild beasts that roam the crags. The etched stone serves as the hunter's first step from a lone wanderer with a gun into an apprentice of Anvilmar's veteran pathfinders.

quest:3109.text: Encrypted Rune. The Encrypted Rune is a coded missive delivered to aspiring rogues taking their first steps in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm, the etched message directs promising shadows into Anvilmar to report to the rogue trainer, Solm Hargrin. While assisting Sten Stoutarm out in the snowy passes of Coldridge Valley, sharp-eyed rogues receive a curious etched stone. Sten admits the piece was slipped to him to hand over, suspecting it came directly from Solm Hargrin. Rather than shouting out across the courtyard for potential scouts and scoundrels, Solm uses an encrypted rune to test a novice's discretion and summon them indoors. Inside Anvilmar, Solm Hargrin welcomes newly arrived operatives to the craft. He offers to teach the maneuvers, strikes, and subtle arts that keep an operative breathing and lining their pockets with coin. Beyond sharpening their daggers, Solm reminds dwarven rogues to look out for their displaced gnomish allies, who are still recovering from the catastrophic fall of Gnomeregan.

quest:311.text: Return to Marleth. Return to Marleth marks the mischievous conclusion to a heated brewing feud in Dun Morogh. Having infiltrated the Kharanos cellar and swapped in a keg of Marleth's fiery Scalder, an adventurer returns to Brewnall Village with a prize barrel of Thunder Ale as indisputable proof. Dwarven rivalries are rarely settled with diplomacy when there is ale on the line. Marleth Barleybrew of Brewnall Village harbors a fierce competitive grudge against the distillers of Kharanos, creators of the famed Thunder Ale. After having her potent 'Scalder' slipped into the Thunderbrew cellar unnoticed, Marleth demands evidence of the feat. Hoisting a genuine barrel of Thunder Ale from beneath their noses serves as both trophy and leverage. Hauling the heavy keg back across the snowswept ridges to Brewnall Village finishes the caper. Marleth is thrilled to see the plan succeed, gleefully reveling in outsmarting Kharanos's guards and cellar masters. While harmless on the surface, the stunt cements the fierce, uncompromising pride that different dwarven families pour into their signature recipes across Dun Morogh.

quest:3110.text: Hallowed Rune. Hallowed Rune is an introductory quest for fledgling dwarven priests in Coldridge Valley. Sten Stoutarm passes along an inscribed rune from priest trainer Branstock Khalder, summoning the novice inside Anvilmar to deepen their connection with the Holy Light. While assisting Sten Stoutarm with clearing the immediate threats outside Anvilmar, a newly arrived priest catches the eye of the settlement's spiritual guide. Branstock Khalder entrusts Sten with a hallowed rune inscribed with prayers and guidance, directing the young adventurer to step inside the sturdy halls of Anvilmar to formally begin their sacred studies. Though dwarven culture often emphasizes martial fortitude and heavy plate, the Holy Light remains a cornerstone of Ironforge society. In Coldridge Valley, holy casters play a vital role alongside warriors and hunters in shielding the enclave from aggressive trogg incursions and dangerous wildlife creeping through the snow drifts.

quest:3112.text: Simple Memorandum. The Simple Memorandum is a missive delivered to aspiring gnome warriors starting out in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm outside, it directs newly trained fighters into Anvilmar to meet Thran Khorman, who has pledged to prepare them for reclaiming Gnomeregan. While clearing out the troggs and boars troubling Coldridge Valley for mountaineer Sten Stoutarm, a young gnome warrior receives a brief message slipped into the dwarf's hands. Recognizing the potential in the refugee recruit, veteran trainer Thran Khorman uses the memorandum to call the newcomer into Anvilmar's central hall to begin proper martial instruction. Though dwarven trainers might occasionally tease gnome warriors about their diminutive stature, Thran Khorman takes their struggle seriously. Sympathizing with the loss of Gnomeregan, Thran likens the gnomes' plight to how dwarves would feel if Ironforge fell to the Dark Irons. In honoring his word, he pledges to instruct exile fighters in the arts of warfare until they are ready to win back their home.

quest:3113.text: Encrypted Memorandum. The Encrypted Memorandum is an introductory summons directed at fledgling gnome rogues arriving in Coldridge Valley. Passed through Sten Stoutarm, the disguised note quietly directs new operatives to seek out Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. While newcomer gnomes assist the mountaineers of Coldridge Valley with local trogg threats, Sten Stoutarm delivers a folded piece of parchment passed to him in confidence. Posing superficially as an official memorandum, the note is an invitation to meet Solm Hargrin, the resident rogue trainer stationed inside Anvilmar. The message reflects the uneasy reality facing the gnomes after the sudden fall of Gnomeregan. Displaced from their subterranean home, gnome survivors must share close quarters with their dwarven hosts in Dun Morogh. Solm Hargrin recognizes that rogues draw suspicion when items vanish, and he advocates for unspoken solidarity among practitioners of the craft to ensure their mutual survival.

quest:3114.text: Glyphic Memorandum. Glyphic Memorandum is an introductory task directing novice mages in Coldridge Valley to their local trainer inside Anvilmar. Entrusted to mountaineer Sten Stoutarm, the missive summons budding arcane practitioners to seek out the eccentric gnome Marryk Nurribit to begin their formal spellcraft studies. While assisting mountaineer Sten Stoutarm with early duties across Coldridge Valley, newly arrived mages find themselves summoned by local arcane authority. Sten receives a written memorandum addressed to the fledgling spellcaster and passes it along, advising them to take a moment to read its contents and head inside the warmth of Anvilmar to meet its author. The author of the memorandum is Marryk Nurribit, a gnome mage trainer stationed inside Anvilmar. Rather than drowning his pupil in dense theoretical lectures, Marryk offers straightforward, grounded advice: stay out of serious trouble, save coin for training and tavern drinks, and strictly avoid the radioactive disaster that is fallen Gnomeregan. With basic expectations set, Marryk stands ready to tutor newcomers in the arcane arts.

quest:3115.text: Tainted Memorandum. Tainted Memorandum is an introductory quest for fledgling gnome warlocks taking their first steps in Coldridge Valley. Passed quietly through Sten Stoutarm, the missive summons the neophyte to the shadows of Anvilmar to meet Alamar Grimm, who preaches self-reliance through dark power rather than trust in their dwarven hosts. Even in the frozen outpost of Coldridge Valley, the practice of the dark arts is met with deep suspicion. While helping Sten Stoutarm deal with local threats, young gnome warlocks receive a slipped note. Sten delivers it reluctantly, giving voice to the uneasy truce that allows warlocks in Alliance lands: 'watch yerself... your kind ain't too trusted 'round these parts.' Upon answering the note, the warlock meets Alamar Grimm lurking inside the halls of Anvilmar. Grimm does not mince words regarding the gnomes' plight. To his eyes, conventional tinkering and ordinary magic failed Gnomeregan utterly, driving their people to near extinction and leaving them stranded as second-class refugees dependent on dwarf goodwill. Rather than praying to the Holy Light or putting faith in dwarven politics, Grimm urges his pupil to summon and master fiends who offer unconditional obedience.

quest:3116.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, Alyissia calls young night elf warriors to defend their people. Conservator Ilthalaine carries her summons as the Kaldorei face changes across Teldrassil and beyond. After you prove your basic survival skills against Shadowglen's restless wildlife, Conservator Ilthalaine gives you an inscribed sigil. The token formally marks your move into combat training. It carries a request from Alyissia, the warrior trainer at Aldrassil, asking you to dedicate your strength to defending your people. Alyissia sets your training against a time of rapid change and danger. In only a few years, the night elves have raised the World Tree Teldrassil, seen a taint spread through forest beasts near and far, and reconnected with ancient lands once thought lost, including Feralas. The Kaldorei need capable defenders against these perils. Alyissia prepares young Kaldorei for more than combat. She urges you not to judge outsiders who arrive on Teldrassil by their race. Some travelers may not act from pure generosity, but allies are vital to the Kaldorei's defense. As you take up the work of protecting your people, she asks you to offer them reasonable trust.

quest:3117.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls young night elf hunters to Aldrassil. Through Conservator Ilthalaine, Ayanna Everstride summons them to meet their trainer and begin learning archery and beastcraft. After young kaldorei hunters help defend Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them an inscribed token. A messenger brought it from their mentor, Ayanna Everstride. The sigil directs each novice up into Aldrassil’s high boughs, where the trainers watch over the canopy. Meeting Ayanna begins a hunter’s training on Teldrassil. She teaches novices marksmanship and how to understand Kalimdor’s wild creatures. A hunter must respect their beast companions and meet the world’s unseen dangers with awareness and humility.

quest:3118.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, a coded summons calls new night elf rogues to begin their training. Conservator Ilthalaine carries it for Frahun Shadewhisper, who also warns of the fragile peace across Kalimdor. While young night elves study nature's balance under Conservator Ilthalaine, those drawn to stealth receive a quieter summons. A runner brings the Encrypted Sigil from Frahun Shadewhisper, Shadowglen's rogue mentor. Its ciphers are meant for initiates of the trade. The bearer is to decipher the message and find Frahun near the roots of Aldrassil to begin instruction. Frahun's message also warns of Kalimdor's uncertain peace. The Third War has ended, but the truce between the Alliance and the emerging Horde remains fragile. Rogue scouts and informers in Shadowglen are urged to sharpen their eyes and ears early. They watch for threats and covert provocations that could renew war across the borders.

quest:3119.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, young night elf priests are called to begin their training in Aldrassil. Conservator Ilthalaine passes along Shanda's message as novices learn to wield Elune's grace. Night elf priests serve Elune as handmaidens and servants of the moon goddess. When a young kaldorei in Shadowglen shows devotion and an affinity for the divine light, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them a hallowed sigil. Shanda, the priest trainer, sent the token by messenger as an invitation to come to Aldrassil and begin spiritual training. Shanda tells the young acolyte that unusual change has reached Teldrassil's sheltered sanctuary. Travelers fill the World Tree's boughs, including members of the wider Alliance who have leave to meet with the kaldorei. The wider world calls, but Shanda urges novices to first attend to the troubles facing Shadowglen before turning to conflicts beyond it.

quest:312.text: Tundra MacGrann's Stolen Stash. Tundra MacGrann, an injured dwarven hunter living out in the cold crags of Dun Morogh, has lost his winter supplies to a notorious local beast. A massive yeti known as Old Icebeard hauled off MacGrann's thorium-reinforced meat locker into its den. Unable to outrun the beast on a bum leg, the hunter relies on passing adventurers to slip inside and retrieve his provisions. Surviving the harsh winters of Dun Morogh demands preparation, especially for mountaineers living outside the warmth of Kharanos and Ironforge. Tundra MacGrann had diligently salted away an entire month's worth of dried meats to outlast the coming cold season flurries. Taking precautions against hungry wild bears, he sealed his rations inside a reinforced thorium meat locker. Unfortunately, he did not account for the sheer brute strength of the mountain yetis, who carried the entire chest away rather than trying to open it on the spot. The culprit behind the theft is Old Icebeard, a feared and vicious yeti lurking in the jagged hills. While MacGrann was away hunting deer, Icebeard snatched the chest and dragged it back to his mountain cave. Though MacGrann remains confident that even a yeti cannot shatter solid thorium plating, his own injured leg makes a recovery mission suicidal. Any brave soul venturing into the cave must either contend directly with the beast or time their intrusion carefully while the monster is out prowling the snowdrifts.

quest:3120.text: Verdant Sigil. A summons reaches newly awakened night elf druids in Shadowglen. Conservator Ilthalaine passes the Verdant Sigil to fledgling shapeshifters, directing them to Mardant Strongoak within Aldrassil. The token marks the start of their formal training in nature and the Emerald Dream. When a young night elf shows promise in keeping Shadowglen's balance, the order calls for a formal introduction. A runner brings the Verdant Sigil to Conservator Ilthalaine, who entrusts it to the initiate. The token shows that the circle in Aldrassil has taken notice and invites the young druid to begin formal training. Presenting the sigil to Mardant Strongoak inside Aldrassil brings the initiate into the fold. Deeper communion with the Emerald Dream and mastery of animal forms lie ahead. For now, Mardant becomes their first guide, teaching them to read nature's spirits and channel the raw power of the woods.

quest:313.text: The Grizzled Den. Pilot Stonegear of Kharanos is looking for someone with true dwarven grit to spruce up his beloved siege engine, Trollplow. To test an aspiring adventurer's mettle, he sends them west into the perilous cavern known as the Grizzled Den to hunt savage wendigos for their thick pelts. Operating a massive dwarven siege tank requires nerves of iron and the constitution to handle teeth-rattling machinery in freezing mountain air. Pilot Stonegear, stationed at Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, claims to have both in spades. Rather than simply giving up work or respect easily, he challenges newcomers to prove they possess the same stalwart temperament by trekking into the frozen hills to face native beasts. Stonegear's siege engine bears the proud and unsubtle name of Trollplow, but its cramped, iron-plated cabin is brutally cold in the bitter Dun Morogh climate. Stonegear hits upon a practical yet wild solution: wendigo pelt. Harvesting thick manes from the ferocious wendigos stalking the Grizzled Den provides the materials needed to fashion a durable, warm rug for Trollplow's deck while keeping local beast numbers in check.

quest:317.text: Stocking Jetsteam. Stocking Jetsteam is an Alliance quest offered by Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Preparing his siege engine for an extended deployment with the Ironforge Siege Brigade, the pilot enlists local hunters to gather boar meat and bear pelts to provision his crew. Stationed just outside Kharanos at Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz oversees preparations for an upcoming long-haul operation on behalf of the Siege Brigade. His siege tank, dubbed Jetsteam, requires both mechanical tuning from master engineer Beldin Steelgrill and a month's worth of field provisions to keep its crew functional in the harsh sub-zero temperatures of Dun Morogh. Because Beldin Steelgrill is occupied under Jetsteam's hood, Bellowfiz cannot abandon his vehicle to gather rations and insulation. He directs travelers to hunt in the snowy plains south of the Grizzled Den, where indigenous boars provide hardy meat for food and native bears yield thick pelts suitable for warm tank bedding.

quest:318.text: Evershine. Evershine is an Alliance delivery quest beginning with Pilot Bellowfiz near Kharanos. The dwarven siege engine pilot sends travelers westward to Brewnall Village to fetch a potent dwarven brew concocted by Rejold Barleybrew. The liquor doubles as a warming drink and an emergency, high-octane fuel for Bellowfiz's siege engine. Dwarven brewing is famed throughout Khaz Modan, but Rejold Barleybrew's recipes in Brewnall Village push the boundaries of standard fermentation. His experimental beverage, Evershine, is infamous for knocking all but the sturdiest dwarves flat on their backs. Despite its fierce potency, it is prized in the bitter cold of Dun Morogh for its sheer heating power. Siege pilots often find unorthodox uses for everyday materials, and Pilot Bellowfiz is no exception. Operating out of Steelgrill's Depot outside Kharanos, Bellowfiz relies on Evershine not just as a nip to stave off the freezing winds, but as supplementary fuel. Dumping the volatile alcohol directly into the furnace of his siege engine, Jetsteam, provides an explosive surge of emergency power that has gotten him out of more than one tight spot.

quest:319.text: A Favor for Evershine. To secure a cask of Evershine for Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot, an adventurer must first lend a hand to Brewnall Village. Brewer Rejold Barleybrew refuses to part with his liquor until the dangerous predators roaming the nearby snowdrifts are thinned out. Rejold Barleybrew has the cask of Evershine that Pilot Bellowfiz requires, but he is in no hurry to surrender his prized brew for free. Rather than asking for coin, Rejold asks for protection. The wild beasts of western Dun Morogh—ravenous Ice Claw Bears, thick-hided Elder Crag Boars, and prowling Snow Leopards—wander uncomfortably close to Brewnall Village, creating constant distraction and peril for the locals. While Rejold is quick to insist that no self-respecting dwarf cowers before wild animals, dealing with predators around the clock consumes valuable hours. Culling the local wildlife gives the villagers the peace they need to focus on distillation and smithing without keeping one eye perpetually on the tree line.

quest:3221.text: Speak with Renferrel. Speak with Renferrel is a brief errand within the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. High Executor Hadrec directs you back to the Royal Apothecary Society's local researcher to discuss findings regarding tainted wolf hearts. After assisting the Deathstalkers across Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec passes along an urgent message from Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel has spent time analyzing the discolored wolf hearts gathered from the local wildlife and requires your presence immediately. Apothecary Renferrel serves the Royal Apothecary Society from his laboratory inside the crypt at the Sepulcher. His ongoing work explores how dark magic and disease are altering the beasts of Silverpine, bridging frontline military recon with chemical research.

quest:3261.text: Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, seasoned Horde hunters seek guidance from Jorn Skyseer. After you hunt local raptors for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker offers deeper lessons. You have hunted the cunning sunscale and scytheclaw raptors stalking the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows martial skill must be joined with understanding of the land's great beasts. With her mentorship complete, she sends you south. Follow the Gold Road south through increasingly rugged plains to Camp Taurajo, a vital tauren settlement near the southern wilds. Jorn Skyseer waits there, an elder tracker ready to teach hunters how to pursue elusive, legendary quarry across the Barrens.

quest:3281.text: Stolen Silver. Gazrog at the Crossroads sends you after payroll silver stolen by raptors. Rumors of their cunning lead you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back. Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and the raptors have taken their wages. You are sent to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. When raptors ambushed the payroll shipment, Gazrog first sought vengeance. But killing the pack would not restore the missing money. The Horde must learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin, and where they took them. Scouts found a raptor nest between two craggy peaks, south of Ratchet and northwest of Northwatch Hold. The creatures dragged the intact lockbox into their territory, where they guard it alongside eggs and fresh kills. Tales of raptor cunning and hoarding now seem true to Gazrog. Ordinary beasts rarely stash metallic valuables.

quest:33.text: Wolves Across the Border. Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves prowling Northshire Valley and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where the valley’s needs continue despite the guards’ focus on Defias bandits. Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls with a grudge against the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have limited strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits, while tradesfolk still have daily needs. Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking. Wolves roam closer to Northshire Abbey as patrols weaken. The Kingdom of Stormwind has too few troops and is strained by missing leadership. Young wolves and timber wolves now prowl the abbey’s paths and orchards. Hunting them supplies Eagan’s pantry and makes nearby trails safer for novitiates, laborers, and newly arrived defenders.

quest:3301.text: Mura Runetotem. You carry a snapjaw shell from the Barrens across the sea to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine Forest. Its strange vitality may help the tauren healer aid the Forsaken. Tonga Runetotem notices something peculiar about altered snapjaws while investigating the magically changed wildlife around the Barrens oases. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. He asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, who is stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms. Mura Runetotem is at the Sepulcher, a Forsaken outpost in Silverpine Forest. She made the arduous journey there to help the Horde's newest allies cleanse and renew their ailing, blighted woodland. Mura hopes the shell's inner glow and enduring spark of life will reveal ways to restore vitality to the northern continent.

quest:332.text: Wine Shop Advert. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina draws passersby to his family's wine shop. He offers a voucher for a free bottle of vintage wine from their canal-side storefront, a small sign of trade in the reconstructed capital. Everyday life in Stormwind revolves around brisk commerce. Renato Gallina walks the Trade District's cobbled streets, promoting Gallina Winery, the small shop he runs with his sister, Suzetta. He hands flyers to thirsty travelers and locals, each offering a free tasting. The Gallina family offers a bottle of their famous pinot noir. Follow the ticket to the winery entrance near the canals, where Suzetta Gallina hands over the bottle. The family hopes a taste of their signature wine will bring newcomers back.

quest:333.text: Harlan Needs a Resupply. Harlan Bagley, a Stormwind merchant, cannot keep sturdy clothes and armor in stock. As demand surges, he sends an urgent cloth order to Rema Schneider at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, unaware of the conflicts brewing beyond the city walls. Across Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley's shelves are emptying fast. Citizens and wandering adventurers are buying reinforced tunics, traveling clothes, and battle-ready armor. Harlan wonders if people are preparing for a harsh season or winter, but the rush has left his shop short of finished cloth. Harlan sends a runner across the city's waterways to Rema Schneider, a seamstress at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is glad of his trade, yet the sudden demand for protective clothing troubles her. Rumors of tension spread through the kingdom, and Rema wonders whether the House of Nobles is hiding talk of open war from ordinary people.

quest:334.text: Package for Thurman. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider needs her son Thurman’s tailoring supplies at Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. He left home without his shears and needles, and Rema asks you to carry them to his workshop. Rema Schneider worries that Thurman will fall behind in his tailoring work without his shears and needles. He left home in a rush, and his mother asks you to carry the tools across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

quest:3361.text: A Refugee's Quandary. Following the disastrous fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and radiation, displaced gnomes have fled into the snowy wilds of Dun Morogh. Outside Anvilmar, an engineer named Felix Whindlebolt lost his vital belongings and tools to Frostmane troll scavengers during the panicked evacuation. When subterranean troggs overran the high-tech city of Gnomeregan, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his advisors authorized the release of radioactive gas in a desperate bid to eradicate the invaders. The gambit backfired catastrophically, slaying thousands of innocents, mutating survivors into mindless leper gnomes, and forcing the remaining populace into a frantic exodus across Dun Morogh. Fleeing engineers and tinkerers carried whatever prized tools and blueprints they could save. However, the icy mountain passes between Gnomeregan and Coldridge Valley are prowled by indigenous Frostmane trolls. As Felix Whindlebolt scrambled toward the sanctuary of Anvilmar, Frostmane raiders snatched his tool chest, lockbox, and bucket of bolts, carting them off to their camps southwest of town.

quest:3364.text: Scalding Mornbrew Delivery. Scalding Mornbrew Delivery is a hurried errand through Coldridge Valley to deliver fresh hot drink before it chills in the mountain frost. Nori Pridedrift entrusts the delivery to an adventurer to ensure Durnan Furcutter receives his mornbrew piping hot. Dun Morogh's biting cold has ruined many a hot meal, and Mornbrew is no exception. After completing a delivery to Grelin Whitebeard, Nori Pridedrift realizes he lacks the time to bring another fresh cup to Anvilmar before it freezes into an unpalatable slush. Rather than let his customer down, he enlists any swift traveler willing to brave the snow. Durnan Furcutter, stationed inside the warmth of Anvilmar's mountain hall, is known to be particular about his refreshments. Chilly Mornbrew simply will not do. Delivering the piping drink intact earns a weary dwarf a much-needed break from his duties, though Nori still expects his favorite mug returned in one piece.

quest:3365.text: Bring Back the Mug. After delivering a piping hot draught of Mornbrew across the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, one final errand remains: returning the empty tankard. Durnan Furcutter sends the runner back across Coldridge Valley to return Nori Pridedrift's prized mug. It is a simple courtesy, but one the brew seller deeply appreciates. Serving piping hot Mornbrew out in the biting freeze of Dun Morogh is a delicate business. Once Durnan Furcutter has finished warming his bones with the scalding brew, the empty tankard cannot simply be tossed in the snow. Dwarven hospitality runs on mutual respect, and letting good dishware go missing is a sure way to find oneself cut off from future rounds. Returning to Coldridge Valley completes the delivery run for Nori Pridedrift. As Nori is fond of reminding forgetful couriers, sturdy drinkware does not simply grow on trees—especially not in the subzero crags of the dwarven homeland. Returning the empty vessel in one piece cements an adventurer's reputation as a reliable hand in the local community.

quest:3376.text: Break Sharptusk!. Break Sharptusk! is a decisive rite of passage issued by Brave Windfeather on Red Cloud Mesa. To secure the tauren homeland against ongoing raids, young champions are sent east into Brambleblade Ravine to slay Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle. Eliminating the Bristleback chieftain strikes a severe blow against the quilboar encroaching upon Mulgore. The grassy heights of Red Cloud Mesa have long served as a peaceful sanctuary where young tauren learn the traditions of the hunt and attunement with the Earth Mother. However, this peace is constantly contested. To the east lies Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked gulch claimed by the hostile Bristleback quilboar tribe. The quilboar view the tauren as invaders stealing sacred ground, launching relentless skirmishes against the tribes attempting to establish a stable life in Mulgore. The persistent attacks on the mesa are not aimless frenzy; they are coordinated under the brutal leadership of Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle. Residing in a fortified makeshift village deep within the ravine, Sharptusk directs his warriors and geomancers against the Shu'halo. Recognizing that the Bristleback will never cease their raids while their chief still draws breath, Brave Windfeather commands an aspiring hero to breach the ravine, strike down Thornmantle, and return with his severed head as proof. For young tauren and their allies, hunting Sharptusk is more than a simple execution—it is an initiation into the harsh realities of survival. As Brave Windfeather teaches, the hunt against beasts teaches patience, but hunting an enemy cunning enough to hunt back tests courage, awareness, and martial discipline. Bringing down Sharptusk delivers justice for fallen kin and marks the hunter's readiness to venture out into the wider plains of Mulgore.

quest:35.text: Further Concerns. Marshal Dughan sends an Alliance courier east from Goldshire to check reports of danger. You cross Elwynn Forest to speak with Guard Thomas, who watches the river crossing toward Redridge. Rumors tell of hostile aquatic creatures creeping along Elwynn's riverbanks. Marshal Dughan commands the Goldshire garrison, where banditry and vermin already trouble the center of the forest. He will not dismiss the reports, but he cannot spare guards from town. Instead, he sends you east to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry at the bridge over the river toward Redridge. Guard Thomas has held the bridge outpost for more than a week and has seen what Goldshire's leaders only feared. Hostile, semi-intelligent murlocs have made camps along the waterways of eastern Elwynn. Stormwind's army is absent, while local garrisons protect town walls and supply lines. That leaves rural bridge posts like Thomas's isolated before the growing danger.

quest:3519.text: A Friend in Need. Iverron lies bitten and in danger in Shadowglen. The young night elf calls for Dirania Silvershine, whose help may save him from Githyiss the Vile's venom. Iverron lies weakened after a bite from Githyiss the Vile. He ignored warnings and went too near the webwood caverns, where the vicious spider struck. Dizziness and failing strength leave him unable to reach safety alone. Iverron sends passersby toward Aldrassil's central tree to find Dirania Silvershine. She looks out for him and knows the dangers of Shadowglen. His life may depend on her preparing an antidote before the venom proves fatal.

quest:3521.text: Iverron's Antidote. Iverron's Antidote is an urgent task in Shadowglen to save a poisoned night elf scout. By gathering wild mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor, adventurers help Dirania Silvershine brew a remedy before the venom takes full hold. While scouting the boughs of Shadowglen, young Iverron fell victim to the poisonous fangs of the local Webwood spiders. Collapsed and dying, his survival depends entirely on the herbal knowledge of Dirania Silvershine at Aldrassil. With the youth fading fast, she must quickly prepare a specialized concoction to neutralize the aggressive venom coursing through his blood. Dirania's recipe relies on the restorative flora of Teldrassil balanced against the venom itself. Hyacinth mushrooms, favored by the thieving grell to the south, provide an earthy base, while delicate Moonpetal lilies gathered from tranquil forest pools offer purifying qualities. To finish the draft, a sample of Webwood ichor must be extracted directly from the spiders prowling near Shadowthread Cave to tailor the cure to their specific poison.

quest:3522.text: Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron waits for medicine before its strength fades. Poisoned by Webwood spiders, the night elf scout depends on Dirania Silvershine's brew, which must reach him within five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the cure from fresh venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi. The unstable mixture keeps its strength for only five minutes after it is distilled. Whoever carries the vial must sprint straight from the glade toward the northern heights without hesitation. Webwood spiders around Shadowglen's barrows and caves have poisoned Iverron. He admits he has a habit of stumbling into danger and often depends on Dirania's herbal skill to save him. Even after drinking the antidote, his recovery is fragile. The hostile spiders still guard his way home, and he remains wary of them.

quest:3524.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore, Washed Ashore begins an inquiry into the many sea creatures dying on its shore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde starts it in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where priestesses fear the strandings may be an ill omen. Darkshore has seen great sea creatures beach themselves from time to time, a tragic but occasional sight. Now the strandings come in growing numbers along the coast. The Priestesses of Elune in the Temple of the Moon see more than a natural oddity in these deaths. They fear the pattern may bring ill omens to northern Kalimdor. The Temple of the Moon sends scholar Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to the port town of Auberdine to learn why the great beasts are coming ashore. She gathers biological samples to send by hippogryph to Darnassus for close examination. But Greymist murlocs swarm the carcasses in the surf, scavenging the remains and keeping researchers from the bones without armed protection.

quest:353.text: Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The road leads from Stormwind's Dwarven District to an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make a weapon for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The Stormpike clan is respected in Ironforge for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore turns to trustworthy travelers to carry the axe north, across the distance between Stormwind and the dwarven borderlands. At Loch Modan's northern guard tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches over lands troubled by wandering troggs and burrowing kobolds. The southern human kingdoms face rumors of unrest and banditry, while the dwarven frontier has dangers of its own. Stormpike needs a new blade to help keep the mountain passes secure.

quest:354.text: Deaths in the Family. Coleman Farthing, a former mill worker now dwelling in Brill, seeks personal vengeance against the aristocratic Agamand family. Convinced to stay and defend their estates against the Scourge during the Third War, Farthing and his fellow workers perished alongside their stubborn employers, only for the Agamands to rise as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, the Agamand family stood as the wealthiest and most influential agrarian dynasty in Tirisfal Glades. Their sprawling mills and fertile pastures produced bountiful grain, commanding the labor of dozens of tenant farmers and millers. When the Plague of Undeath crept across the kingdom, the Agamands refused to flee or abandon their ancestral holdings, convinced that stone walls and loyal workers could hold off the horrors advancing from the east. Believing their lords' assurances, loyal employees like Coleman Farthing stood their ground to defend the estate. The defense proved futile against the Scourge's relentless onslaught. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered, their bodies rotting where they fell before being raised into undeath. While Farthing eventually broke free through Sylvanas Windrunner's liberation, the Agamand patriarchs and heirs remained trapped under the Lich King's mental grip, wandering the ruined mills as mindless Scourge sentries. Now residing in Brill, Coleman Farthing harbors intense resentment toward the former masters whose arrogance cost him his mortal life. Seeking closure and retribution, he sends Forsaken champions to Agamand Mills to destroy Gregor, Nissa, and Thurman Agamand. Farthing openly hopes that behind their rotting visages, his former masters retained just enough consciousness to feel terror as their unlife was violently brought to an end.

quest:355.text: Speak with Sevren. Following the settling of Coleman Farthing's personal score at Agamand Mills, Magistrate Sevren summons the adventurer to Brill. The mills house far more than bitter family ghosts; they represent an active Scourge peril on the settlement's northern border. Coleman Farthing sought personal retribution against his former neighbors, the Agamands, sending travelers north to tear through the undead lurking about the flour mills. Once those remains were delivered, Coleman recognized that his private grudge intersected with a wider tactical problem: the entire Agamand estate remains swarming with mindlessly aggressive Scourge minions right on Brill's doorstep. Magistrate Sevren oversees civic and military security in Brill for the Dark Lady. Impressed by reports of an adventurer capable of surviving deep incursions into the haunted farmlands, Sevren steps in to direct those capable hands toward the root of the infestation—the ancient Agamand family crypt itself.

quest:356.text: Rear Guard Patrol. Rear Guard Patrol is a military scouting mission tasked by Deathguard Linnea to protect the Forsaken defenses along Tirisfal's eastern border. It directs operatives to purge stray Scourge horrors and lingering spirits haunting the Balnir Farmstead before they can compromise the supply lines supporting the Bulwark. The Bulwark stands as the primary bulwark holding back the pestilence and armies of the Western Plaguelands from spilling into Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Linnea oversees rear-echelon security along this frontier. Because the line cannot afford to divide its forces against ambushes from behind, any undead that bypass the choke point must be destroyed before they can sever the supply lines feeding the front. Once a working farm of eastern Tirisfal, the Balnir Farmstead fell to ruin during the Third War. Now thoroughly blighted, the overgrown fields and crumbling stables provide cover for interloping Bleeding Horrors and restless, Wandering Spirits. Clearing the site denies the Lich King a staging post inside Tirisfal itself and safeguards the road for Horde reinforcements.

quest:357.text: The Lich's Identity. The Lich's Identity is an Undercity quest given by Bethor Iceshard in the Magic Quarter. Seeking to uncover the identity of a reclusive lich living on Brightwater Lake, Bethor sends an emissary to steal the figure's spellbook to gauge his power and allegiance. North of the Undercity, in the misty waters of Brightwater Lake, a lone lich dwells in self-imposed exile on a small island. Unlike the mindless pawns of the Lich King, this necromancer possesses his own free will, yet he lives in deep paranoia. Convinced that any undead who approach him are Scourge thralls sent to drag him back into servitude, he unleashes his summoned minions on anyone setting foot on his shores. Word of the rogue lich eventually reached Bethor Iceshard, the archmage overseeing the mages in the Undercity. Bethor recognized the strategic importance of such an entity: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner seeks every scrap of magical mastery and every capable will to bolster the Forsaken against their many foes. To assess whether the hermit could be recruited, Bethor requires proof of his identity and necromantic expertise.

quest:358.text: Graverobbers. Magistrate Sevren of Brill tasks adventurers with purging Rot Hide gnolls from the Mass Grave southwest of Garren's Haunt. These undead beasts were sent by the Scourge to dig up the corpses of early plague victims to swell their ranks. Slaying them and recovering their embalming ichor protects the fallen and aids the Royal Apothecary Society's research. When the Plague of Undeath first tore through Tirisfal Glades, the dead piled up faster than formal burials could accommodate. Immense mass graves were dug across the north to contain the staggering loss. Until recently, those buried remains escaped resurrection. Now, however, the Scourge has unleashed Rot Hide gnolls upon the trenches southwest of Garren's Haunt, sending them to exhumate the decayed remains to reinforce the Lich King's armies. The Rot Hides are sustained by embalming ichor, an alchemical concoction that preserves and animates their rotting frames. By commanding scouts to slay the graverobbers and extract this fluid, Magistrate Sevren strikes two blows at once: halting the Scourge's harvest of raw bodies and delivering valuable biological specimens directly to the apothecaries in Brill, who seek to turn the Lich King's own craft against him.

quest:36.text: Westfall Stew. In Westfall, another family is leaving its farm as banditry drives homesteaders from their land. Before departing, Verna Furlbrow entrusts her cherished local recipe to Salma Saldean. Defias thieves and wild mechanical harvest reapers have driven Verna and Farmer Furlbrow from their family acreage. They pack their wagon and prepare to seek refuge behind Stormwind's walls. Before leaving, Verna gives her neighbor Salma Saldean the recipe for Westfall Stew, hoping the farm's home-cooked tradition will live on. Salma Saldean and her husband, Farmer Saldean, still hold their homestead just down the road. Verna's recipe marks the loss of another neighbor to the unrest, yet keeps a local farm tradition alive. Salma sets out to gather the ingredients needed to feed those still struggling on the frontier.

quest:360.text: Return to the Magistrate. Return to the Magistrate concludes an urgent reconnaissance dispatch between the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades and the town of Brill. Having reported to Deathguard Linnea at her waystation east of Brill, adventurers are sent back to deliver troubling news directly to Magistrate Sevren. The message confirms that the mindless minions of the Lich King continue to test the borders of the young Forsaken nation. The eastern road out of Tirisfal Glades leads directly into the blighted ruins of the Western Plaguelands, where the Scourge holds devastating sway. To keep the undead hordes from spilling over into their newly claimed homeland, the Forsaken established the Bulwark—a fortified checkpoint watched from a waystation behind the line by grim sentries like Deathguard Linnea. After gathering reports of what presses against the eastern gate, Linnea sends messengers racing back west along the King's Road toward Brill before enemy infiltrators can capitalize on any gaps. When Magistrate Sevren receives the dispatch in Brill, it confirms his worst fears: Scourge scouts are finding pathways around or through the frontline perimeter. For the Forsaken, every creeping ghoul and mindless skeleton is not merely a military nuisance, but a reminder of the enslavement they broke free from during the fall of Lordaeron. Sevren remains adamant that no matter how ceaseless the Lich King's onslaught becomes, the free undead will never surrender their newfound autonomy.

quest:361.text: A Letter Undelivered. A faded, bloodstained missive found among the skeletal ruins of Agamand Mills, addressed to Yvette Farthing. It reveals a tragic parting between two lovers as the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, offering a glimpse into what the Forsaken left behind when they traded life for undeath. Written by Thurman Agamand, the eldest son of patriarch Gregor Agamand, this unsent parchment never reached its intended recipient before the family estate collapsed into ruin. When the Plague of Undeath consumed Tirisfal Glades, Thurman refused to abandon his ancestral home and kin. Amid the horrors of the onslaught, he took up quill to write one last message to Yvette Farthing, whom he had loved before the kingdom turned to ash.

quest:362.text: The Haunted Mills. Coleman Farthing of Brill seeks vengeance against his former landowners, the Agamands, by having their restless undead remains collected and destroyed. This task sends you north to Agamand Mills to put down Devlin Agamand, the sharp-tongued younger son of the estate. It begins a bitter vendetta against the family who failed to protect Tirisfal's common folk from the Plague. Before the Third War, Agamand Mills stood as the breadbasket of northern Tirisfal, owned by a wealthy landed family. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the common folk looked to the noble landowners for safety, only to find neither sanctuary nor salvation. Coleman Farthing survived in undeath, but his heart remains consumed by hatred for the family he served. Rather than letting them roam in eternal torment, Farthing desires the morbid satisfaction of collecting their bones to desecrate them under his own heel. Devlin Agamand was the younger brother of Thurman Agamand. In life, Devlin was widely remembered as a weak, spiteful, and sharp-tongued youth who stood in stark contrast to his gentle elder brother. When the Plague of Undeath crept into the mill estate, Devlin was among the quickest to fall prey to the corruption. Now, stripped of whatever fragile wit he possessed in life, his mindless corpse chatters incessantly along the northern road leading into the family mills.

quest:363.text: Rude Awakening. Rude Awakening is the first task given to newly awakened Forsaken within the crypts of Deathknell. After rising from death freed from the Lich King's iron grip, you are directed away from the incinerators and sent down the hill to learn the reality of your new existence from Shadow Priest Sarvis. Opening your eyes in the damp subterranean chill of Deathknell's crypt is an unsettling introduction to undeath. Undertaker Mordo stands watch over the freshly interred, sorting the revived into those who have reclaimed their free will and those destined for the burning pits. For many, rising from the grave means waking to rot, cold stone, and total disorientation, having slipped through the grasp of the Scourge by sheer circumstance. Before reaching the chapel, newly awakened dead must grasp a grim truth: they were once mindless tools of the Lich King. It was Lady Sylvanas Windrunner who shattered that psychic enslavement, allowing remnants of former humanity to reclaim independent thought. Stepping up from the tomb and heading down into Deathknell marks the first step into a world where both the living and the Scourge view you as an abomination to be eradicated.

quest:364.text: The Mindless Ones. Shadow Priest Sarvis tasks newly awakened Forsaken with culling the Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies that wander the northern edges of Deathknell. These shambling corpses are Scourge thralls, devoid of free will and utterly bound to the Lich King's command. Not all who rise from the dirt of Lordaeron regain their minds. While the Forsaken threw off the mental domination of Ner'zhul when his power waned, countless corpses remain hollow husks chained to his will. In northern Deathknell, these Mindless and Wretched Zombies wander without purpose other than raw violence. For a newly risen undead, putting them down is the first bitter trial of existence—proving one's autonomy by severing the chains of those who never broke free. Though Shadow Priest Sarvis laments that these vast legions of dead cannot be recruited to bolster the Forsaken's desperate struggle, there is no curing them. The mindless undead are permanently broken instruments of slaughter. Leaving them to roam invites chaos to Deathknell's doorstep and provides the Lich King with easy fodder. Eliminating them is both a tactical necessity and an act of grim finality for Lordaeron's fallen people.

quest:365.text: Fields of Grief. Fields of Grief is an early Forsaken mission assigned by Deathguard Simmer along the road north of Deathknell. It tasks fledglings with raiding a living human farmstead to harvest Tirisfal pumpkins for the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill. For new Forsaken adventurers freshly risen from the crypts of Deathknell, stepping onto the misty roads of Tirisfal Glades is an immediate lesson in hostility. Deathguard Simmer represents the pragmatic malice of Sylvanas Windrunner's forces: survival means seizing what the living possess and turning it toward the Undercity's darker endeavors. The targets of the raid are the mortal human farmers attempting to work the blighted soil west of the road, north of Deathknell. Described by the Deathguard as infesting the realm like mold on a corpse, these peasants cling to their homesteads under the uneasy protection of nearby Scarlet Crusade towers. Snatching their crops deals a spiteful blow to their supplies while feeding the Royal Apothecary Society's endless demand for reagents.

quest:366.text: Return the Book. Bethor Iceshard enchants Gunther Arcanus's stolen spellbook to prove his own freedom and recruit his former Kirin Tor colleague to the Forsaken cause. Taking the tome back to Gunther's island retreat reveals that neither former wizard is a thrall to the Lich King. After discovering that the renegade necromancer on Brightwater Lake was his old companion Gunther Arcanus, Bethor Iceshard devised an ingenious method of communication. Having previously ordered the theft of Gunther's spellbook to uncover the necromancer's identity, Bethor weaves an intricate dweomer into its pages. Rather than a demand or an armed parley, the enchantment serves as an arcane signature, proving that Bethor is not only active in Lordaeron, but completely liberated from the Lich King's mental yoke. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Bethor Iceshard, Gunther Arcanus, and Thule Ravenclaw were fellow students and friends within the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Their paths diverged sharply when the Lich King rose: Thule betrayed his brethren and willingly sided with the Scourge, while Bethor and Gunther both fell to the Plague, and Bethor later broke free alongside Queen Sylvanas. Believing Gunther was either dead or enslaved, Bethor's realization that Gunther also achieved self-willed undeath sparked an urgent effort to draw him into the Forsaken.

quest:367.text: A New Plague. A New Plague is an introductory task in Brill that reveals the Forsaken's overarching strategic ambition. Apothecary Johaan tasks recruits with harvesting the blood of wild darkhounds to lay the groundwork for a virulent pathogen commissioned directly by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. In the damp village of Brill, Apothecary Johaan works on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society under a mandate directly from the Dark Lady. Sylvanas Windrunner has charged her alchemists with crafting a disease unlike anything Azeroth has ever seen. While the original plague of undeath served the Lich King by slaughtering humanity and binding their souls, this new creation is explicitly designed to annihilate Arthas Menethil and lay waste to his Scourge legions. Developing a biological weapon capable of destroying the undead requires grim experimentation. Johaan believes that the blood of indigenous beasts, starting with the fierce darkhounds roaming the gloom of Tirisfal Glades, holds vital chemical properties. By harvesting vials of this tainted animal blood, Johaan begins isolating elements to test whether the natural resilience and predatory biology of native creatures can catalyze a lethal contagion.

quest:368.text: A New Plague. Tasked by Apothecary Johaan in Brill, this errand requires gathering scales from the local Vile Fin murlocs prowling the Tirisfal coast. The Royal Apothecary Society aims to harness unique biological reagents to refine their budding new contagion, ensuring it can spread beyond isolated victims to engulf larger populations. Poisoning a single target is simple alchemy, but formulating a plague capable of sweeping across entire lands demands more complex components. Apothecary Johaan's ongoing research in Brill hinges on creating a disease that can self-propagate and endure in the wild. To engineer this transmissibility, he turns his attention toward the shoreline wildlife of Tirisfal Glades, identifying the resilient biology of the coastal Vile Fin murlocs as a promising source of raw material. The northern and western shores of Tirisfal Glades are plagued by aggressive murloc tribes known as the Vile Fin. Harvesting their scales provides Johaan with organic compounds adapted to damp, harsh conditions. By incorporating the murlocs' slick, resilient scales into his developing cauldron, the apothecary seeks to bolster the virulence and environmental stability of the Royal Apothecary Society's new plague.

quest:3681.text: Tome of Divinity. Tome of Divinity is a summons directed at developing human paladins visiting Ironforge. Master Brandur Ironhammer bids initiates make the journey south to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, where Master Duthorian Rall oversees advanced training in the sacred Tomes of Divinity. While dwarven paladins train vigorously within Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, the broader traditions of the Silver Hand remain deeply entwined with the Church of the Holy Light in human lands. Word sent north from Stormwind calls on promising holy warriors to present themselves directly before the senior priesthood and paladin mentors of the Cathedral of Light. Master Brandur Ironhammer recognizes when a student has progressed far enough to step into the deeper mysteries of the faith. Journeying south—whether by the subterranean Deeprun Tram or across the mountain passes—brings initiates to Stormwind's Cathedral District, where Duthorian Rall prepares them to study the sacred Tomes and master the rites of redemption.

quest:369.text: A New Plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan turns his attention toward developing a potent new biological agent for the Forsaken. By studying ancient texts, he discovers that a historic, deadly plague survived through the venom of eastern Tirisfal's night web spiders, prompting an urgent retrieval effort. While pursuing his alchemy for the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill, Apothecary Johaan scours aged tomes in search of deadlier mixtures. He uncovers records of an ancient pestilence that once ravaged thousands of lives. Crucially, the texts indicate that the deadly pathogen survived across generations by harboring within the local arachnids of Tirisfal Glades, making their venom an invaluable biological reagent. To acquire a viable sample of the pathogen, Johaan directs agents toward the eastern reaches of Tirisfal Glades. South of the Scarlet Monastery lies Venomweb Vale, a fog-shrouded hollow infested with vicious night web spiders. Harvesters must venture into their dens to extract fresh venom glands, securing the final ingredient needed to finalize Johaan's experimental brew.

quest:37.text: Find the Lost Guards. Guard Thomas is waiting at Elwynn's eastern bridge for word of two missing guards. Rolf and Malakai were sent north along the river to watch for murlocs, but neither has returned. Guard Thomas watches the eastern crossing of Elwynn Forest, where the King's road approaches Redridge. Murlocs have made the nearby waters more dangerous. Days ago, Thomas sent two Stormwind guards, Rolf and Malakai, north along the riverbanks to scout the threat and clear out nests. Neither has returned, and Thomas fears violence stopped their patrol.

quest:370.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Executor Zygand directs Forsaken champions to strike down Captain Perrine and his garrison stationed at a ruined tower southwest of Brill. Using intelligence recovered in Deathknell, the Forsaken aim to push back the zealous crusaders threatening their borders. Documents recovered from the Scarlet Crusade in Deathknell by Executor Arren revealed active troop movements across Tirisfal Glades. Rather than waiting for the fanatics to mount an offensive against the newly fortified town of Brill, Executor Zygand uses this captured intelligence to orchestrate preemptive strikes against their field commanders. Stationed at a dilapidated watchtower southwest of Brill, Captain Perrine oversees a contingent of Scarlet Zealots and Missionaries. From this vantage, the Crusade attempts to monitor Forsaken movements and project power deeper into Tirisfal, making Perrine's death crucial to the defense of the Dark Lady's young kingdom.

quest:371.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. This military operation tasks Forsaken defenders with striking at the Scarlet Crusade encampment near the Balnir Farmstead in southeastern Tirisfal Glades. Under orders from Executor Zygand, players eliminate Captain Vachon and his accompanying friars to stall Crusader raids threatening the Dark Lady's domain. As the Forsaken strive to secure the perimeter around Brill and the Undercity, the Scarlet Crusade maintains fortified pockets across the countryside. Reports funneling into town from Executor Arren alert the military command to active Crusader incursions operating out of a crumbling guard tower in southeastern Tirisfal Glades, uncomfortably close to the abandoned Balnir Farmstead. Recognizing that disorganized zealots are far less perilous than coordinated squads, Executor Zygand focuses the offensive on their field leadership. By eliminating Captain Vachon alongside the Scarlet Friars who bolster his men with holy magic, the Forsaken aim to shatter this cell's operational cohesion and suppress human raids into nearby Forsaken territories.

quest:372.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. This mission represents the culmination of Executor Zygand's early campaign to secure Tirisfal Glades against Scarlet Crusade incursions. Operating out of Brill, Forsaken agents are directed to strike directly at Captain Melrache and his personal vanguard at a ruined watchtower past Faol's Rest. While the Forsaken consolidate their hold over the ruins of Lordaeron, the Scarlet Crusade relentlessly probes the borders of Tirisfal. From an elevated watchtower situated in northern Tirisfal past Faol's Rest, zealous crusaders have organized raiding parties against Forsaken patrols and territory. Rather than waiting to repel another assault, Executor Zygand chooses decapitation: eliminating the command structure that directs the local raids. Commanding this northern encampment is Captain Melrache, an uncompromising officer flanked constantly by two sworn bodyguards. Melrache's position gives the Crusade observation over the coastal roads and surrounding woods. Slaying him breaks the immediate coordination of the crusaders near Brill, neutralizing a direct threat to Lady Sylvanas's fledgling kingdom and driving the zealots back toward their stronger fortifications further east.

quest:374.text: Proof of Demise. Proof of Demise is a military directive issued by Deathguard Burgess in Brill to thin the ranks of the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Initiated on the orders of Varimathras, Sylvanas Windrunner's dreadlord lieutenant, it tests a soldier's loyalty to the Forsaken cause. Recruits are ordered to strip signet rings from fallen crusaders as tangible evidence of their slaughter. The campaign across northern Tirisfal Glades is not merely defensive; it is a coordinated war of eradication. Varimathras, the dreadlord who surrendered and pledged his blade to Sylvanas Windrunner, oversees many of the Forsaken's aggressive military maneuvers against the living. His directives trickle down to commanders like Executor Zygand and frontline officers such as Deathguard Burgess. Burgess makes the directive clear: the human race is viewed as vermin to be purged from Lordaeron, and the zealous crusaders nearby are the immediate target. Words alone do not satisfy the commanders in Brill. To prove obedience to the Dark Lady and her lieutenant, soldiers must plunder Scarlet Insignia Rings straight from the fingers of slain zealots. These rings bear the iconography of the Scarlet Crusade, marking their bearers as sworn enemies of the Forsaken. Returning with a handful of these trophies serves as unassailable proof of dead crusaders and a demonstration of uncompromising allegiance.

quest:375.text: The Chill of Death. In the town of Brill, a Forsaken tailor named Gretchen Dedmar struggles against the creeping cold of mortality and decay. Fearing that the encroaching mindless state will rob her of the ability to serve Lady Sylvanas, she asks for simple materials to sew herself a warm blanket. For the Forsaken, undeath is not a static condition of eternal preservation. As Gretchen Dedmar describes, the lingering Plague of Undeath runs through her body like an icy serpent, draining the warmth from her limbs and threatening to pull her into the mindless state that afflicts so many wandering corpses in Tirisfal Glades. Her shivering hands make ordinary work nearly impossible. Despite her failing strength, Gretchen refuses to abandon her duty to the Forsaken kingdom. When Sylvanas Windrunner first rallied the liberated dead, Gretchen contributed by sewing burial shrouds and body bags for fallen soldiers. By gathering sturdy duskbat pelts and coarse thread, travelers help keep her hands steady enough to craft a blanket and prolong her useful service to the Forsaken cause.

quest:376.text: The Damned. The Damned is an early task given to newly awakened Forsaken by Novice Elreth in the chapel of Deathknell. In exchange for the materials needed to fashion crude clothing and battlefield wraps, Elreth provides salvageable armor to protect fledgling undead from the perils surrounding the cemetery. Awakening into undeath leaves little room for vanity or sentimentality. Novice Elreth attends to the steady stream of fresh Forsaken pulled from the dirt of Deathknell, serving as an assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis. Between tending to battered soldiers and mending garments, supplies run perilously thin. To ensure new arrivals do not fall apart during their initial trials, Elreth sends them into the surrounding glades to hunt native duskbats and scavenger wolves, trading salvaged armor for the raw pelts, wings, and sinew required to keep the camp functioning.
