The armor offered by Elreth is far from pristine forge-work; it is hand-me-down gear pulled from those who failed to endure their awakening. Her grim parting words—hoping the garments serve the recipient better than the previous owner—reflect the cold calculus of Forsaken survival. In Tirisfal Glades, nothing is wasted, and every piece of leather and rusted chain has already outlived at least one corpse.

quest:38.text: Westfall Stew. Salma Saldean cooks Westfall Stew on her farm, making a meal from what the frontier offers. Its ingredients reflect how Westfall homesteaders endure bandits, famine, and dangerous beasts. Westfall's settlers contend with bandits, famine, and rampaging beasts, far from Stormwind's lavish larders. Families like the Saldeans make do with what the land provides. Salma Saldean turns ingredients many city folk might call pests or scraps into a sustaining meal for working farmhands. Salma's recipe brings together local okra, stringy meat from circling vultures, and snouts from wild goretusks roaming the plains. It also calls for fresh murloc eyes gathered from coastal raiders. The thought of river beasts and carrion birds may turn delicate stomachs in Elwynn, but Westfall cooks swear the blend makes a rich, fortifying meal.

quest:380.text: Night Web's Hollow. Night Web's Hollow is an early assignment from Executor Arren to clear out the spiders infesting a nearby gold mine northwest of Deathknell. Facing critical shortages of raw materials, the fledgling Forsaken need the mine's wealth to sustain their settlement and war effort. Newly risen recruits are sent into the tangled cavern to cull the arachnid infestation piece by piece. Survival for the newly risen Forsaken involves more than just defending against the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders. Building a fledgling society requires raw resources, and precious metals like gold were scarce in northern Lordaeron even at the height of the Alliance's strength. Executor Arren, overseeing operations in Deathknell, recognizes that the Forsaken cannot hope to arm, equip, and establish themselves without secured wealth. Directly northwest of the cemetery grounds lies Night Web's Hollow, a natural cavern containing a viable gold vein. Unfortunately, monstrous arachnids have overrun the tunnels, filling the depths with thick webbing and deadly venom. Lacking the seasoned troops to conduct a full-scale purge, Arren relies on fresh recruits to whittle down the young and adult spiders until mining crews can eventually burn away the webs and extract the ore.

quest:381.text: The Scarlet Crusade. This early mission from Executor Arren tasks newly awakened Forsaken with ambushing a nearby camp of Scarlet Crusade zealots southeast of Deathknell. It serves as a grim introduction to one of the Forsaken's most fanatical and persistent enemies. Once the immediate peril of the Night Web spider infestation is handled, Executor Arren turns Deathknell's attention toward an encroaching threat. A detachment of the Scarlet Crusade has established a foothold just southeast of the settlement. These zealots refuse to acknowledge any distinction between mindless Scourge minions and free-willed Forsaken, meaning their presence on the border poses an existential threat to the newly risen dead. Understanding that dialogue is impossible with holy fanatics who view all dead flesh as an abomination, Arren orders a preemptive strike. Adventurers are sent to cut down Scarlet Initiates and Converts before the encampment can grow into an organized forward assault on Deathknell. The trophies brought back—their crimson armbands—stand as stark proof that survival in Tirisfal must be claimed by force.

quest:382.text: The Red Messenger. Executor Arren tasks newly risen Forsaken with intercepting a courier dispatched from the Scarlet Monastery to the crusade camp outside Deathknell. Intercepting the messenger secures critical intelligence on local Scarlet movements before the zealots can solidify their presence in the valley. This mission marks one of the earliest offensive operations undertaken to secure the Forsaken's fledgling sanctuary. Word travels quickly through Tirisfal Glades, even among the dead. Superiors in Brill alerted Executor Arren that the Scarlet Crusade sent an emissary from their stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery westward into Deathknell. While the Crusaders maintain an aggressive presence across Lordaeron, dispatching a courier directly to the edge of the Forsaken's waking grounds indicates an organized push to eradicate newly risen undead before they can muster an organized defense. The courier, Meven Korgal, blended into the small Scarlet encampment east of Deathknell without bearing distinctive heraldry. Executor Arren directed a targeted strike to assassinate Korgal and confiscate his dispatch. Stripping the courier of his missives denies the local zealots further tactical coordination with their eastern headquarters.

quest:383.text: Vital Intelligence. Vital Intelligence marks the end of a freshly risen Forsaken's training in Deathknell. Entrusted with intercepted Scarlet Crusade documents, the courier is sent out into Tirisfal Glades to report to Executor Zygand in Brill. Having neutralized local threats and intercepted a courier of the Scarlet Crusade, newly recruited Forsaken are deemed ready for broader service. Executor Arren entrusts the recovered intelligence to the player, directing them out through the sheltered canyon of Deathknell and east along the road toward Brill, past Cold Hearth Manor.

quest:3861.text: CLUCK!. In Westfall, a chicken may answer when you call and feed it. Follow its scratched message to the Saldean family, and a warm egg may be yours to hatch. Ordinary chickens wander the farmsteads of Azeroth, and most travelers pass them by. Mimic a chicken's gestures and clucking, and it may stop pecking to regard you with interest. In that brief moment, the bird scratches letters in the dirt. The message points to the farmer who can provide the food it wants. The bird's request calls for Special Chicken Feed. In Westfall, the Saldean family keeps this grain for their flock. Offer the feed and cheer the chicken on as it eats. In return, it lays a warm egg that can be nurtured into a feathered companion.

quest:39.text: Deliver Thomas' Report. In eastern Elwynn, Guard Thomas sends word of two dead guards and rising danger. He asks you to carry the report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, where the garrison has few hands to spare. Guard Thomas watches the bridges into eastern Elwynn, where river traffic meets the wilderness. Guards Malakai and Rolf have been killed by aggressive murloc tribes. With his remaining guards too few to contain them, Thomas sends you down the road to Goldshire with an urgent report. Marshal Dughan receives Thomas' report in Goldshire, already struggling to keep patrols on the roads. Kobolds infest the area, Defias bandits threaten travelers, and Stormwind City has sent no reinforcements. The deaths of two experienced guards add to his burden. Murlocs may soon threaten Goldshire itself, while the defenses across the region grow ever thinner.

quest:3901.text: Rattling the Rattlecages. Rattling the Rattlecages is an early trial assigned by Shadow Priest Sarvis to newly awakened Forsaken in Deathknell. Tasked with destroying twelve Rattlecage Skeletons, fresh undead prove their resilience against the Scourge and demonstrate that they possess the willpower to defend their newly won freedom. Having culled the mindless zombies stumbling through Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken are immediately pushed into a harsher trial. Shadow Priest Sarvis directs recruits to confront the Rattlecage Skeletons roaming the outskirts of the settlement. These animated bones lack any trace of sapience or self-control, yet they hit harder and fight with greater ferocity than the decaying corpses nearby. Surviving their clattering ambushes demonstrates that a new recruit will not falter when placed under immediate pressure. To Sarvis and the leadership in Deathknell, culling the skeletons serves a dual purpose. It protects the fragile refuge from being overrun by the lingering grip of the Lich King while weeding out those recruits who cannot cut it. Those who fail or hesitate risk meeting the same fate as the mindless wretches wandering the woods. Overcoming the Rattlecages proves to Sarvis that the recruit possesses the mettle required to navigate a world that despises their very existence.

quest:3902.text: Scavenging Deathknell. Scavenging Deathknell is an early logistical task assigned to newly awakened Forsaken by Deathguard Saltain in Deathknell. As freshly raised undead claw their way from the soil, the Forsaken must scavenge abandoned boxes and crates throughout the blighted settlement to equip incoming recruits. It illustrates the raw scarcity facing Sylvanas's nascent people, who must reclaim discarded goods simply to survive. Newly raised Forsaken awaken into a grim reality of decay and deprivation. Unlike established nations with bustling supply lines and armories, the free undead in Deathknell possess next to nothing. Deathguard Saltain's blunt demand reflects the ruthless practicality required to build an army from the graveyard dirt: every piece of salvageable cloth, leather, and iron must be hauled back to clothe and arm those still crawling out of their plots. The settlement of Deathknell is littered with remnants of its former human inhabitants alongside supplies abandoned during the kingdom's fall to the Scourge. Rather than letting usable materials rot away in crates across town, the Deathguards press newborn undead into service as salvagers. As Saltain makes clear, the Forsaken expect no charity from the living world and must rely entirely on their own industriousness to stand on their feet.

quest:3903.text: Milly Osworth. At Northshire Abbey, Deputy Willem sends you to help Milly Osworth. Her wagon and livelihood are in jeopardy, and she needs help across the abbey grounds. The work takes you from defending the abbey to aiding Elwynn Forest's civilians. After you prove your mettle against the Defias thieves encroaching on Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem recognizes you as capable and willing to help. He sends you to assist his friend Milly Osworth. This favor is personal, outside the abbey's official guard duties, and Milly is a civilian caught in the valley's growing unrest. Milly waits beside her wagon on the far side of Northshire Abbey, near the stables. Deputy Willem must stay at his post to defend the abbey. Milly's troubles lie out in the valley, where the stretched guard garrison has too few hands to help her.

quest:3904.text: Milly's Harvest. Defias brigands have driven Milly Osworth from the Northshire vineyards. Her harvest lies scattered in buckets and crates among the occupied rows, where it may be stolen or crushed. Milly Osworth fled the southeastern fields of Northshire Valley when Defias brigands swarmed the vines. She left her gathered grapes behind in buckets and crates among the occupied rows. Northshire's garrison is stretched thin, and Milly fears that boots and fighting will crush any fruit the bandits leave behind. Defias bandits now occupy working vineyards, a sign of how little safety Northshire can offer. Stormwind's attention is elsewhere, and the valley has too few guards. Farmers like Milly must depend on recruits and wanderers to protect their property and secure the food and wine that supply the abbey.

quest:3905.text: Grape Manifest. Milly Osworth records her rescued grape harvest for Northshire Abbey. She writes a manifest of the yield recovered from Defias thieves, then sends it to Brother Neals so the brotherhood can replenish its wine stores. Northshire Valley's soil and orchards have long supported local food and the abbey's wine. When thieves and bandits seized the eastern fields, they cut off the abbey's supply of grapes and food. With the harvest recovered from the occupied fields, Milly Osworth records the yield in a manifest. Brother Neals oversees food and drink at Northshire Abbey. He is known for sampling Northshire's vintages in the quiet of the bell tower. Brigands still threaten the gates, but fresh grapes give the brotherhood a moment to toast the Light and take heart.

quest:3921.text: Wenikee Boltbucket. Near the Mor'shan Rampart, Wenikee Boltbucket may be able to mend a broken samophlange. Sputtervalve tinkered with the device after it was retrieved from the Sludge Fen, and now needs an expert hand before his colleagues in Undermine demand results. Sputtervalve's claims to his fellow engineers in Undermine now hang on a broken machine. An adventurer retrieved the mysterious samophlange from the Venture Company's control console at the Sludge Fen, and Sputtervalve could not resist showing it off. His tinkering damaged the delicate contraption. He needs someone with sharper skill to diagnose the damage and repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket camps beside the road just south of the Mor'shan Rampart. The rampart divides the northern Barrens from Ashenvale. Her inquisitive mind is drawn to intricate machinery, and the broken samophlange quickly captures her attention. Its internal gears hold her curiosity, and she sets to work figuring out how to rebuild it.

quest:3922.text: Nugget Slugs. At the Sludge Fen, Wenikee Boltbucket needs parts for a recovered samophlange. The eccentric tinkerer sends you to the nearby Venture Company drilling crews for spare hardware. Wenikee Boltbucket has a recovered samophlange and wants to learn how the intricate machine works. Its goblin mechanisms need exact parts, so she sends you to the Venture Company crews at the Sludge Fen. Their heavy tool buckets hold the seventeen-point-five gauge nugget slugs she needs.

quest:3923.text: Rilli Greasygob. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob is the specialist Wenikee Boltbucket seeks. She sends you there with a damaged samophlange, hoping his knowledge of its Venture Company origins can explain the device. Wenikee Boltbucket examined the samophlange recovered from the Venture Company drilling site in the Barrens. Her extra gauges showed the apparatus nearing collapse. More levers and dials might destroy it, so she stopped and sent the problem to someone with knowledge of its design. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Wenikee sends you to Nogg's Machine Shop. Rilli Greasygob works there as an engineer and once learned his trade within the Venture Company. He recognizes the machine at once and marvels that anyone survived exploring the company's contested operations in the Barrens.

quest:3924.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob needs help with a broken samophlange. The goblin engineer sends you back into the Barrens for the operating instructions, held by his former Venture Company rival. Rilli Greasygob once worked beside Boss Copperplug in the Venture Company. Copperplug oversaw the samophlange’s inner workings and guarded their secrets closely. He shared no manual with Rilli. Instead, he gave out separate pages only to underlings he trusted, leaving his fellow engineer without the knowledge to understand the device.

quest:398.text: Wanted: Maggot Eye. Wanted: Maggot Eye is an official death bounty posted on the Brill notice board by the town's Forsaken leadership. A notorious gnoll has been looting nearby graveyards and farms to supply dead bodies directly to the Lich King's Scourge. Executor Zygand requires proof of the creature's execution to secure the lands around Garren's Haunt. In Tirisfal Glades, the dead are far from resting peacefully. The gnoll known as Maggot Eye earned a severe death sentence not merely for scavenging, but for active collaboration with the Lich King. While gnolls are generally viewed as savage brutes driven by simple hunger, Maggot Eye has been systematically digging up corpses and collecting remains to fuel the ranks of the Scourge army. For the Forsaken, whose entire existence hinges on breaking free from the Lich King's dominion, feeding dead kin back into the Scourge war machine is among the highest offenses possible. Executor Zygand, overseeing local military enforcement in Brill, commissioned this bounty to put an end to the grave robberies near Garren's Haunt. To collect the prize, the executioner must sever Maggot Eye's paw as unmistakable proof that the beast will trouble Tirisfal no longer.

quest:399.text: Humble Beginnings. Baros Alexston seeks help from his home in Stormwind's Cathedral Square. His family's Westfall farm has burned, and thieves hold its ruins; he hopes to recover an heirloom from his youth. Baros Alexston grew up working the fields of Westfall. Now he is an accomplished architect in Stormwind City, advising on stonework and city buildings. His path from farm boy to city planner is rare in the kingdom, yet he remains attached to the modest beginnings that shaped him. Lawlessness swept across Westfall, and the Alexston Farmstead fell to it. Bandits and vagrants burned the house, forcing Baros's father from his livelihood. Family heirlooms were left behind amid the fire and occupation. Baros asks you to search the ruined, bandit-held farmstead west of Sentinel Hill for his first compass, hidden before the home fell.

quest:40.text: A Fishy Peril. In Goldshire, A Fishy Peril begins with reports of murlocs moving inland through the waterways. Remy "Two Times" asks travelers to alert Marshal Dughan, whose guards are already stretched thin. Remy "Two Times" grows uneasy over a new threat while seeking business in Goldshire. Murlocs are creeping up the streams and into inland shallows, disrupting fishing and menacing innocent travelers. Remy fears the local guard is overlooking a danger that is still growing, so he asks passersby to carry word to the heart of the township. Marshal Dughan hears the report in Goldshire but remains skeptical. He is charged with protecting the realm while royal forces are stretched thin elsewhere, and Riverpaw gnolls and Defias highwaymen already demand his attention. With no confirmed military intelligence, he will not divert his scarce men to pursue rumors of fish-men in the eastern streams.

quest:400.text: Tools for Steelgrill. Tools for Steelgrill is an early Alliance delivery errand that introduces travelers leaving Kharanos to the nearby mechanic workshop at Steelgrill's Depot. Tharek Blackstone sends you up the road with a fresh crate of heavy equipment for Beldin Steelgrill, the master siege engine tech who works through spanners and ratchets faster than town suppliers can keep up. Beldin Steelgrill carries an undisputed reputation across Dun Morogh as the sharpest siege engine mechanic in the mountains, but his violent work ethic takes a heavy toll on his workshop. According to Tharek Blackstone in Kharanos, Steelgrill cracks arclight spanners and snaps tools almost as fast as local supply crates can arrive. When a fresh batch of durable gear is assembled in Kharanos, anyone heading northeast is quickly recruited to lug the heavy parcel out to the depot. Arriving at Steelgrill's Depot, travelers find the yard crowded with smoke, grease, and idling iron war machines. Beldin's backlog is thick with demanding military repairs, including critical work on Pilot Stonegear's siege engine. Beldin had snapped his last fang-ratchet mere hours before your arrival, making the delivered crate an immediate lifeline for Ironforge's tracked armor fleet.

quest:403.text: Guarded Thunderbrew Barrel. The Guarded Thunderbrew Barrel rests in the cellar of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. It represents the prized stock of the famed dwarven brewing family, watched over day and night to keep thieves and rivals from meddling with their craft. In the cold snows of Dun Morogh, few things are guarded more fiercely than good ale. Beneath the floorboards of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, stout casks of potent brew age in peace. The family takes no chances with their stock, posting watchful sentries like Jarven Thunderbrew right beside the barrels to ensure not a single drop is tampered with or siphoned off. Dwarven brewing is as serious a discipline as smithing or mining. The Thunderbrews take immense pride in their proprietary recipes, particularly potent batches of Thunder Ale. Between greedy troggs creeping around Dun Morogh and bitter brewing rivalries across the Alliance, Jarven's vigilant presence ensures the family's liquid gold remains untouched until properly tapped.

quest:404.text: A Putrid Task. A Putrid Task is an early military assignment offered by Deathguard Dillinger in Brill. It directs adventurers to push back the mindlessly aggressive Scourge encroaching upon the old bridge west of the settlement. Collecting proof of the monsters' destruction secures the road and eases pressure on Tirisfal's defenders. Brill sits at a critical crossroads in eastern Tirisfal Glades, making any enemy approach a direct threat to the Forsaken power base. Mindless Scourge constantly seep westward across the waterways, clustering around the broken remnants of the old stone bridge. Without regular patrols beating them back, the shambling corpses would quickly choke transit between Brill and the western farmsteads. For the Forsaken, Scourge roaming their borders is not merely a strategic nuisance; it is an insult. Every mindless ghoul and rotting corpse represents the servitude and torment that Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's followers broke away from. Deathguards like Dillinger take grim satisfaction in crushing their former captors, demanding severed claws as brutal proof that the mindless dead have been put to rest for good.

quest:405.text: The Prodigal Lich. Following your service in Brill against Scourge remnants and rot hide gnolls, Magistrate Sevren directs you south to the Undercity. Bethor Iceshard, a prominent archmage in the Magic Quarter, requires a capable operative for a sensitive mission regarding a wayward lich. Having proven your capability in the ruined town of Brill, Magistrate Sevren deems you worthy of higher-level Forsaken endeavors. Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage dwelling in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, has demanded an agent tested in combat against the Scourge. Sevren hands over official orders, dispatching you beneath the ruins of Lordaeron into the subterranean corridors of the Forsaken capital. While Sevren admits ignorance of the exact specifics, he reveals that the task revolves around finding and recruiting a rogue lich. Liches are among the most lethal spellcasters raised by the Scourge, making any interaction fraught with peril. When you deliver the orders to Bethor atop his arcane sanctum, the icy mage cuts straight to business, eager to assess whether Brill's magistrate has sent someone strong enough to handle such dangerous quarry.

quest:407.text: Fields of Grief. Fields of Grief concludes Apothecary Johaan's experiment to weaponize ordinary pumpkins gathered from Solliden Farmstead. Having infused the crop with his latest alchemical concotion, Johaan dispatches you to feed the laced vegetable to a captive Scarlet Crusader languishing in Brill. Apothecary Johaan of the Royal Apothecary Society believes the Forsaken must exploit every tactical advantage to fend off the Scourge from the north and human incursions from the south. Rather than relying solely on raw blade-work or dark sorcery, the Society seeks to harness ordinary staples of the land. By tainting the pumpkins recovered from the mortal farmers of Solliden Farmstead, Johaan intends to prove that even common produce can be transformed into an instrument of death on behalf of the Dark Lady.

quest:408.text: The Family Crypt. The Family Crypt is a Horde quest tasking players with confronting the Scourge inside the Agamand Family Crypt. Commanded by Magistrate Sevren in Brill, adventurers must destroy the raised Agamand ancestors and slay the skeletal Scourge commander, Captain Dargol. While the Forsaken have carved out a fragile dominion in Tirisfal Glades, remnants of the Lich King's Scourge remain deeply entrenched in the countryside. The Agamand Mills, once a prosperous flour-producing heartland of Lordaeron, have become a dangerous Scourge stronghold. Magistrate Sevren in Brill watches this military buildup with grave concern, knowing that every inch yielded to mindless undead undermines the Forsaken's independence. The center of the local Scourge occupation is the Agamand Family Crypt, where the skeletal commander Captain Dargol has set up headquarters. Using dark necromancy, Dargol has dragged generations of Agamand family dead from their rest, twisting them into Rotting and Wailing Ancestors to swell his ranks. Sevren dispatches Forsaken agents to purge the crypt, lay the disturbed dead back to rest, and severed Dargol's head to shatter Scourge coordination in northern Tirisfal.

quest:409.text: Proving Allegiance. Proving Allegiance is the crucial trial presented by Gunther Arcanus to determine whether you truly serve the free-willed Forsaken or the Lich King. To earn the solitary necromancer's trust, you are sent to summon and destroy Lillith Nefara, a dangerous Scourge operative lurking near his island. Gunther Arcanus has isolated himself on an island in Brightwater Lake since rising into undeath, fiercely clinging to his autonomy. Though Bethor Iceshard's magical enchantments on Gunther's spellbook confirmed the emissary does not carry the foul taint of the Scourge, words and charms are not enough for the paranoid hermit. To earn his confidence, an outsider must demonstrate active hostility toward the minions of the Lich King through decisive violence.

quest:410.text: The Dormant Shade. The Dormant Shade is a dark ritual performed at Gunther's Retreat on Brightwater Lake in Tirisfal Glades. By placing a mystic candle upon an old, blood-soaked table, a traveler summons forth the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara, whose defeat proves to Gunther Arcanus that the visitor is the Lich King's foe. On the island of Gunther's Retreat in Brightwater Lake rests a battered, bloody dinner table. Far from an ordinary piece of neglected domestic furniture, it serves as the physical focus for a sinister conjuration. Stained with dried gore and abandoned to the shadows, the table acts as a makeshift ritual slab where death and dark magic linger.

quest:411.text: The Prodigal Lich Returns. The Prodigal Lich Returns marks the conclusion of the effort to recruit Gunther Arcanus into the Forsaken. Having proven your intentions and restored his grimoire, you carry an arcane communion gem back to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Gunther Arcanus spent years isolated on an island in Brightwater Lake, having broken free from the Lich King's grip through sheer force of will, completely unaware that Sylvanas Windrunner had liberated Lordaeron. Bitter and suspicious of outsiders, Gunther distrusted the emissaries of the Undercity until an adventurer returned his spellbook and proved their hostility toward the Scourge. Satisfied that his visitor was not an enemy, Gunther entrusted them with a Nether Gem to establish contact with his former colleague.

quest:412.text: Operation Recombobulation. Operation Recombobulation is a bold engineering effort orchestrated by Razzle Sprysprocket in Kharanos. In response to the tragedy of Gnomeregan, Razzle and Ozzie Togglevolt seek to reverse the horrific transformation of their afflicted kin into leper gnomes using an experimental contraption known as the Recombobulator. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan to purge the trogg menace, it failed to destroy the invaders and instead warped the majority of the gnomish population into deranged, sickly leper gnomes. Refusing to accept this tragic mutation as permanent, inventor Razzle Sprysprocket has partnered with Ozzie Togglevolt to develop a technological cure: the Recombobulator. Their audacious goal is nothing less than restoring their mutated brethren back to health and sanity. Building a delicate prototype requires precise components, namely Restabilization Cogs and Gyromechanic Gears. In an ironic twist of fate, these essential parts are salvaged directly from the hostile leper gnomes wandering outside the sealed gates of Gnomeregan. By harvesting mechanical debris from their corrupted brothers and sisters, Razzle hopes to assemble the very device that will undo their shared tragedy.

quest:413.text: Shimmer Stout. Following the creation of his experimental Shimmer Stout in Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew asks travelers to carry a fresh barrel out to his brother Wellart. Wellart serves as a dwarf Mountaineer stationed at the southern guard tower guarding the pass toward Loch Modan, where a cold post makes a strong drink all the more welcome. Rejold Barleybrew has perfected his new creation, Shimmer Stout, using shimmering fronds gathered from the icy crags of Dun Morogh. While the rest of the Barleybrew family dedicates their craft to the vats and kegs of Brewnall Village, Rejold's brother Wellart chose the life of a Mountaineer. Knowing the lonely conditions of guard duty on the frontier, Rejold sends a fresh barrel along with passing travelers as both a brotherly favor and a true taste test. Wellart Barleybrew is stationed at the southern guard tower flanking the South Gate Pass into Loch Modan. High atop the mountain pass, the Mountaineers endure bitter winds and occasional beast attacks while keeping watch over travelers walking the mountain road. Running low on drink and restless for excitement, Wellart finds that Shimmer Stout delivers quite a punch—so much so that it seems to brighten his vision in the dim mountain night.

quest:414.text: Stout to Kadrell. Stout to Kadrell is an Alliance delivery quest that leads travelers out of the frozen heights of Dun Morogh and into the temperate valley of Loch Modan. Entrusted with a cask of Rejold Barleybrew's newly perfected Shimmer Stout, you carry the potent brew across the territorial border to share with Mountaineer Kadrell on patrol in Thelsamar. After tasting the newly finished Shimmer Stout created by his brother Rejold, Mountaineer Barleybrew is convinced it is too good to keep entirely within Dun Morogh. Stationed at the eastern border post guarding the mountain passes, Barleybrew looks out toward his kin guarding neighboring lands. Dwarven mountaineering can be a cold, grueling assignment, and a stout heart calls for stout drink. Wanting an honest appraisal from a fellow patrolman on the line, Barleybrew sends a cask eastward with passing travelers bound for Loch Modan. The journey marks a natural rite of passage for young dwarven and gnomish adventurers who have spent their early days among the snowbound crags of Dun Morogh. Passing southeast through the South Gate Outpost and traversing the long tunnels cut through the mountain bedrock, travelers suddenly emerge into the warmer, wooded basin of Loch Modan. Patrolling along the road through the settlement of Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell gladly takes a break from his vigil to tap the cask, discovering that Barleybrew's new recipe has an astonishing kick.

quest:415.text: Rejold's New Brew. Rejold's New Brew is an Alliance errand in Dun Morogh summoning an adventurer back to Brewnall Village. Having perfected a new concoction using gathered Shimmerweed, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew wants a trusted friend to sample his latest recipe. It serves as the bridge between gathering brewing supplies and distributing his prized Shimmer Stout across the mountain realm. Word spreads quickly through Dun Morogh when a dwarven brewer strikes gold in his cellar. After securing Shimmerweed from the bitter slopes, local contacts like Tharek Blackstone or Pilot Bellowfiz urge passing adventurers to report back to Brewnall Village. Rejold Barleybrew has finished fermenting his experimental batches and is eager to share the spoils with the traveler who made it possible. Brewnall Village thrives on distinct ale craft, and Barleybrew's newest batch is no ordinary draught. Infusing local herbs into his mash produced a distinct beverage known as Shimmer Stout. Before shipping barrels off to neighboring outposts and thirsty patrons in Loch Modan, Rejold insists that the adventurer who risked life and limb for the herbs gets the honor of the inaugural sip.

quest:4161.text: Recipe of the Kaldorei. Zarrin teaches a lesson in balance through the Recipe of the Kaldorei. In Dolanaar, young cooks learn to gather only what they need from Teldrassil's woods. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and teaches young adventurers the traditions of his people. The night elves once called themselves the kaldorei, or children of the stars. Zarrin begins their understanding of that heritage with the bond between a hunter, their food, and Teldrassil's boughs, rather than the battlefield. Zarrin teaches restraint through a simple demand: gather small spider legs from the woodland arachnids outside Shadowglen, but take exactly seven. The kaldorei seek harmony with nature by taking only what they need and showing kindness to the wild. Even in troubled times, that balance matters. A spider kabob becomes a lesson in living with care.

quest:417.text: A Pilot's Revenge. Following the trail of a missing dwarven siege engine pilot leads to a frozen corpse in the wilds of Dun Morogh. Found among the remains, Hildelve's personal journal details his fatal struggle against a notorious predator known as Mangeclaw, leaving behind a dying wish for vengeance. Pilot Hildelve did not survive his time stranded in the rugged snowy crags. When travelers locate his remains, they discover his journal resting beside him. In his last penned words, Hildelve recorded a savage encounter with a massive Ice Claw bear he named Mangeclaw. Though he managed to fend off the monstrosity initially, the injuries proved severe, and the beast eventually returned to finish off the weakened pilot. Knowing his end was near, Hildelve wrote down one final plea in his journal: retribution against the monster that took his life. Returning to Pilot Hammerfoot with the journal and a claw torn from the fallen beast brings grim closure to the Ironforge Siege Brigade, honoring their lost comrade and removing a deadly menace from the mountain paths.

quest:418.text: Thelsamar Blood Sausages. In the bustling town of Thelsamar, cook Vidra Hearthstove keeps the local laborers and miners fed with a famous highland staple: blood sausages. Preparing this hearty dwarven fare requires freshly gathered ingredients from the surrounding valley of Loch Modan. Thelsamar is never short on hungry appetites. Between energetic children and weary miners returning from the Ironband Excavation, Vidra Hearthstove works tirelessly over the tavern stove. To keep the populace fed and satisfied, she relies on a local culinary tradition known across Loch Modan: savory blood sausages made from the wildlife wandering the rugged mountain pass. While traditional blood sausage relies on fresh blood, seasoned meat, and natural casings, Vidra's recipe reflects the rugged pragmatism of the dwarves. Boar intestines provide the casings, bear meat forms the dense filling, and spider ichor is added to lend a sharp, pungent bite. Though collecting venomous fluid and entrails is not for the faint of heart, the result is a regional favorite that travelers quickly learn to appreciate.

quest:419.text: The Lost Pilot. Pilot Hammerfoot fears the worst for his comrade, Mori Hildelve, who ventured into the craggy hills of Dun Morogh on foot after wrecking his siege engine. Hildelve was searching for a rare ore vital for potent blastpowder, but days have passed amidst unsettling roars echoing through the peaks. Dwarven siege engines are formidable war machines, but even iron treads struggle against the treacherous, jagged ridges of Dun Morogh. While scouring the slopes for a rare mineral deposit required to produce high-grade blastpowder, Pilot Mori Hildelve pushed his engine too far up a steep hill and busted the machine. Undeterred by the breakdown, Hildelve ordered his companion, Pilot Hammerfoot, to stay behind and guard the broken machinery while he pressed higher into the frozen wilderness on foot. Days went by with no sign of Hildelve returning to camp. In the dead of night, strange and vicious beastly growls began echoing down from the rocky crags, turning Hammerfoot's mild impatience into creeping dread. Though Hildelve had a reputation for being as tough as nails, surviving the frigid heights of Dun Morogh without mechanized armor or heavy support against prowling predators is a dangerous gamble.

quest:420.text: Senir's Observations. This errand completes a scouting line out of Coldridge Valley, carrying Grelin Whitebeard's completed report through the trogg-infested pass to his brother Senir in Kharanos. It bridges the secluded training grounds of Anvilmar with the broader troubles facing Dun Morogh. Through Senir's candid reception, travelers catch their first glimpse of political friction simmering between field scouts and the Ironforge Senate. After Grelin Whitebeard recovers his stolen journal from the Frostmane trolls, he prepares a detailed report of the valley's threats for his brother Senir. Mountaineer Thalos, stationed guarding the gate out of Coldridge Valley, entrusts passing adventurers with carrying this dispatch. Leaving the relative seclusion of the introductory vale means braving the tunnel cut through the mountain, which has recently been overrun by violent troggs ambushing all traffic. Travelers who punch through emerge onto the snowblown highways of central Dun Morogh, following the main road straight into the cozy hub of Kharanos. Senir Whitebeard, found seeking warmth over drinks at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, greets newcomers with rough mountaineer hospitality. Reading through Grelin's findings, Senir chuckles over his brother's aggressive rhetoric. Grelin liberally invokes the name of King Magni Bronzebeard to press for urgent action, an assertive tactic Senir notes is bound to agitate the stubborn Ironforge Senate. Senir admits he has fallen behind on filing his own observations due to the bitter cold, but receiving Grelin's dispatch nudges him back into service, opening further work monitoring hostile forces across the snowfields.

quest:421.text: Prove Your Worth. Prove Your Worth is an introductory Horde quest offered by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. To assist the Forsaken campaign against southern human and dwarven territories, adventurers are tasked with thinning the feral worgen prowling near the roadside. It marks the opening step in unraveling the arcane fallout wrought by Archmage Arugal. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, have set their sights on securing the regions south of Tirisfal Glades, including human and dwarven enclaves. However, the path through Silverpine Forest remains fraught with danger. Instead of an open staging ground, the Forsaken find their supply lines and forward bases threatened by feral Moonrage worgen that roam the pine-choked hills. The presence of these beasts is no natural occurrence. Dalar Dawnweaver points the finger directly at Arugal, a disgraced former mage of Dalaran who unleashed otherworldly worgen upon the region during the Scourge invasion. Arugal has since claimed Shadowfang Keep, letting his feral creations overrun the forest. Before Dalar will entrust soldiers with deeper investigations into Arugal's sorcery, recruits must demonstrate their martial prowess by culling the nearest Moonrage Whitescalps.

quest:422.text: Arugal's Folly. Assigned by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, this quest tasks Forsaken agents with securing Arugal's earliest spellbooks from a nearby farmstead. Uncovering the magic behind the worgen curse is vital for the Forsaken to turn it against the mad mage and secure Silverpine Forest. Recovering the Remedy of Arugal marks the first step in unraveling the threat looming from Shadowfang Keep. Dalar Dawnweaver, an ambitious Forsaken mage residing in the crypts of the Sepulcher, holds no respect for Archmage Arugal. To Dawnweaver, Arugal was an unremarkable practitioner whose inclusion in the Kirin Tor was baffling and whose magical understanding seemed amateurish. However, the monstrous beasts now roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver intends to deconstruct the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

quest:423.text: Arugal's Folly. This task sends Forsaken agents to collect enchanted shackles from Moonrage worgen roaming Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver, analyzing Arugal's notes, aims to unravel how the renegade mage artificially reinforced his unstable magic. Studying these bindings brings the Forsaken closer to dismantling the worgen threat plaguing the region. Upon inspecting Arugal's recovered research, Dalar Dawnweaver expresses utter contempt for his former peer. According to Dalar, Arugal was never fit to serve Dalaran, let alone handle high sorcery during the kingdom's direst hour. To compensate for his mediocre talent, Arugal relied on enchanted relics and hardware to bolster and bind his summoned worgen beasts. Dalar requires physical samples of these items to dissect the magical tether holding the monsters together. The cursed inhabitants of Silverpine, transformed into Moonrage worgen, wander the woods carrying physical manifestations of Arugal's binding enchantments. Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls stalk the regions to the north and east of the Sepulcher. Prized for the residual arcane energy woven into their metal, their heavy shackles serve as crucial specimens for Dawnweaver's counter-research against Shadowfang Keep.

quest:425.text: Ivar the Foul. Ivar the Foul is a quest in Silverpine Forest that marks the culmination of the reconnaissance mission undertaken by Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick. Trapped at the farmstead known as the Ivar Patch, Rane asks Horde travelers to eliminate the savage ghoul Ivar the Foul so Quinn can recover from his mauling and complete their report to High Executor Hadrec. Siblings Rane and Quinn Yorick were deployed by the Deathstalkers to conduct reconnaissance across Silverpine Forest on behalf of High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their reconnaissance grinded to a sudden, violent halt when moving through a farmstead in the northern forest, where they were ambushed by the vicious ghoul known as Ivar the Foul. Though the scouts managed to escape with their unlives, Quinn was severely mauled in the confrontation. Even after receiving an alchemical remedy concocted from forest beasts, Quinn remains too frail to march. Knowing Ivar prowls the nearby barn waiting for Rane's guard to falter, Rane calls upon Horde adventurers to storm the barn, sever Ivar's head, and permanently secure the homestead.

quest:426.text: The Mills Overrun. Tasked by Deathguard Dillinger in Brill, this mission sends Forsaken soldiers to break the Scourge's foothold at the nearby Agamand Mills. Mindless undead gather among the ruined windmills, threatening to establish a forward base dangerously close to Tirisfal Glades' settlements. To halt this staging ground, recruits must shatter the ranks of skeletal soldiers and bonecasters. The Agamand Mills once anchored the agricultural heart of Tirisfal Glades, but in the wake of the Third War, their windmills overlook a far grimmer harvest. Scourge forces under the Lich King's thrall have begun massing on the grounds. If these mindless thralls successfully secure the mills, they will have an entrenched base of operations from which to push deeper into Tirisfal and strike directly at the fledgling Forsaken holdings. Deathguard Dillinger wastes little time on sentiment. Tasked with fortifying Brill and policing the territory, Dillinger orders recruits to hunt down Rattlecage and Cracked Skull Soldiers alongside Darkeye Bonecasters. By demanding notched ribs and blackened skulls as proof of their destruction, Dillinger ensures the skeletal ranks are being physically battered apart, throwing the mindless remnants back toward the Plaguelands before their offensive can truly begin.

quest:427.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Executor Zygand in Brill coordinates the Forsaken campaign against the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Using intelligence recovered by Executor Arren, you are dispatched to eliminate Scarlet Warriors stationed at a guard tower west of the Solliden Farmstead. This assault marks the Forsaken military's opening offensive to purge the zealous crusaders from their borders. The fledgling Forsaken state under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner faces simultaneous threats on multiple fronts. While the Deathguard keeps a wary vigil against the swelling armies of the Lich King, the fanatical mortals of the Scarlet Crusade contest Forsaken dominance over their former homeland. The Crusade considers all undead abominations to be purged with fire and blade, blind to the fact that the Forsaken have broken free of the Scourge's control. Thanks to intelligence documents secured by Executor Arren at Deathknell, Executor Zygand now knows the exact encampments and outposts held by the zealots across Tirisfal Glades. With regular Deathguard garrisons occupied by Scourge containment, independent Forsaken champions are commissioned to strike out directly. The first strike falls upon the guard tower west of Solliden Farmstead, where Scarlet Warriors muster and threaten the western approaches to Brill.

quest:428.text: Lost Deathstalkers. Lost Deathstalkers is a reconnaissance mission assigned by High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Two Forsaken scouts, Rane and Quinn Yorick, went missing weeks ago while surveying the haunted farmsteads of northern Silverpine Forest. Tracking them down reveals not only their fate, but the encroaching perils that threaten the Forsaken hold on the region. The Deathstalkers serve as the eyes, ears, and hidden daggers of Lady Sylvanas and the Forsaken. When operatives go silent, command takes notice. High Executor Hadrec deployed the scouts Rane and Quinn Yorick into northern Silverpine Forest weeks ago to monitor the abandoned farms and watch for enemy movements. Having received no courier or report since their departure, Hadrec fears the duo met a grim end at the hands of the Scourge or worse. Northern Silverpine is rife with danger, situated between the ruined estates of Lordaeron and the shadowed borders of Tirisfal Glades. Wandering undead, prowling beasts, and feral worgen make unescorted travel perilous even for seasoned rogues. Tracking the Yoricks requires searching the dilapidated northern farmsteads where their reconnaissance first began, hoping to recover whatever intelligence they gathered before danger overwhelmed them.

quest:429.text: Wild Hearts. Wild Hearts is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest tasked by Rane Yorick. To save her brother Quinn from wounds inflicted by the ghoul Ivar the Foul, you must harvest discolored worg hearts and deliver them to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher for an alchemical remedy. Following the disastrous mission that left the Deathstalkers pinned down at a farm in northern Silverpine, Rane Yorick finds herself attending to her severely wounded brother, Quinn. The feral ghoul Ivar the Foul left Quinn mangled and failing to recover. Knowing conventional rest will not restore an undead body torn by such savagery, Rane looks to the macabre arts of the Royal Apothecary Society to stitch her brother back together. Silverpine's wolves have not escaped the dark corruption plaguing northern Lordaeron. The local worgs carry corrupted, discolored hearts that contain uniquely potent essences. While vile to ordinary eyes, the Royal Apothecaries have learned to distill these blighted organs into concoctions capable of revitalizing withered Forsaken flesh.

quest:430.text: Return to Quinn. Return to Quinn is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest where an adventurer delivers a restorative draught concocted by Apothecary Renferrel to the wounded Deathstalker Quinn Yorick. Trapped and weakened at the Ivar Patch north of the Sepulcher, Quinn requires the draught before he can contemplate returning to duty. Following the harvesting of wild beast hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher brews a restorative potion formulated to aid Quinn Yorick. Renferrel has little time for sentimentality or bedside manners, quickly handing off the mixture to return to his own clandestine alchemical research, leaving the adventurer to run the courier run back into the wilderness. Quinn Yorick hides beside his sister, Deathstalker Rane Yorick, amid the ruined farmstead known as the Ivar Patch. Severely hurt by the ghoul Ivar the Foul and unable to march through hostile territory, Quinn drinks the draught immediately upon arrival. While the concoction restores his strength enough to eventually travel, the surrounding territory remains fraught with danger, particularly under the watchful malice of the ghoul lurking nearby.

quest:431.text: Candles of Beckoning. Candles of Beckoning is a brief task centered around salvaging specialized ritual tapers discovered in Tirisfal Glades. These eerie tallow candles are steeped in dark practices and recovered from a crate on Gunther's Retreat, Gunther Arcanus's island in Brightwater Lake. The crate on Gunther's Retreat supplies the Candle of Beckoning used in his test of allegiance. Gunther asks an adventurer to take a candle to the old, bloody altar just off the island's southern coast, light it, and confront the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara. The crate holding these candles sits on Gunther's Retreat, the island in Brightwater Lake where the lich Gunther Arcanus dwells. A single candle is all that is needed for the test Gunther sets in Proving Allegiance: lit upon the old, bloody altar off the island's southern coast, it awakens the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara.

quest:432.text: Those Blasted Troggs!. Foreman Stonebrow is at his wit's end after troggs completely overran his operations at Gol'Bolar Quarry. Destructive and aggressive, the beasts have trashed his mining equipment and powder barrels, leaving him furious and demanding retaliation. Unable to fight them himself due to failing aim, he pays brave adventurers to head down into the pit and cull the brute Skullthumpers. Gol'Bolar Quarry was once a proud, productive dwarf excavation site nestled in the snowy hills of eastern Dun Morogh. That prosperity ended abruptly when subterranean troggs broke through the bedrock and swarmed the lower terraces. Instead of merely occupying the tunnels, the savages have wreaked wanton havoc, smashing scaffolding and blowing through precious barrels of blasting powder. Watching the ruin of his life's work from the safety of the ridge has pushed Foreman Stonebrow to the brink of apoplexy. Frustrated by his own aging hands and poor aim, he relies on passing wanderers and Alliance recruits to execute raw vengeance. Thinning the ranks of the burly Rockjaw Skullthumpers provides him a brief moment of relief, though nothing short of total extermination will truly satisfy his wrath.

quest:433.text: The Public Servant. Senator Mehr Stonehallow of Ironforge has traveled directly to Gol'Bolar Quarry to address the sudden trogg invasion threatening Dun Morogh's mining operations. Seeking to reclaim the site, he enlists adventurers to cut down the aggressive Rockjaw Bonesnappers so miners can return to work. It is rare to find a member of Ironforge's Senate standing in the slush and dirt of a contested mine, but Senator Mehr Stonehallow is no typical politician. Holding dual allegiance to the dwarven ruling body and the scholarly Explorers' League, Stonehallow has taken personal responsibility for organizing a response to the trogg infestation at Gol'Bolar Quarry. Rather than waiting for slow legislative measures, he directly contracts capable mercenaries and travelers to cull the invaders. Gol'Bolar Quarry was once a vital source of stone and mineral wealth for Dun Morogh, but deep excavations broke into previously sealed subterranean hollows. Primitive, savage troggs of the Rockjaw tribe flooded into the pits, wrecking delicate mining equipment and driving out civilian laborers. Stonehallow's objective is to clear out the vicious Rockjaw Bonesnappers, paving the way for Mountaineer garrisons to secure the quarry and restore iron-shoveling infrastructure.

quest:435.text: Escorting Erland. Trapped indoors by aggressive prowling predators, Deathstalker Erland requires an escort through Silverpine Forest to regroup with his partner. Assisting him safely across the wilderness delivers him directly to Deathstalker Rane Yorick. Even seasoned scouts of the Forsaken occasionally find themselves outmatched by the unforgiving ecology of Silverpine Forest. Deathstalker Erland finds himself cornered inside a dilapidated shelter, surrounded by starved wolves eager to pick at what little flesh remains on his withered frame. Alone, breaking through their pack is suicide. Erland's objective lies near the Ivar Patch, where his partner Deathstalker Rane Yorick maintains watch. The route cuts directly through predatory wolf territory. Once guided through the prowlers, Erland sprints the final stretch to reach the safety of Rane Yorick's outpost, where the scouts can consolidate their intelligence for the Undercity.

quest:437.text: The Dead Fields. The Dead Fields is an assault mission issued by High Executor Hadrec from the Sepulcher. Forsaken scouts discovered that the Rot Hide gnolls infesting an abandoned northern farmstead are led and shielded by the Scourge banshee Nightlash, whose destruction is critical to securing Silverpine Forest. North of the Sepulcher lies an abandoned farmstead known as the Dead Fields. Once ordinary farmland, the grounds are now choked by Rot Hide gnolls—pestilent, plagued scavengers that infest the Silverpine countryside. High Executor Hadrec previously sent small raiding parties to dislodge them, but every offensive stalled under unnatural magical resistance. The Rot Hides are not acting merely on feral instinct; they are reinforced by the Scourge. A banshee named Nightlash oversees the area, using dark sorcery to scatter Forsaken skirmishers whenever the gnolls face ruin. Hadrec dispatches Horde champions to cut down the gnolls until Nightlash is lured out, demanding her spectral essence as proof of her demise.

quest:445.text: Delivery to Silverpine Forest. This errand serves as a vital courier mission linking the Royal Apothecary Society's research in Brill with their ongoing efforts in Silverpine Forest. Tasked by Apothecary Johaan, you carry valuable findings to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher to aid the development of the Dark Lady's New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society operates under the direct command of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, tasked with concocting a New Plague capable of wiping out both the living and the Scourge. Isolated laboratories across Forsaken territory cannot work in a vacuum; survival and progress demand constant communication. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan has gathered experimental results that must be circulated to other researchers in the field without delay. Silverpine Forest represents the next frontier of Forsaken expansion and research. Based out of the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel oversees biochemical testing amidst regional threats like the Moonrage worgen, rogue humans, and lingering Scourge. By receiving Johaan's notes from Tirisfal Glades, Renferrel integrates new alchemical findings into his own local experiments, further advancing the Society's grand design.

quest:447.text: A Recipe For Death. A Recipe For Death is an alchemical errand commissioned by Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Tasked with gathering grizzly bear hearts and arachnid blood, adventurers transport the volatile biological reagents to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity to aid in formulating the Forsaken's lethal New Plague. Positioned on the front lines in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel recognizes the grim arithmetic facing Sylvanas's people. Surrounded by the relentless legions of Arthas and enduring remnants of humanity, conventional warfare offers little hope. The Forsaken's grand ambition lies in developing a New Plague—an engineered contagion potent enough to rot both living humans and undead Scourge alike. Renferrel's field research determined that combining arachnid venom from the Skittering Dark with toxins concentrated in the hearts of native bears yields a virulent foundation. Once the harvested organs and blood are collected from the wilderness of Silverpine, they must be delivered beneath the ruins of Lordaeron into the heart of the Apothecarium. There, Master Apothecary Faranell oversees the grand design of the Royal Apothecary Society. Faranell immediately takes custody of Renferrel's samples, testing their contaminable properties to refine formulas that might one day secure Forsaken supremacy across the continent.

quest:449.text: The Deathstalkers' Report. The Deathstalkers' Report is a crucial military courier assignment delivered to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. After securing injured Deathstalkers in the northern wilds, you carry their gathered intelligence concerning unexpected Scourge activity back to Forsaken high command. This dispatch alters the Forsaken's assessment of their hold on Silverpine Forest. The Deathstalkers act as the eyes, ears, and daggers of the Dark Lady, pushing into the untamed wilderness ahead of standard military units. Near the border of Tirisfal and Silverpine, an advance patrol ran into catastrophic resistance while charting enemy movements. Though Deathstalker Quinn barely survived his injuries and Erland fought his way to safety, their scouting mission yielded intelligence essential to the Forsaken occupation of Silverpine Forest. When High Executor Hadrec reviews the sealed field report, it confirms dark news: the mindless forces of the Scourge have maintained a far heavier and more aggressive presence in Silverpine than Undercity strategists anticipated. Instead of merely securing abandoned human hamlets and pacifying rogue beasts, the Sepulcher command must brace for coordinated Scourge opposition while fighting to claim the region.

quest:4495.text: A Good Friend. At Aldrassil, Dirania Silvershine grows worried when Iverron misses his daily visit. She asks travelers to search the hills near Shadowthread Cave, north of Shadowglen. Dirania Silvershine waits beneath Aldrassil for Iverron, who visits her every day. Hours pass without him, and she asks travelers heading into Shadowglen to look for her friend. Iverron often wanders the hills in northern Shadowglen, near the webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. The spiders make the surrounding slopes dangerous for travelers. Search west of the cave entrance, where Iverron is hiding and needs help.

quest:45.text: Discover Rolf's Fate. In eastern Elwynn, two Stormwind guards are missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks lead toward a murloc village, where the search for Rolf continues. Guard Thomas sent patrols around eastern Elwynn Forest as threats grew, but Malakai and Rolf vanished near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints pressed into the mud lead east along the water's edge, straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

quest:456.text: The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine calls newly awakened night elves to tend Shadowglen’s wildlife. Young nightsabers and thistle boars have grown too numerous, and keeping Teldrassil’s natural harmony calls for stewardship and difficult choices. In Shadowglen, beneath the Great Tree’s sprawling boughs, heavy spring rains have disrupted Teldrassil’s young, fragile forest cycle. Some wildlife populations have grown beyond what the land can sustain. They threaten to strip the glen of resources and bring famine to the ecosystem. Preserving the forest calls for active care. Conservator Ilthalaine watches over Shadowglen’s woods, keeping any one part from overtaking the others. To prevent mass starvation among the animals, he sends young night elves into the grove to thin thistle boars and predatory nightsabers. The work is unglamorous, but vital: kaldorei stewardship means seeking harmony with nature through active balance and difficult decisions.

quest:457.text: The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine sends defenders into Shadowglen to thin its growing wildlife. Mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers threaten the glade's balance. Shadowglen's adult animals now threaten the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine sends young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers. Their appetites can exhaust the land's limited plants and game. North of Aldrassil, younger cubs give way to mottled nightsabers and aggressive boars that root through the soil. For kaldorei, controlled hunting is a grim duty, but it protects the whole forest from collapse.

quest:458.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm hears troubling whispers from the forest spirits. He asks you to find Tarindrella, an elusive dryad whose unexpected return hints at trouble beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Melithar Staghelm receives troubling omens from the woodland spirits while training novices beneath Aldrassil’s boughs. Tarindrella, a dryad regarded as a protector of the wild, has returned to Shadowglen after many years away from Kalimdor’s woodlands. Dryads rarely appear without cause, and Melithar fears the natural order is out of balance.

quest:459.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella seeks the cause of the forest’s sudden unrest and the furbolgs’ disappearance. Grells have turned aggressive, and Fel Moss points to dark magic in Teldrassil’s boughs. Shadowglen’s quiet woods have grown hostile. The furbolgs have left their ancestral dens and gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Feral grells and grellkin now overrun the woodland paths, and Tarindrella has noticed the dark change spreading through Teldrassil. Tarindrella suspects corruption is stirring the forest’s creatures. You slay the grells and bring her samples of Fel Moss, evidence of dark enchantments clinging to Teldrassil’s boughs. With the corruption confirmed, she sends young defenders to Dolanaar to speak with Druid Athridas Bearmantle.

quest:46.text: Bounty on Murlocs. Murlocs are spreading through eastern Elwynn, and the Stormwind Army has put a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear the shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before the murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers now attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a minor nuisance has grown into a threat across eastern Elwynn, while the western roads remain comparatively secure. Guard Thomas is stationed at the eastern bridge beside the Redridge Mountains, where dangers beyond the bridge and disorder at home compete for his attention. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and Stormwind's military command is mired in bureaucracy. Town garrisons rarely get the reinforcements they request. Marshal Dughan and local officers have turned to public bounties, offering coin for murloc fins to slow the attacks along the waterways.

quest:4681.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore's misty coast, dead sea creatures have drawn Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde into a troubling inquiry. She serves the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and seeks to learn why marine life is stranding or dying along the shore. Dead sea creatures line Darkshore's beaches and shallows, puzzling the night elves of Auberdine. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde has already examined one stranded creature along the beach. Now she asks you to dive west of the docks, near a sunken vessel, and inspect the bones of a massive sea turtle. The evidence will help her report to the Temple of the Moon.

quest:47.text: Gold Dust Exchange. At Goldshire's crossroads, Gold Dust Exchange brings Remy "Two Times" coin for gold dust from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. Travelers gather the dust and trade it to the nervous broker for pay. Goldshire sits where Elwynn Forest's roads meet, and travelers, merchants, and guards pass through town. Remy "Two Times" is a shady broker with a habit of repeating his words and a sharp eye for profit. Instead of paying mining crews to dig for raw minerals, he turns to travelers passing through the Lion's Pride Inn. He offers coin for gold dust taken from the kobolds in the region. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. These rat-like tunnelers chip through the dark for candles and shiny baubles, gathering flecks of unrefined ore in their pouches. Pushing them back serves the kingdom, and gathering their dust turns the work into a trade for coin.

quest:4722.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s surf-battered shore, a massive sea turtle lies beached as murlocs pick over its carcass. Viable biological samples remain among the scavenged remains, and Auberdine naturalists send them to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for study. Darkshore’s long coast often catches the dead and confused from the Great Sea. Ancient sea turtles drift ashore after death or beach themselves in confusion. Their carcasses quickly draw scavengers, and hostile Greymist murlocs have made crude camps around this turtle’s skeletal frame. They carve away flesh and shell, yet viable bone, shell, or tissue samples may remain intact in the wreckage. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is stationed in Auberdine as a field researcher, documenting unusual marine life and ecological disturbances along the coast. Night elves regard stranded beasts with reverence and scientific curiosity. Suitable remains are cataloged and prepared for shipment to scholars in Darnassus, who seek to understand why so many giants of the open sea are washing ashore.

quest:4723.text: Beached Sea Creature. At Mist's Edge, a giant sea thresher lies stranded while murlocs feed on its carcass. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples for night elf researchers in Darnassus, who seek to learn why deep-sea giants are washing ashore. Enormous thresher remains have appeared along Mist's Edge, where shipwrecks and tide-washed debris are familiar sights. This beast dwarfs the wildlife of Darkshore's shallows, suggesting it came from far beyond the calm waters of the Veiled Sea. Murlocs swarm over the corpse to feed, but they lack the strength and coordination to bring down a creature of this size. Something else killed the predator before the sea carried it ashore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde coordinates efforts in Auberdine to salvage bones and biological samples from Darkshore's stranded sea giants. Night elf researchers in Darnassus hope the remains will show whether illness, disturbances in the deep sea, or arcane corruption drives the giants onto the killing sands.

quest:4725.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's shore, Beached Sea Turtle lies with a broken carriage on its shell. Greymist murlocs have gathered around the great carcass. You find a broken carriage strapped across a giant sea turtle's shell on Darkshore's misty shore. Many sea creatures have washed up along this coast, but this turtle was made to carry a load. Its handlers drove it onto the beach, and the carriage now lies abandoned in the tide. Greymist murlocs soon swarm the turtle's remains. They have made a den among the rotting meat and scavenged timber. A marked container lies among their refuse and the broken carriage frame, left by the turtle's former masters.

quest:4727.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s northern shore, Beached Sea Turtle remains untouched by nearby Greymist murlocs. A sample is carried to Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon. Naturalists and priestesses seek to learn why great sea creatures wash ashore and scavengers leave them alone. Greymist murlocs crowd Darkshore’s northern coast and scavenge whatever food washes up from the Veiled Sea. Yet the great turtle’s skeleton lies mostly untouched. Those studying the shore wonder whether the murlocs missed it or avoided it for some unknown reason. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples from beached sea turtles for the Temple of the Moon. The night elf priestesses study the disturbances in Darkshore’s waters. Skeletal fragments may help them learn whether sickness, magic, or dangerous sea predators are killing the ancient creatures.

quest:4728.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a giant sea mammal lies washed ashore beside an abandoned dig site. Its carcass and scattered tools draw murlocs and passing travelers. A giant sea mammal lies on Darkshore's sand, partly gutted and worn by the sea. A rusted wheelbarrow and discarded tools mark the place where an organized study began. The researchers left before they could finish. Dwarven field researchers from the Explorer's League were studying the carcass in Darkshore. Their work stopped when local murlocs swarmed the site to scavenge. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine acts for the Temple of the Moon and accepts salvaged bone samples to help study the unnatural wash-ups along the coast.

quest:4730.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a great sea mammal lies half-devoured on the sand. Murlocs gather around it, and Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples to learn why gentle sea beasts are dying on the shore. Far north along Darkshore's lonely beaches, a great sea mammal lies rotting and half-eaten. Murlocs pick over its bones, more vicious than usual. These beasts were gentle in life, and their deaths trouble the coast as much as the blighted forests inland. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde says these gentle mammals live in the waters around Teldrassil's base. Unlike aggressive threshers, they have never been known to drive themselves onto the rocks. The Temple of the Moon is gathering bone samples to learn what corruption or threat drives them from the deep.

quest:4731.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's coast, a Beached Sea Turtle lies dead beneath the carriage it once hauled. A box marked with strange runes rests in the wreckage. A dead sea turtle lies among the ancient bones scattered along Darkshore's coast. Splintered carriage boards still cling to its broad shell. The turtle was driven onto the rocks while hauling cargo, rather than stranded by sickness or disorientation. A container carved with unfamiliar, serpent-like marks lies in the wreckage, amid scavengers feeding on the remains.

quest:4733.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore's rocky Twilight Shore, a colossal thresher lies stranded, far larger than any known local specimen. Its death and stranding add to the deep-sea troubles worrying the night elves. You find driftwood and sea debris along the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore, but one inlet holds the remains of an enormous thresher. Tides and scavengers have begun picking it apart, yet its skeleton dwarfs ordinary predators in these coastal shallows. The giant is an outsider to these waters. Sickness or disorientation may have driven it onto the rocks, or some deeper disturbance may lie out in the Veiled Sea.

quest:4740.text: WANTED: Murkdeep!. Auberdine posts an Alliance bounty for Murkdeep, blamed for a Sentinel's death and ships lost off Darkshore. The village council wants the dangerous murloc chieftain dead. Find him south along the misty coast. The Greymist murlocs along Darkshore are usually a nuisance, but Murkdeep has turned against Auberdine. The wanted poster outside the inn names him as the killer of at least one night elf Sentinel. It also suspects him of sabotaging or wrecking two cargo vessels offshore. With ships lost and raids along the coast, the Auberdine Village Council has set a public bounty on the murloc leader. Murkdeep lurks off the southern coast, near murloc huts clustered around a bonfire. Trespassers draw an organized defense: Greymist coastrunners and shore-crawlers surge from the surf to protect their settlement. Murkdeep then emerges alongside his vanguard to strike the intruders. Proof of Murkdeep's death meets a grim need for the Sentinels. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea handles the bounty payout for the council. With Greymist leadership broken, travelers and ships on the foggy Darkshore coast gain a reprieve from sabotage.

quest:475.text: A Troubling Breeze. Athridas Bearmantle waits for word from Starbreeze Village, but the reports have stopped. Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren watches over the sleeping Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, and his silence points to danger in Teldrassil. Athridas Bearmantle depends on regular word from Gaerolas Talvethren, the Great Warden watching over the Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The druids sleep there to keep their sacred pact with Ysera in the Emerald Dream. Their sanctuary matters to the spiritual balance of the young World Tree. Now reports from the east have ceased, and unease spreads through the forest.

quest:476.text: Gnarlpine Corruption. Near Starbreeze Village, Gnarlpine Corruption threatens Teldrassil. Wounded Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren sends word to the night elf leadership in Dolanaar: Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the village and fallen to demonic corruption. Their violence may reach the sleeping druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Near the ruins of Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren lies grievously wounded after an ambush by his former allies. The Gnarlpine furbolgs were long regarded as peaceful neighbors and stewards of the wild, but now they have turned feral. Too injured to carry the warning himself, Gaerolas entrusts you with bringing word to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the madness spreads farther through Teldrassil.

quest:4761.text: Thundris Windweaver. In Auberdine, reports of Blackwood aggression reach the village elder. Terenthis sends you to Thundris Windweaver with news of the furbolgs’ growing hostility. Thundris seeks the cause of the corruption spreading through Darkshore. After scouting corrupted furbolg camps in Darkshore, you carry Terenthis’s report to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Terenthis remains in the wilds to investigate the spreading corruption. As village elder, Thundris oversees the settlement’s daily welfare and considers the spiritual and environmental dangers facing the kaldorei. Your report gives Auberdine’s leadership evidence that the furbolgs are growing more than territorial: an unnatural malice is taking hold of them. Thundris has heard of rising hostility from the forest dwellers near Auberdine. The furbolgs’ aggression is not the only concern. Corruption is spreading through Darkshore’s soil, plants, and waters. Thundris believes the land cannot be healed until the source of the blight is found. He turns to the waterways and enlists capable allies to trace the taint upstream.

quest:4762.text: The Cliffspring River. In Darkshore, foul water now runs down the Cliffspring River toward Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver asks Alliance investigators to take a sample from the pool beneath a road bridge waterfall. He suspects the corruption began beyond the riverbanks. The Cliffspring River runs from the eastern highlands to the coastal shoals of Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Its waters have begun to carry an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Thundris Windweaver fears the foul water will poison the shores and the town's supplies, so he sends scouts upriver to take samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

quest:477.text: Border Crossings. Border Crossings is an espionage task assigned by Shadow Priest Allister in the Sepulcher to investigate Dalaran's covert operations in Silverpine Forest. By intercepting supply crates bound for the Dalaran encampment near Pyrewood Village, the Forsaken hope to uncover why the Kirin Tor are actively supporting the human bastion of Ambermill. While Ambermill stands as the main stronghold of surviving human resistance in eastern Silverpine Forest, the magi of Dalaran have not left them to stand alone. Wagon shipments filled with supplies and arcana have been smuggled out of the Hillsbrad Foothills, crossing through Silverpine to supply forward outposts and staging grounds. One such logistical camp sits just north of Pyrewood Village, manned by Dalaran personnel watching the road. Shadow Priest Allister and the Forsaken leadership at the Sepulcher find Dalaran's intense investment in Ambermill troubling. To them, a provincial town would hardly justify the Kirin Tor risking resources and lives deep within Forsaken-claimed territory unless some greater strategic or magical objective was at stake. Investigating the crates gives the Forsaken direct intelligence on what Dalaran is shipping west.

quest:478.text: Maps and Runes. Maps and Runes is a Forsaken reconnaissance mission in Silverpine Forest. After discovering a suspicious shipment shipped toward Ambermill, adventurers recover a rune-inscribed pendant to deliver to Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher for further investigation. While intercepting logistics around Ambermill, Horde agents uncover a Dalaran crate concealed along the border routes. Rather than mundane supplies, the container holds detailed regional charts and an enigmatic, rune-inscribed pendant. Recognizing the potential danger of Dalaran's arcane reach so close to their borders, scouts carefully retrieve the artifact to avoid alarming the surrounding human sentries.

quest:481.text: Dalar's Analysis. Dalar's Analysis is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest linking Shadow Priest Allister's espionage against Ambermill with the arcane research of Dalar Dawnweaver. After uncovering a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate, adventurers bring the relic to Dalar at the Sepulcher for scrutiny. The artifact reveals that the surviving mages of Dalaran are marshaling significant magical power for a hidden initiative. Following a raid on a Dalaran supply crate at a camp north of Pyrewood Village, Shadow Priest Allister receives a rune-inscribed pendant found beneath a bundle of old maps. Recognizing that its enchantment lies beyond his spiritual purview, Allister directs the relic to Dalar Dawnweaver, an arcane scholar stationed at the Sepulcher who is better suited to decipher Dalaran's magical warding.

quest:4811.text: The Red Crystal. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea asks travelers in Auberdine to investigate a red crystal in Darkshore's eastern mountains. Hostile moonkin are multiplying nearby and seem drawn to it, and the Sentinels need to know if the formation is real. Moonkin were long seen as gentle, mystical creatures bound to the wilds of Kalimdor. Now aggressive packs are multiplying along the slopes east of Auberdine. Some night elves still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea puts the town's safety first as the danger grows. Reports place the beasts at a single spot among the eastern peaks. Scouts and wanderers speak of an unnatural red crystal jutting from a rocky hillside high above Darkshore. Rumors travel easily along the fogbound coast, so Glynda wants someone to see the place firsthand.
