Bringing such a wild, airborne hunter under control tests your reflexes and your calm, demanding that you endure its talons while using the enchanted rod to align your spirit with its instincts. For the tauren, hunting and animal companionship are fundamentally spiritual pursuits rather than mere subjugation. By mastering creatures of both earth and sky, you demonstrate the balance and respect necessary to walk the plains without disrupting nature. Yaw Sharpmane recognizes this maturity, taking back his temporary taming rod and passing on the lasting techniques of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming a companion of your own choosing.

quest:6089.text: Training the Beast. Training the Beast is the culminating rite of passage for young tauren hunters in Mulgore. After demonstrating the spiritual patience and resolve required to soothe the wild beasts of the plains, hunters are sent to Thunder Bluff to learn the lifelong discipline of bonding with, nourishing, and commanding a permanent animal companion. Having successfully tested their spirit against the dangerous predators of Mulgore—plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops—tauren hunters are judged ready for the true mantle of the hunter. Yaw Sharpmane, the mentor in Bloodhoof Village, entrusts the novice with a journey to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. There stands Holt Thunderhorn, a legendary figure among the shu'halo whose reputation for communing with the wilds is surpassed only by his reverence for the Earthmother. To the tauren, a beast is not a simple weapon or thrall; it is a partner granted through harmony with the natural world. Holt Thunderhorn imparts the vital knowledge required to sustain this partnership. A hunter must learn not only how to guide the creature's combat instincts, but how to nourish its body through regular feeding, mend its injuries, and call its spirit back should it fall defending its companion on the plains.

quest:61.text: Shipment to Stormwind. William Pestle sends a parcel from Goldshire to his brother Morgan in Stormwind. Its candles carry wax supplies from Elwynn Forest to Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. William gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods in Goldshire, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot easily leave his post at the Lion's Pride Inn, so he depends on travelers heading into the city to carry goods for him. William's parcel holds large candles gathered from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. He says he collects them for their wax. Delivering the shipment brings those supplies to Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District.

quest:6101.text: Taming the Beast. Dazalar guides a night elf hunter through a second trial in Dolanaar. With an enchanted taming rod, you subdue a nightsaber stalker and learn how wild beasts differ. Dazalar teaches you that the forest's creatures do not all behave alike. Each species has its own temperament, and a hunter must learn to meet it on its own terms. Beneath Teldrassil's canopy, the next test brings you against beasts more cunning and predatory than webspinners. Kaldorei revere nightsabers as sacred predators, fierce guardians, and companions of the Sentinels. With the taming rod, you face a nightsaber stalker and must keep a steady nerve and calm authority. Winning its trust shows you can handle a predator, not only the more docile creatures of the woods.

quest:6102.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast brings a young night elf hunter to the final trial of basic training. Under Dazalar’s direction, hunters tame a predatory owl of the skies before gaining the power to choose a lifelong companion. Night elf hunters must make peace with creatures across Teldrassil before their basic beastcraft is complete. After proving their will against beasts of the underbrush, they face the spirit of the skies, the Strigid Screecher. These watchful birds of prey roost high in the boughs west of Dolanaar. Patience and a steady nerve are needed to pacify one with the enchanted Taming Rod. Taming the Strigid Screecher fulfills the ancient lessons of communion between kaldorei hunters and nature. When the apprentice returns the spent rod to Dazalar, the training exercises end. The apprentice earns the full art of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming beasts of their own choosing across Azeroth.

quest:6103.text: Training the Beast. In Teldrassil, Training the Beast sends night elf hunters from the wilds to Darnassus. After taming beasts among the boughs, they learn pet care and discipline from Jocaste. Dazalar sends you from the wilds near Dolanaar to Darnassus once you prove you can tame a beast. Before you travel Kalimdor with a loyal companion, you need to learn more than how to use a taming rod. Subduing a wild creature tests your strength and will, but an untrained beast can still be unpredictable. Jocaste teaches you the arts of caring for a companion in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. She shows you how to feed your pet, bring it back if tragedy strikes, and train it to fight. For night elves, this bond reflects reverence for nature, not simple control.

quest:6121.text: Lessons Anew. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends Alliance druids from Darnassus to Moonglade for training. There, Dendrite Starblaze begins their instruction in cleansing venom and toxins. Druids learn from Cenarius, the demigod whose teachings and blessings bind them to the living world. His gifts include the power to cleanse venom with a simple incantation. Such power is not given lightly. Before young druids can wield it, they must learn the hard, ordinary work of fighting toxins without nature's magic. Mathrengyl Bearwalker trains druids in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. He sends his student past local practice and on to Moonglade. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze coordinates the Cenarion Circle's wider efforts and has practical work for the novice.

quest:6122.text: The Principal Source. At Cliffspring Falls, a sickness among Darkshore's deer draws the Cenarion Circle's attention to the water. Dendrite Starblaze sends young druids from Moonglade to collect a sample for Auberdine naturalist Alanndarian Nightsong. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore with fresh water. When deer began to sicken with a lingering malady, the Cenarion Circle looked to the river for its cause. Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade suspects the water source is tainted and sends novice druids to gather a sample at the cavern mouth beneath the falls. Vicious naga dwell inside Cliffspring River Cave, near the falls' headwaters. Their presence threatens anyone trying to investigate the blight. The Cenarion Circle needs a sample from the cave mouth to study what is making the wilderness sick.

quest:6123.text: Gathering the Cure. Gathering the Cure is an essential trial for young night elf druids learning to master nature's healing powers in Darkshore. Guided by Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine, the druid collects vital natural reagents to brew a restorative salve for the region's ailing wildlife. This task lays the practical foundation for understanding how herbal remedies combat venom and disease. Following the discovery of a contaminated water source plaguing the local wildlife, Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine sets out to concoct an effective curative salve. While the sampled Cliffspring water forms the base of the mixture, genuine healing requires potent natural catalysts. The afflicted forest deer cannot recover on their own, making the gathering of wholesome remedies a matter of urgency for the Cenarion Circle. The restorative salve demands two crucial flora: Earthroot and Lunar Fungus. Earthroot provides pure curative properties, requiring the practiced eye of an herbalist to harvest from the rocky soil. To lend the mixture potency, Alanndarian sends the druid into the nearby eastern caves to gather fungal blooms that flourish in the dark, nestled among increasingly territorial and agitated moonkin.

quest:6124.text: Curing the Sick. Darkshore’s deer are sick, and Curing the Sick asks you to bring them relief. Alanndarian Nightsong gives you salve to treat the poisoned animals before you report to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. In Darkshore, deer fall sick from the Cliffspring River south to the border of Ashenvale. They wander the misty woods, weakened by toxins in the soil and streams. After you gather the needed reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong gives you freshly brewed animal salve to treat the afflicted deer.

quest:6125.text: Power over Poison. In Darnassus, a young druid returns to complete Power over Poison. The Cenarion Circle's trial began in Darkshore, where the initiate learned to brew a remedy by hand. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong asks young druids to gather Earthroot and Lunar Fungus by hand. They brew a salve to heal stricken wildlife. Before granting the magic to purge toxins, the Cenarion Circle wants initiates to know the hardship of treating poison without spiritual aid. The work teaches them what common folk face when venom strikes, and why a druid must meet their suffering with care. After the remedy proves effective in Auberdine, Starblaze sends the druid across the sea to Darnassus. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits in the Cenarion Enclave. Pleased with the initiate's grace under pressure, he teaches the art of cleansing toxins through nature's power. But virulent poisons in the wilds around Auberdine trouble him, for they point to an unnatural blight disturbing the land's balance.

quest:6126.text: Lessons Anew. Lessons Anew is a rite of passage for young tauren druids, initiated by Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise of Thunder Bluff. It directs apprentices to travel to the sacred haven of Moonglade to begin mastering the art of cleansing natural and unnatural poisons. Guided by the night elf Dendrite Starblaze, this lesson sets aside mock trials in favor of confronting an urgent, real-world poisoning crisis. Druids hold a sacred mandate to protect the wilds, which includes the miraculous ability bestowed by Cenarius to purge virulent toxins with a simple incantation. However, such potent magic is not handed over without grounding. Turak Runetotem insists that before channeling divine energies to effortlessly dispel blights, a druid must understand the physical toll of venom and learn to treat it through grounded, mundane means. Rather than conducting training solely on the bluffs of Mulgore, promising acolytes are sent north through sacred pathways to Moonglade. There, within the peaceful village of Nighthaven, ancient night elf mentors such as Dendrite Starblaze oversee the education of both elf and tauren practitioners. This shared instruction highlights the delicate truce that exists within the Cenarion Circle, rising above the political strife separating Horde and Alliance.

quest:6127.text: The Principal Source. Dendrite Starblaze sends Horde druids to Dreadmist Peak for a water sample. From Moonglade, she asks them to bring it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads, where it can help explain the poison harming wildlife. Dreadmist Peak rises northwest of the Crossroads, with springs and pools high above the dry northern Barrens. Their waters shape local weather and moisture. The Burning Blade, a cult devoted to demons, has taken hold on the crags. Dendrite Starblaze fears their foul sorcery may taint the basin around this important mountain. Sick gazelles stumble across the northern savanna, north of the main east-west trail through the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem seeks help for the local tauren and turns to the Cenarion Circle to learn what is poisoning the herd. Druids who reach the peak and bring back a sample of its tainted water give Tonga what he needs to study the sickness and brew an antidote.

quest:6128.text: Gathering the Cure. At the Crossroads, young tauren druids face a sacred passage under Tonga Runetotem's guidance. You gather earthroot and sturdy kodo horns to make a salve for the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Tonga Runetotem needs raw ingredients to brew an antidote from the water sample you secured at Dreadmist Peak. Natural water forms the salve's base, earthroot supplies its medicinal qualities, and ground kodo horn gives it the strength to drive venom from a creature's system. For a young druid, gathering them means relying on the gifts of the earth and hunting local beasts. Tonga Runetotem uses the salve's preparation to teach the limits of physical medicine. Herbal lore and alchemy can counter specific toxins, but each poison usually needs its own cure. Rather than carry endless herbs and horns, druids learn to attune to nature's healing energies. That lesson leads to the druidic art of Cure Poison.

quest:6129.text: Curing the Sick. Curing the Sick is an essential trial for young Horde druids, tasking them with healing afflicted wildlife in the northern Barrens. By applying a freshly concocted herbal salve to ailing gazelles, initiates demonstrate both their practical field medicine and their commitment to preserving natural balance. Completing this duty proves their dedication directly to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Across the northern savanna of the Barrens, grazing gazelles have begun succumbing to an unnatural affliction. After gathering earthroot and kodo horns to assemble a curative remedy, Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads entrusts a young druid with administering the field treatment. The initiate must search north of the main crossroads to find and minister to ten suffering animals, providing immediate relief before the rot takes further root in the ecosystem. Once the salve is dispensed, the druid's path leads back into the tranquil boughs of Moonglade. There, Dendrite Starblaze recognizes the initiate's compassion and vigilance. He notes that the suffering of the gazelles is merely a symptom of a deeper, insidious corruption stalking Kalimdor's wilderness. By tending to the lowliest beasts, tauren druids demonstrate that reverence for Cenarius transcends tribal boundaries, earning deeper secrets of poison cleansing and nature magic.

quest:6130.text: Power over Poison. Power over Poison is the concluding rite in a young Horde druid's trial to master restorative nature magic. Having cured afflicted gazelles around the Crossroads using only herbal mixtures, the initiate returns to Turak Runetotem on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise to receive the true gift of Cure Poison. Before granting a fledgling druid the innate magical power to cleanse venoms, the Cenarion Circle demands they understand the physical reality of affliction. Dendrite Starblaze sent the novice to the Crossroads, where Tonga Runetotem had them gather earthly reagents for a curative salve made by hand. Only by treating the poisoned plains gazelles of the Barrens without spiritual aid does the student witness the agonizing struggle ordinary creatures face against natural and unnatural toxins. With the trial complete, Dendrite sends the initiate back to Turak Runetotem, the grand druid trainer residing on the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Turak observes that the strange, virulent poisons surfacing near the Crossroads threaten the natural balance of the plains and warrant grave concern. Commending the initiate's grace under pressure, Turak permanently imparts the spiritual art of curing poisons, entrusting them to safeguard Kalimdor's living creatures.

quest:6181.text: A Swift Message. Quartermaster Lewis at Sentinel Hill needs urgent armor shipments from Stormwind to equip the People's Militia. Because Westfall receives almost no official military aid, he sends you to Thor the gryphon master to carry an urgent requisition note to the capital by air. Sentinel Hill stands isolated against a rising tide of Defias outlaws and gnolls, starved of direct military aid from Stormwind. Quartermaster Lewis relies on private contacts in the capital to keep the People's Militia supplied with weapons and armor. With gear running thin, his only lifeline is Osric Strang, an armorer located in Old Town. Getting an urgent requisition to him requires swift travel, leading Lewis to enlist travelers to contact Westfall's gryphon master, Thor. Gryphons provide the Kingdom of Stormwind with an invaluable rapid transit and courier network. Perched at Sentinel Hill, Thor manages the outpost's aerial link back to the capital. Handing Lewis's note to Thor opens the skies between Westfall and the royal city, demonstrating how crucial the gryphon riders are to sustaining frontier garrisons cut off from formal aid.

quest:62.text: The Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds have overrun The Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure farms. The mine's fall points to a growing pest problem across Elwynn Forest. While Northshire Valley faces its own vermin, reports reach Goldshire that kobolds have claimed another vital site. Between the feuding Stonefield and Maclure homesteads south of town, the Fargodeep Mine once supplied stone and ore for the realm. Now shrill chattering and tallow candles fill its damp tunnels. Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the depths and learn how bad the trouble is. The report of kobolds in the mine adds to the Stormwind Guard's strain. Its troops are already stretched thin defending against Defias bandits and gnoll incursions, leaving too few to clear the tunnels. When Dughan hears the report, he worries about other mineral sites, including the Jasperlode Mine to the northeast.

quest:6261.text: Dungar Longdrink. At Stormwind's Trade District roost, Dungar Longdrink arranges swift gryphon transport for supplies bound to Westfall's embattled defenders. Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems have pushed Westfall close to breaking point. Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia are desperate for provisions. Lewis sent word to the capital, and armorer Osric Strang packed the requested equipment. Carrying military cargo on foot through bandit-ridden Elwynn and Westfall takes precious time. Stormwind's new aerial routes offer a vital link to the frontier. The gryphon roost sits in Stormwind's Trade District, where Dungar Longdrink coordinates courier and passenger flights. Wildhammer dwarves traditionally raise and handle these majestic beasts. They carry people and cargo across human lands when roosts at both ends know the route. Bringing Osric's heavy crate straight to Dungar teaches couriers how aerial logistics work. It connects the capital's stockpiles directly to frontier outposts such as Sentinel Hill.

quest:6281.text: Continue to Stormwind. You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town. Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note in Sentinel Hill. The local gryphon master Thor offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom's trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and the river border of Elwynn Forest, then over Stormwind City's high white ramparts. After you land at the capital's trade roosts, you head into Old Town to find Osric Strang at his shop, Limited Immunity. Osric supplies the frontier, but his grim reception shows the growing rift between Westfall's beleaguered People's Militia and the distracted rulers in Stormwind Keep.

quest:6285.text: Return to Lewis. Dungar Longdrink sends armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Osric's Crate crosses Elwynn and Westfall by gryphon, carrying supplies to defenders under pressure. Westfall is slipping from the kingdom's grasp. Defias bandits, ravenous gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers threaten the land. Overland supply routes face harassment, and roads are dangerous for solitary wagons. The flight master network offers a crucial lifeline. Osric, an armorer in Stormwind's Old Town, prepared a heavy crate of armor for the battered volunteers of the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Gryphons are loyal, well-trained beasts, but travel across the lands depends on established familiarity. Dungar Longdrink explains that gryphons instinctively know how to return to their capital roost in Stormwind. To carry a rider to a remote outpost, though, they need the traveler to have met its flight master in person. You have already checked in with Thor at Sentinel Hill, opening the skies over the frontier to rapid travel. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis receives the crate. He is the officer tasked with outfitting Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteer force, and he sets to work distributing the armor among the frontier defenders. For Sentinel Hill, reliable aerial contact with the capital can mean the difference between holding the line and being overrun by the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:6321.text: Supplying the Sepulcher. Supplying the Sepulcher is a logistical task issued by Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. To keep the local Deathguard detachment equipped against feral horrors and Scourge prowling the woods, an urgent weapon requisition must be routed via bat handler Karos Razok toward weapon suppliers in the Undercity. While Deathguard Podrig reports that the Sepulcher is relatively well-stocked, continuous attrition in Silverpine Forest consumes equipment at an alarming rate. Between feral beasts, prowling Scourge remnants, and aggressive local threats, frontline gear wears down or gets abandoned in skirmishes. Under orders from Executor Hadrec, Podrig drafts a direct requisition order addressed to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer operating out of the capital. Securing a steady flow of replacement blades and armor is essential if the Forsaken hope to retain their fragile footholds outside Tirisfal Glades. Moving critical correspondence and military supplies through Silverpine's mist-choked roads on foot is slow and prone to ambush. To bypass these perils, the Forsaken rely on captive, trained vampire bats. Handing Podrig's requisition to bat handler Karos Razok integrates foot soldiers into the broader aerial logistics network of the Undercity, establishing the aerial transit lines that tie outlying garrisons directly to Sylvanas's capital.

quest:6322.text: Michael Garrett. Michael Garrett is a simple courier task linking trade in the Undercity with the Forsaken's flight network. After collecting supplies packed by Gordon Wendham in the Trade Quarter, you are directed to deliver the crate to the bat handler Michael Garrett to arrange aerial transport out toward the Sepulcher. It highlights how the Forsaken utilize trained vampire bats to connect their capital with outposts across Lordaeron. Running a fledgeling kingdom carved out of the ruins of Lordaeron requires constant logistics. Outposts like the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest rely heavily on goods, munitions, and provisions moving out from the Undercity. Gordon Wendham packs the necessary field supplies into a single crate in the city's Trade Quarter, but carting freight by ground through blighted forests is both slow and vulnerable to ambush by Scourge remnants or wild beasts. To bypass the dangers on the roads, the Forsaken rely on captive vampire bats bred and maintained by skilled handlers. Michael Garrett oversees these winged beasts from his roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Delivering the cargo to him ensures the supplies can be strapped to a bat and flown directly over the hills to Silverpine, teaching new couriers how the capital coordinates with remote settlements.

quest:6323.text: Ride to the Undercity. Ride to the Undercity introduces fledgling Forsaken adventurers to the Horde's aerial flight network across Lordaeron. Carrying weapon requisitions from the embattled outpost of the Sepulcher, couriers take a dread bat directly into the Undercity's Trade Quarter to resupply regional defenders. Maintaining lines of communication between the Forsaken capital and its frontline outposts requires swift, reliable transit. Karos Razok, the bat handler stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, manages the trained dread bats that ferry messengers and supplies across the plagued landscape. With roads crawling with hostile beasts, Moonrage worgen, and remnants of the Scourge, taking to the skies is the safest and fastest way to ensure urgent military requests reach the capital. Upon touching down in the Undercity's bustling Trade Quarter, the courier delivers Podrig's equipment requisition directly to Gordon Wendham. As an Undercity weaponsmith dedicated to the Dark Lady's cause, Wendham ensures that regional outposts like the Sepulcher remain outfitted with clean, battle-ready armaments. Sustaining these defensive hubs is vital for the fledgling Forsaken nation as it secures its borders against surrounding enemies.

quest:6324.text: Return to Podrig. Return to Podrig is a logistics quest concluding a courier run between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. After delivering a dispatch to the capital, the courier is entrusted with a crate of weapons to ferry back to Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher using the Forsaken bat handler network. Outposts throughout Lordaeron depend heavily on regular shipments from the Undercity to remain operational. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Deathguard sentries face pressure from local worgen, Dalaran remnants, and Scourge stragglers. Supplying remote garrisons with freshly forged armaments is vital to holding the region under Forsaken control. Bat Master Michael Garrett operates the central roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, serving as the hub for Forsaken aerial travel. While bats naturally return to the capital, riders must first coordinate with local handlers like Karos Razok before flights to distant outposts can be charted. Flying Gordon's Crate across Lordaeron's skies teaches couriers how the Forsaken bind their scattered strongholds together.

quest:6341.text: The Bounty of Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong is sending fish samples from Rut'theran Village to Auberdine for comparison. She wants to learn whether Teldrassil's fish are larger and more plentiful than those along the mainland coast. Nessa Shadowsong asks you to carry fish bones and scales to Laird in Auberdine. Fishers in Rut'theran Village bring in large, plentiful catches, and she wants to know whether the mainland waters yield the same kind of fish. The samples will let Laird compare the island catch with fish from the coast of Darkshore. Nessa Shadowsong sends you to Vesprystus, the hippogryph master in Rut'theran Village, with the collection for Auberdine. Carrying the samples to him arranges your passage across the water to Darkshore.

quest:6342.text: Flight to Auberdine. You leave Teldrassil for Auberdine with a bundle of unusual fish specimens. Vesprystus sends you from Rut'theran Village by hippogryph to deliver them to Laird. Rut'theran Village is a sanctuary at the edge of the wider world for young adventurers leaving Teldrassil. A mundane ferry crosses the strait between the island and mainland Kalimdor, while night elves also travel by bonded hippogryph. Nessa Shadowsong entrusts you with a parcel of rare fish parts, and you take wing to reach the shores of Darkshore. Laird waits for Nessa's findings at the docks of Auberdine. He finds enormous scales as large as fists and a jawbone nearly twice the size of mainland specimens. The waters around the base of the World Tree seem to produce altered or abnormally large life, a curiosity tied to Teldrassil's potent, restless nature.

quest:6343.text: Return to Nessa. You carry Laird's findings from Auberdine back to Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. The journey is an introductory errand that teaches young travelers how to cross between Kalimdor and Teldrassil. Laird sends you back across the water with his written observations. He has found stark differences between the fish caught off Darkshore and those near Teldrassil, and suspects the great World Tree changes the local marine life. You can return to Rut'theran Village by hiring a flight from Caylais Moonfeather, the hippogryph master, or by boarding the regular ferry at Auberdine's pier. Nessa Shadowsong receives Laird's reply at Rut'theran Village and is fascinated by the difference in marine life. Fish near the World Tree grow so large that they bring an immediate boon to local fishermen, though the Kaldorei still do not know why. Nessa plans to share the findings with her fellow villagers. For now, she is content to harvest the abundant sea life and watch for whatever forces may be responsible.

quest:6344.text: Nessa Shadowsong. In Darnassus, Mydrannul sends a courier to meet Nessa Shadowsong below the World Tree. The delivery runs from Rut'theran Village to Darkshore, linking the canopy city with the shore. Mydrannul watches over travelers seeking work and purpose in Darnassus. Fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong needs a package carried across the sea to Darkshore, so Mydrannul directs able couriers toward the coast. Many young night elves begin their journeys among Teldrassil's boughs; this delivery takes them beyond the tree. From the Temple Gardens, the western portal in Darnassus leads down through the World Tree to Rut'theran Village. At the ocean-level roots, fishing docks and hippogryph perches connect Teldrassil with the rest of Kalimdor. Nessa Shadowsong tends her trade there and prepares shipments for Auberdine.

quest:6361.text: A Bundle of Hides. Jahan Hawkwing sends cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff for leatherworking. The delivery takes you across central Kalimdor and introduces the Crossroads wind rider roost. Hunters bring game hides and meat to the Crossroads, where Jahan Hawkwing gathers pelts from across the Barrens. The outposts cannot process every raw hide, so he asks travelers to carry them west to Thunder Bluff. Master leatherworkers there can turn the pelts into gear for the Horde. The trail across the Barrens and into Mulgore is rough, and quilboar and predators threaten anyone carrying cargo on foot. Jahan sends you to Devrak, the Crossroads wind rider master. He can take the goods by air aboard a trained wyvern, linking the Horde’s scattered settlements.

quest:6362.text: Ride to Thunder Bluff. This quest sends young Horde adventurers taking their first flight path across Kalimdor aboard a wind rider. Entrusted with a shipment of cured hides, travelers depart the dry crossroads of the Barrens to deliver valuable leatherwork supplies directly to the heights of Thunder Bluff. For many travelers making their way through the Barrens, booking a flight with Devrak marks their first journey through the skies on the back of a wind rider. These winged wyverns provide vital aerial links between the dispersed settlements of the fledgling Horde, avoiding the perilous ground routes prowled by quilboar and centaur packs. The shipment consists of a bundle of cured hides prepared in the Barrens and destined for Ahanu, a craftsman working out of Hewa's Armory in Thunder Bluff. Nestled right beneath the great wind rider roost on the central mesa, Ahanu relies on raw supplies brought in from hunting outposts across the plains to outfit local warriors and hunters.

quest:6363.text: Tal the Wind Rider Master. Tal the Wind Rider Master is a simple courier task connecting Mulgore leatherworkers with merchants in the Barrens. The leatherworker Ahanu entrusts a parcel of finished hides to be flown out of Thunder Bluff. Delivered directly to Tal, the mesa's flight master, it introduces fledgling Horde travelers to the wind rider transport network. Trade between Mulgore and the arid scrub of the Barrens is essential for the young Horde. Ahanu, a leatherworker selling his wares on Thunder Bluff's lower rise, produces durable leather goods intended for Jahan Hawkwing's trade stall at the Crossroads. Because the overland walk down the bluffs and through the golden plains takes hours on foot, merchants rely on winged couriers to ferry fragile or urgent parcels over the craggy divide. Perched upon the highest central tier of Thunder Bluff, Tal tends to the city's flock of wind riders—also known as wyverns. These intelligent, leathery-winged beasts are ideally suited for navigating Kalimdor's unpredictable thermal drafts and rugged peaks. Tal coordinates flights departing to outposts like the Crossroads, ensuring messengers and cargo pass quickly between the tauren capital and their orcish allies.

quest:6364.text: Return to Jahan. Return to Jahan marks the concluding leg of an introduction to the Horde's wind rider flight network between Mulgore and the Barrens. After visiting Thunder Bluff to deliver hides to the skinner Ahanu, travelers take a wyvern back to the Crossroads carrying finished leather wares for the merchant Jahan Hawkwing. For many travelers, this errand is their first experience soaring aboard a trained wind rider. Tal, the wind rider master perched high atop Thunder Bluff's central mesa, arranges flights across the plains of central Kalimdor. As long as a traveler has already established contact with the roost at another settlement—such as Devrak's outpost at the Crossroads—these winged beasts can effortlessly cover leagues that would otherwise demand a perilous overland trek through the Red Rocks and northern Barrens. The courier run serves an economic purpose alongside flight training. Jahan Hawkwing operates out of the bustling settlement of the Crossroads, where hunters, scouts, and mercenaries gather daily. Raw hides sent to Ahanu on the high rises of Thunder Bluff are refined into durable armor and equipment, then flown back to the dusty intersection of the Barrens to supply the Horde's expanding frontier efforts.

quest:6365.text: Meats to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sends a parcel of Barrens meat toward Orgrimmar. He asks young orc and troll adventurers to carry it to Devrak, the wind rider master, and learn the flight route to the Horde capital. Wildlife fills the Barrens, from zhevras and plainstriders to kodos and thunder lizards. Zargh has prepared choice cuts for a personal delivery to Gryshka, the innkeeper in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Rather than risk the long, dusty trek across the Southfury River into Durotar, he sends runners from the Crossroads to the wind rider perch. Meeting Devrak gives a young Horde warrior a first look at the wind rider flight network. Wind rider masters connect remote outposts like the Crossroads to the Horde's fortified seat of power in Orgrimmar. Devrak prepares you and the cargo for a swift flight over the savannah.

quest:6384.text: Ride to Orgrimmar. A wind rider carries Horde travelers from the Crossroads to Orgrimmar. With Zargh’s fresh cuts of meat in hand, you fly to the capital’s Skytower and deliver them to Innkeeper Gryshka. Devrak sends trained wind riders between the Crossroads and Orgrimmar. The flight crosses the dry Barrens and reaches Durotar’s red cliffs, sparing travelers the hard journey on foot. From high above the dusty canyon trails, the wyverns carry messengers and travelers, along with dispatches and trade goods, straight to the capital. Zargh has prepared fresh cuts of meat for Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Strength. From the central Skytower, her inn is a short walk away. Gryshka accepts the parcel and remarks with fondness that Zargh knows how to win a lady’s heart.

quest:6385.text: Doras the Wind Rider Master. Innkeeper Gryshka needs a courier to carry her thanks to Zargh at the Crossroads. She sends travelers to Doras the Wind Rider Master at Orgrimmar's skytower to arrange the flight back to the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka sends thanks to Zargh after a shipment of meat arrives safely from the Barrens hunting grounds. With no time to travel through Durotar herself, she trusts the established aerial courier network linking major Horde settlements to carry her letter back across the frontier. At the flight tower in the Valley of Strength, Doras oversees Orgrimmar's wind rider roost. The trained wyverns carry military messages and supplies between the capital and outposts such as the Crossroads, far faster than anyone traveling by foot or kodo cart.

quest:6386.text: Return to the Crossroads.. Gryshka's reply is on its way from Orgrimmar to Zargh at the Crossroads. A wind rider carries it across the distance between Durotar and the Barrens. You carry Gryshka's written reply to Zargh after bringing her a parcel of prime meat in Orgrimmar. Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's high bluffs, provides a mount for the return to the Barrens. You have already met Devrak at the Crossroads, so the wyverns know the flight path. The ride crosses the desert sky and saves you the long march overland across the Southfury River. Zargh's courtship has won Gryshka's warm reply. Quality provisions have pleased her, and Zargh celebrates, even musing about an impending wedding. The delivery also brings you back to the Barrens' central hub for travel.

quest:6387.text: Honor Students. Mining instructor Brock Stoneseeker rewards promising young apprentices in Thelsamar with honorary mining picks. To arrange delivery of the tools from Ironforge, he directs adventurers to enlist the aid of the local gryphon master, Thorgrum Borrelson. In the dwarf town of Thelsamar, mining is more than an occupation—it is a cornerstone of daily survival and dwarven pride. Brock Stoneseeker watches dozens of fresh recruits pass through his training, drilling them on rock composition and tunnel safety. For the students who distinguish themselves above the rest, tradition demands recognition in the form of a finely crafted honorary pick. Because local supply is limited, obtaining these picks requires reaching across Khaz Modan into the heart of Ironforge. Rather than trusting the slow, mountainous trek back through Dun Morogh on foot, Brock relies on the kingdom's aerial courier network. Thorgrum Borrelson tends the gryphon roost perched beside Thelsamar, offering rapid transit to the capital. Handing Brock's order to Thorgrum initiates a courier run that connects rural frontier training directly to the grand foundries of the dwarven capital.

quest:6388.text: Gryth Thurden. This errand introduces adventurers to Ironforge's gryphon network by tasking them with carrying a bundle of ceremonial tools to the city's gryphon master. Entrusted with the Honorary Picks by Golnir Bouldertoe, the courier must deliver them to Gryth Thurden so they can be dispatched back to Loch Modan. After traveling from Loch Modan to the Great Forge, couriers receive a bundle of Honorary Picks from Golnir Bouldertoe meant for Brock Stoneseeker's mining apprentices. Rather than making the trek back down the mountain passes on foot, Golnir advises taking advantage of the dwarven gryphon network, sending the messenger across the city to coordinate with Ironforge's master handler. Gryth Thurden manages the flight roosts within the great mountain hall, connecting Ironforge to dwarven settlements across Khaz Modan. Thurden agrees to arrange transport back to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar provided the adventurer has already scouted the route and spoken with the local handler there. The delivery teaches fledgling heroes the vital role aerial couriers play in tying the dwarven kingdom together.

quest:6391.text: Ride to Ironforge. Ride to Ironforge is an introductory courier quest that sends newly trained adventurers on their first gryphon flight from Thelsamar in Loch Modan into the dwarven capital. Entrusted with a list of top mining students from Brock Stoneseeker, the traveler carries the dispatch straight to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Great Forge. For many young mountaineers and travelers, the flight from Thelsamar to Ironforge marks their very first journey astride a gryphon. Handled by Gryphon Master Thorgrum Borrelson, this short passage carries travelers over Dun Morogh's snowy ridges and directly into the cavernous entry of the mountain fortress. The errand itself serves the Deep Mountain Mining Guild. Brock Stoneseeker regularly sends word of his most promising mining pupils from Thelsamar. Waiting at the Great Forge is Golnir Bouldertoe, who inscribes the apprentices' names onto ceremonial honorary picks to reward their hard work in Loch Modan's quarries and mines.

quest:6392.text: Return to Brock. Having delivered Brock Stoneseeker's missive to Ironforge, you are entrusted with a batch of Honorary Picks to carry back to Thelsamar. Taking advantage of the dwarven aerial transit network, you board a gryphon with Gryth Thurden to return quickly across the mountains. The great mountain stronghold of Ironforge relies on a coordinated network of gryphon roosts to maintain communication and trade with outlying settlements like Loch Modan. Gryth Thurden, Ironforge's gryphon master, oversees this transit from the city's central flight master platform. Because travelers must first establish a rapport with an aerie's handler before flying there, Gryth ensures you have already spoken with Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar before saddling a mount for the return trip. Your journey serves a practical purpose beyond introducing you to gryphon travel: Brock Stoneseeker, a respected mining instructor in Thelsamar, needs new equipment for his apprentices. With the Honorary Picks safely delivered to his hands, young miners across the valley can begin working the rich copper and tin veins that line the hills surrounding the Loch.

quest:6395.text: Marla's Last Wish. Marla's Last Wish is an early Forsaken task given by Novice Elreth in Deathknell. It asks you to hunt down the Scourge-enslaved remnants of Samuel Fipps so he can be buried beside his murdered wife, Marla. The task reflects the fledgling Forsaken society's yearning to honor human ties and distinguish themselves from the mindless Scourge. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Marla and Samuel Fipps lived together as husband and wife. When the plague swept through their lands, Samuel succumbed to the contagion and was reanimated as a mindless thrall of the Scourge. Though Marla was spared undeath, she could not escape Samuel himself, who brutally slew her in his mindless frenzy. Despite dying at her husband's hands, Marla harbored no hatred in her final moments. Her dying wish, remembered by Novice Elreth, was to rest eternally beside her husband in the Deathknell graveyard. Novice Elreth dispatches Forsaken adventurers northeast of Deathknell to locate Samuel Fipps, who still wanders among a ruined campsite. Putting an end to Samuel's torment serves a dual purpose: it cleanses an encroaching Scourge minion from the valley and allows his physical remains to be carried back to Marla's resting place. As Elreth emphasizes, honoring the deceased and respecting their final wishes is a vital moral distinction separating the newly liberated Forsaken from the mindless malice of the Scourge.

quest:64.text: The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, the Furlbrows have fled their farm, leaving a cherished heirloom behind. Recovering the pocket watch offers them a chance to salvage something personal from the chaos spreading through the region. Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts rose from the pumpkin patches in the night, waking them with little time to gather what they could carry. In the rush to flee, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse. Defias thugs and thieves, including Benny Blaanco, now pick through the abandoned Furlbrow farm. For ordinary folk, returning for a keepsake could mean death. By securing the pocket watch from the wardrobe, you restore a measure of dignity to a family that has lost nearly everything to Westfall's lawlessness.

quest:65.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's thieves threaten the farms and roads. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you from Sentinel Hill east into Redridge to seek a contact who may know where they hide. Westfall's harvests are gone, and bandits in red bandanas roam the land. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia hold Sentinel Hill under near-constant attack, but they do not know who directs their enemies. Stoutmantle knows that fighting stray looters will not save the region. He needs to find the cartel's inner circle and learn who commands it. Gryan Stoutmantle sets aside military channels and Stormwind's absent nobles, and calls on someone he knows. He sends trusted adventurers east, past Elwynn and into the Redridge Mountains. In Lakeshire, a quiet village by the lake, Wiley the Black waits on the upper floor of the local inn. The rogue knows the underworld better than any militia captain, and may offer the first lead to the Brotherhood's hideouts.

quest:6541.text: Report to Kadrak. At the Crossroads, Thork sends proven Horde fighters north to report to Kadrak. The orc holds a watch tower near the Ashenvale border and prepares recruits for the fighting ahead. The Crossroads faces quilboar, centaur, and local brigands, while the Horde looks north to Ashenvale's thick forests. Thork directs fighters who have proved themselves in the central Barrens to the northern border tower, where Kadrak is stationed. Kadrak oversees the southern approach to Ashenvale and organizes reinforcements for the Horde's foothold across the border. Splintertree Post and an outpost along the Zoram Strand help the Horde strengthen its presence in the timber-rich woodlands, where native night elves resist them fiercely.

quest:6543.text: The Warsong Reports. Kadrak sends couriers from the northern Barrens to gather reports across Ashenvale. The Warsong Reports carry orders and field observations from outriders near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand. Kadrak watches the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale from a fortified tower. The Horde needs the pass because the Barrens cannot supply the timber Orgrimmar requires. The Warsong clan has pushed into the ancient elven forest to reach those supplies. Couriers carry orders between scattered patrols and help keep them in step, while night elf ambushes threaten the wilderness trails. Warsong scouts watch three parts of Ashenvale. On the western coast, a runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches naga activity and other coastal threats along the Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, a scout coordinates defense against Sentinel raids. Farther east, an outrider watches the road toward the shattered ruins of Azshara. Their reports give Kadrak a view of night elf movements and weaknesses along the frontier.

quest:6608.text: You Too Good.. Lumak sends you from Orgrimmar to find his friend Nat Pagle. Your skill has outgrown ordinary lessons, and Nat camps on a distant islet south of Theramore Isle. Lumak trains fishers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He sees that you have learned all he can teach about rod and reel, and admits you are too good for ordinary lessons. To learn the art of artisan fishing, you must seek knowledge beyond the city and the Horde. Lumak sends you to find his human friend, Nat Pagle. He warns you not to harm or eat Nat, despite the friction between the Horde and Alliance across Kalimdor. Nat camps on an islet south of Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh. He keeps clear of politics and cares only whether the fish are biting.

quest:6611.text: To Gadgetzan You Go!. In Orgrimmar, Zamja sends Horde cooks south to learn from an eccentric goblin butcher. Zamja trains cooks in the Drag, where she feeds warriors and travelers passing through Durotar. When a cook has learned every recipe and technique she can teach, Zamja admits she has imparted all her culinary mojo. She sends her seasoned pupil to Tanaris, saying only a master of strange and exotic meats can help a talented cook advance further. In Tanaris, Gadgetzan is a steam-powered trading hub run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Dirge Quikcleave works inside the town tavern. The eccentric goblin butcher has an unconventional palate and no squeamishness about food. Across Kalimdor, he is known for turning monstrous desert creatures, and sometimes scraps of leather, into hearty meals for hardened adventurers.

quest:6623.text: Horde Trauma. At Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Horde Trauma calls skilled medics into front-line surgery. Doctor Gregory Victor, chief physician of the Horde's trauma division, seeks hands able to save lives under extreme pressure. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, the orc first aid trainer Arnok tells proficient healers that they have caught Doctor Gregory Victor's attention. Victor oversees Horde Trauma from Hammerfall, tucked away in the contested hills of the Arathi Highlands. Arnok regards the summons as the pinnacle of professional advancement for a battlefield surgeon. At Hammerfall, constant skirmishes with Stromgarde's forces and local hostile factions leave Victor inundated with wounded grunts, raiders, and scouts. The chief physician wastes no time welcoming recruits with pleasantries. Instead, he orders newcomers into their scrubs to prove their worth in brutal, fast-paced emergency triage.

quest:6962.text: Treats for Great-father Winter. At the Smokywood Pastures display in Orgrimmar, the Greatfather Winter performer is worn out from hearing holiday wishes. He asks you for gingerbread cookies and milk. The Greatfather Winter who greets visitors in the Valley of Strength works for Smokywood Pastures. Long hours listening to citizens speak of festive treats leave him hungry. He turns to passing travelers for warm baking and a cold drink. You can bake the cookies with Holiday Spices sold by Smokywood Pastures peddlers and Small Eggs gathered from wild birds. Bring them together with Ice Cold Milk from a local tavern, and the feast's organizers offer you festive cheer and a small token of gratitude.

quest:6984.text: A Smokywood Pastures' Thank You!. Great-father Winter waits in Orgrimmar to thank those who recovered Smokywood Pastures' stolen holiday treats. Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive a token of appreciation for bringing the supplies back. In Orgrimmar, Smokywood Pastures sells treats, recipes, and seasonal cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. Their shipment was stolen in the snowy hills of the Alterac Mountains, and business stalled. With the treats recovered and the Abominable Greench dealt with, Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive the company's thanks. Great-father Winter waits beside the holiday tree in the Valley of Strength. The goblins have arranged for him to honor those who rescued the holiday supplies with a seasonal blessing and a Smokywood Pastures Special Gift.

quest:7.text: Kobold Camp Cleanup. At Northshire, Kobold Camp Cleanup puts new recruits to their first test defending Stormwind's borders. Marshal McBride sends volunteers after kobolds in the northern woods, where their growing numbers threaten the abbey grounds. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and novice training. In recent years, Stormwind's forces have grown thin. With the King missing and royal garrisons scattered, wild creatures and opportunists press at civilization's edge. Marshal McBride directs the valley's defense from Northshire Abbey. He depends on fresh volunteers to keep threats from disrupting the abbey or endangering the surrounding vineyards. Kobolds are timid cave-dwellers with a strong attachment to candles. They usually pick at underground seams, far from direct sunlight. Now an entire clan has reached Northshire's northern timberline. If left unchecked, their numbers can turn scavenging into open raids. McBride sends recruits to thin their vanguard and test their resolve to defend the realm.

quest:730.text: Trouble in Darkshore?. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker seeks help for his missing crew. His introductory appeal sends travelers across the sea to Auberdine, where the dwarven expedition met Darkshore's wild, shadowy coast. Darnassus, the grand night elven capital, is home to dwarven researchers from Ironforge studying Kalimdor's ancient mysteries. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sent an excavation party across the water to Darkshore to unearth artifacts of antiquity. Weeks have passed without a message or progress report, and Greywhisker fears his field crew has met dangers they could not survive alone. Greywhisker laments that many in the Alliance dismiss dwarven archaeology as an eccentric hobby. Findings in Khaz Modan have convinced his colleagues that an ancient, terrifying force threatens Azeroth from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. The work in Darkshore's ruins is more than scholarship: it seeks to understand historic cataclysms and the deep-seated menaces buried beneath ancient soil.

quest:745.text: Sharing the Land. Assigned by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village, this task sends young Horde adventurers to curb the destructive poaching of the local Palemane gnolls. By culling their tanners, skinners, and poachers, you protect Mulgore's wildlife and learn the tauren philosophy of living in balance with the Earth Mother. The tauren hold deep reverence for the natural world, taking from it only what is necessary to survive and honoring the Earth Mother in all things. The Palemane gnolls, having settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, harbor no such respect. Rather than hunting in moderation, they aggressively butcher wildlife across the plains, leaving stripped carcasses and upset ecosystems in their wake. For a people striving to build a peaceful homeland in Mulgore, this reckless slaughter cannot be tolerated. Baine Bloodhoof initially hoped to resolve the matter peacefully, attempting to open dialogue with the encroaching gnolls. The Palemanes rejected every overture, answering diplomacy with hostility and continued devastation. Seeing that negotiation is futile, Baine turns to force. Young braves are sent directly to their hunting camps to put down the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer permanent damage. This mission serves as a rite of passage and a moral lesson for growing champions. Upon returning from the culling, Baine reminds the adventurer that taking life must never be done out of malice, but out of necessity to maintain harmony. Life and death exist as an interconnected circle where one cannot thrive without the other, a foundational truth every guardian of Mulgore must carry forward.

quest:746.text: Dwarven Digging. Dwarven Digging is a quest in Mulgore given by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village. Concerned that dwarven excavations will enrage the native beasts and defile the sacred earth, Baine tasks young Horde defenders with sabotaging their efforts by confiscating and shattering their pickaxes. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have begun staking out a dig site in the rolling hills of Mulgore. The Explorer's League and its excavation crews seek titan relics and earthen secrets across Kalimdor, but their operations rarely respect indigenous lands or customs. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother to be revered, not stripped and hollowed for stones and metal. Baine Bloodhoof recognizes that the dwarven machinery and relentless blasting threaten the fragile harmony of the plains. Beyond the physical destruction, the commotion agitates the local wildlife, stirring the plains kodos into frenzy. By smashing the prospectors' tools at their own forges, the tauren hope to send a blunt message and stall the encroachment before lasting harm is done.

quest:747.text: The Hunt Begins. The Hunt Begins is a foundational rite of passage for young adventurers in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Tasked by Grull Hawkwind, initiates are sent to hunt local plainstriders to provide meat and feathers for the village. Fulfilling this task marks the first step toward earning the respect of Chief Hawkwind and eventually gaining entry into Thunder Bluff. On the heights of Red Cloud Mesa, survival and tradition intertwine. The tauren hunt out of necessity to feed and clothe their people, while also viewing the stalk and chase as a vital test of discipline and sport. When the stores of Camp Narache run lean, the community looks to its rising youth to gather fresh plainstrider meat for cooking and sturdy feathers for tribal garments. No aspiring hero simply walks off Red Cloud Mesa into the wider reaches of Mulgore without proving their worth. Grull Hawkwind serves as a primary judge of character for the newcomers, insisting that one must prove their capability before stepping before his father, Chief Hawkwind. Bringing in a clean hunt demonstrates not only self-reliance, but devotion to supporting the tribe.

quest:748.text: Poison Water. Poison Water begins the tauren effort to purge pollution from Mulgore's sacred wells. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, young Horde defenders gather natural components from the plains to craft a restorative ritual totem. The grassy plains of Mulgore are sacred ground to the tauren, but insidious forces have begun threatening their vital lifeblood. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder stationed in Bloodhoof Village, discovers that goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted the precious water wells that sustain the tribes and the local wildlife. The pollution strikes directly at the spiritual heart of the nomadic people who recently settled here. To counteract industrial contaminants, Mull relies on traditional tauren shamanism rather than crude remedies. Cleansing the Winterhoof Water Well requires crafting a potent ritual totem imbued with the vitality of Mulgore's indigenous predators. He sends hunters to track prairie wolves for their paws and mature plainstriders for their talons across the southwestern plains, enlisting the strength of the land to heal its own wounds.

quest:7493.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. After Onyxia's fall, skilled leatherworkers in Orgrimmar learn how her scales can guard against the black dragonflight. Overlord Runthak recognizes their craft and teaches a rare technique for making protective cloaks, needed against the flames of Blackrock Spire. Onyxia's fall is a triumph for the Horde, yet the black dragonflight remains a threat. The broodmother's scaled hide resists draconic flame. Horde leaders seek craftsmen who can turn the dragon's remains into defensive armor rather than let them go to waste.

quest:7497.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly recognizes the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft needed to make a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can also work her hide. When an artisan with master leatherworking reports to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer recognizes how much those skills matter in the battles ahead.

quest:752.text: A Humble Task. A Humble Task is an early rite of duty given by Chief Hawkwind in Camp Narache. As the Chieftain attends to pressing tribal concerns on the Red Cloud Mesa, he asks a young adventurer to venture southeast and check on his elderly mother at the local water well. The request emphasizes communal responsibility, elder reverence, and the daily harmony essential to the tauren way of life. In the shadow of Camp Narache, every member of the tribe is expected to pull their weight and share in the harmony of life. For young tauren coming of age, tribal duty is not measured solely in battle prowess against quilboars or predators; it begins with basic social responsibility. Chief Hawkwind demonstrates this ethos directly: bound to his post by administrative and defensive leadership, he places his trust in novice adventurers to watch over the community's vulnerable elders. Mulgore's Red Cloud Mesa relies on vital natural water wells scattered beyond the perimeter of the encampment. Early in the morning, Greatmother Hawkwind left the village unattended to retrieve fresh water from the southeastern spring. In a land stalked by territorial wildlife and encroaching Bristleback quilboars, an elder remaining absent for hours raises quiet concern, prompting Hawkwind to send aid to ensure she is unharmed.

quest:753.text: A Humble Task. A Humble Task is an introductory rite of service in Red Cloud Mesa, where an elder tests a fledgling adventurer's humility and diligence. By carrying fresh well water across the plains to Camp Narache's leader, young tauren learn that serving their people starts with the simplest duties. Greatmother Hawkwind has walked many trails in her long life, and while her spirit remains steady, her legs no longer carry her across the plains with the speed of her youth. Stationed near the water well on the southern edges of Red Cloud Mesa, she tends to her responsibilities with patient resolve. When aspiring tribal defenders cross her path, she redirects their youthful energy toward practical community needs, offering them a chance to prove their worth through service rather than violence. The task asks the initiate to haul a filled water pitcher back northwest to Camp Narache and present it directly to the settlement's leader, Chief Hawkwind, who happens to be the Greatmother's son. In tauren society, survival across the arid plains of Mulgore demands shared labor and reliable supplies of fresh water. Demonstrating respect for the community's elders by shouldering their burdens is considered the cornerstone of becoming a true protector of the tribe. Chief Hawkwind sees more than a mere chore completed when a young wanderer arrives bearing water from his mother. In tauren custom, an individual's readiness to champion their people across wider lands begins with humility and an unprompted willingness to help. By demonstrating this quiet discipline, the initiate catches the chief's eye and earns recommendation for the ancient Rites of the Earthmother, the true spiritual tests that open the gates to Thunder Bluff.

quest:754.text: Winterhoof Cleansing. Winterhoof Cleansing is a rite entrusted to Horde adventurers by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. After goblin operations fouled the local springs, a consecrated totem must be carried into the Venture Company's territory to purify the Winterhoof Water Well. Restoring this spring is a vital first step in healing the poisoned waters of central Mulgore. The grassy plains of Mulgore rely on a delicate network of ancestral water wells to sustain both wild game and the scattered tauren tribes. Recently, ruthless industrial mercenaries of the Venture Company moved into the rolling hills southeast of Bloodhoof Village. Their operations have contaminated the local aquifers, leaving the Winterhoof Water Well rank and toxic. Wild beasts shun the tainted water, and the nearby camps face an impending crisis if the corruption spreads further through the earth. To counter the industrial filth, Mull Thunderhorn carves and enchants a ritual cleansing totem infused with the blessings of the Earth Mother. However, delivering this remedy requires braving armed Venture Company goons who have staked their claim over the spring. By placing the totem directly at the wellhead, an adventurer dispels the foul runoff, allowing clean, life-giving water to rise once more from the depths of the earth.

quest:756.text: Thunderhorn Totem. Thunderhorn Totem is a task given by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village to craft a sacred cleansing totem. To combat goblin-borne pollution spreading through Mulgore's water wells, young Horde champions must gather natural talons from plains predators to bind the land's primal strength into ritual wood. As the Venture Company's industrial exploitation poisons Mulgore's precious water sources, Mull Thunderhorn works urgently to craft remedies. Creating the Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem requires the natural essences of the plains' most focused hunters: prairie stalkers and flatland cougars. By taking the claws of these predators roaming east and west of Bloodhoof Village, the ritual channels the raw, uncorrupted predatory vigor of the wildlife directly into the totem. Tauren tradition sees a profound distinction between hunting for sustenance or spiritual balance and the wholesale plunder practiced by the goblins. Mull emphasizes that the purity with which native predators hunt is vital for purifying corrupted earth. Where goblin machinery defiles the springs with oil and industrial waste, the natural strength of the beasts contending with the land provides the spiritual catalyst needed to restore the Thunderhorn Water Well.

quest:757.text: Rite of Strength. The Rite of Strength is the initial trial in the traditional Rites of the Earthmother undertaken by young tauren at Camp Narache. To demonstrate their bravery and defense of the tribe, initiates must cull encroaching Bristleback quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine and present their belts to Chief Hawkwind. For a young tauren seeking recognition from tribal elders and eventual acceptance in Thunder Bluff, completing the Rites of the Earthmother is an essential duty. Bestowed by Seer Graytongue, the Rite of Strength serves as the starting trial. It demands physical courage and decisive action in defense of Red Cloud Mesa, testing whether an initiate can face the tribe's mortal foes without flinching. The chosen crucible for this trial is Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked gash east of Camp Narache occupied by Bristleback quilboar. These aggressive interlopers continuously trespass on ancestral lands, ambushing hunting parties and raiding camp supplies under cover of darkness. Slaying them and claiming their belts serves as both proof of valor and a necessary measure to keep the settlement secure.

quest:758.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing. Thunderhorn Cleansing is an essential spiritual rite in Mulgore, charging travelers with purifying the corrupted Thunderhorn Water Well. Armed with a ritual totem prepared by Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers restore the contaminated spring vital to the local tribe. Successful purification earns the heartfelt approval of the Thunderhorn ancestors. Water wells across the sweeping plains of Mulgore are vital lifelines for the tauren nomadic tribes who recently settled the grasslands. When foul poisons taint these underground springs, both wildlife and nearby settlements face devastating consequences. The Thunderhorn Water Well, situated north of Bloodhoof Village, fallen victim to contamination, requires deliberate spiritual intervention to heal the troubled land. To counteract the corruption, Mull Thunderhorn crafts a consecrated Cleansing Totem imbued with spiritual potency. Carrying this relic directly to the poisoned waters allows adventurers to channel ancestral power into the spring, dispersing the toxins and restoring pristine natural balance. Mull receives direct confirmation of the deed's success when the spirits of Thunderhorn ancestors visit him in a dream to express their enduring gratitude.

quest:759.text: Wildmane Totem. Wildmane Totem represents the third and final stage in Mull Thunderhorn's efforts to craft cleansing totems for Mulgore's poisoned wells. To restore the Wildmane Well, the ritual demands offerings taken from the territory's fiercest natural predators: prairie wolf alphas. After securing the materials required to consecrate totems for the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, only one afflicted source remains in central Mulgore: the Wildmane Well. The poisoned water across the plains threatens both migrating wildlife and settlements, demanding powerful primal ingredients to restore the earth's natural balance. To counter the potent corruption lingering in the northern waters, Mull Thunderhorn requires a sacrifice of ferocity. Prairie wolf alphas prowl the grasslands, particularly around the towering bluffs beneath Thunder Bluff. Harvesting their teeth channels the relentless drive and resilience of Mulgore's apex hunters directly into the crafting of the cleansing totem. In tauren spiritual tradition, drawing upon the land's creatures carries emotional and elemental weight. Mull views the gathering of alpha teeth not as conquest, but as a somber necessity where the sacrifice of Mulgore's predators helps heal the Earth Mother's stricken waters.

quest:76.text: The Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have overrun the Jasperlode Mine in eastern Elwynn. Marshal Dughan sends scouts to learn how far the infestation has spread. After kobolds swarmed the Fargodeep tunnels south of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan feared they had reached other mines. Jasperlode lies in the rocky foothills northeast of the Tower of Azora and supplies raw stone and metal to the kingdom. Dughan cannot spare Stormwind guards from their town patrols, so he sends independent adventurers east to see whether kobolds have taken this mine too. Scouts who reach Jasperlode's chambers find kobolds have driven out the human miners and fortified the dark passages. Marshal Dughan faces another blow as the crisis grows. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and royal troops are withheld from outlying territories. The local garrison has too few soldiers to clear the mines, leaving the kingdom's heart short of minerals and hemmed in by threats.

quest:760.text: Wildmane Cleansing. Wildmane Cleansing marks the culmination of the tauren ritual efforts to purify the vital watering holes of Mulgore. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, heroes take the completed Wildmane Totem north to cleanse the final poisoned well. Driving back goblin pollutants restores balance to the plains and secures the pastoral livelihood of the tauren tribes. Water is sacred lifeblood across the sun-drenched plains of Mulgore, sustaining the herds, the soil, and the nomadic tribes who have recently gathered around Thunder Bluff. When the Venture Company and encroaching goblins began contaminating these aquifers with toxic industrial runoff, the tauren elders recognized an existential threat. Following the purification of the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, the Wildmane Water Well stands as the third and final corrupted site requiring spiritual intervention. Crafted from specific elements gathered across the region, the Wildmane Cleansing Totem channels the restorative power of ancestral spirits and elemental earth. Planting the totem beside the foul waters north of Thunder Bluff disperses the foul chemicals, drawing out the toxins and reviving the natural flow. By completing the ritual, the tauren safeguard their people from disease and send an unmistakable message that the despoiling of their sacred ground will not be tolerated.

quest:763.text: Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the transition of a young tauren out of the secluded Red Cloud Mesa and into the wider plains of Mulgore. Having proven your mettle in Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sends you north to Bloodhoof Village with a carved totem to continue the ancient trials under Baine Bloodhoof. For generations, young tauren have tested their strength within the safe cradle of Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Completing the initial trials proves one has the discipline and resolve to survive, but the sacred Rites of the Earthmother require far more than surviving local wildlife. Chief Hawkwind recognizes when an initiate has outgrown the mesa's sheltered hunting grounds and must step into the broader community. To bridge the journey between Narache and the central settlements, Chief Hawkwind provides a hand-carved totem as a mark of introduction. Bearing this emblem down the winding path to Bloodhoof Village, you present yourself to Baine Bloodhoof, the young chieftain of the village and son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. The totem serves as testament to your readiness for the rites of spirit and wisdom that lie ahead.

quest:764.text: The Venture Co.. Investigating a ravaged Venture Company caravan in Mulgore uncovers an aggressive buildup of Venture Company goblins digging into the eastern hills. Having had their formal requests for mining permits flatly rejected, the company chose to quarry the Earth Mother's soil anyway, prompting Morin Cloudstalker to commission a lethal response. The tauren of Mulgore revere the land as an extension of the Earth Mother, cherishing its pristine plains and balanced wildlife. When the Venture Company approached the tribes seeking rights to blast and excavate the rolling hills for raw ore, their petitions were categorically denied. Undeterred by tribal decrees or territorial sovereignty, the relentless cartel sneaked heavy machinery, laborers, and overseers directly into Mulgore's eastern ridges to mine illicitly. Tauren scouts like Morin Cloudstalker recognize that corporate greed cannot be reasoned with through diplomatic appeals once picks hit the stone. With documents recovered from a ravaged Venture Co. caravan confirming the company's mining operation, Morin dispatches Horde champions to cut down both the taskmasters cracking the whips and the laborers driving the drills. The bloody reprisal is intended to ensure the Venture Company calculates the cost of trespassing as far too steep.

quest:765.text: Supervisor Fizsprocket. Supervisor Fizsprocket is a high-ranking Venture Company overseer stationed within the mining tunnels of Mulgore. Charged by Morin Cloudstalker with putting an end to the goblin enterprise's calculated pillaging, Horde adventurers enter the mine to eliminate him and recover his detailed clipboard. Documents recovered from a destroyed Venture Company caravan revealed that the Venture Company was not merely digging for ore—they were deliberately formulating schemes to drive the tauren from Mulgore entirely. By uprooting the locals, the rapacious corporation sought unchecked freedom to strip the rolling hills and deep subterranean veins of every natural resource.

quest:766.text: Mazzranache. Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village has fallen victim to a venomous bite from Mazzranache, a legendary plainstrider that terrorized his grandfather a generation ago. Struck by fever and delirious nightmares, the tauren requires a potent remedy brewed from Mulgore's wildlife before the infection claims his life. For years, Maur Raincaller regarded Mazzranache as little more than a harrowing family tale passed down by his grandfather. The elder tauren spoke of an unusually savage plainstrider armed with glowing red eyes, razor-sharp talons, and a toxic bite that defied the peaceful nature of most Mulgore wildlife. When Maur crossed paths with the beast out on the open grass, the legend proved all too real, leaving him severely wounded and struggling to make it back to safety. The creature's venom works swiftly, inducing high fevers and nightmarish delirium. To purge the venom before it turns fatal, traditional tauren medicine relies on the vitality of the local beasts. Maur requires a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, a plainstrider scale, and a swoop gizzard. By combining the essences of these varied hunters and scavengers, he can brew a concoction capable of halting the necrotic spread and nursing him back to health.

quest:767.text: Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a pivotal coming-of-age trial within the Rites of the Earthmother, testing a young adventurer's spiritual maturity. Initiated by Baine Bloodhoof, the quest directs aspirants to seek counsel from the village seer, Zarlman Two-Moons. Undertaking this journey is essential for anyone seeking the blessings and respect of the elders on the rises of Thunder Bluff. For generations, the nomadic tauren have turned to the Earthmother to guide their people across the plains of Kalimdor. Now gathered within the safe borders of Mulgore, their spiritual traditions remain the cornerstone of their society. The Rite of Vision is one of the ancient trials known as the Rites of the Earthmother. While earlier trials test an initiate's physical strength and connection to the hunt, the Rite of Vision demands an inward journey, directing young tauren and honored allies to commune directly with the spirits. Before any spiritual vision can be sought, an initiate must be prepared by someone steeped in ancient wisdom. In Bloodhoof Village, that responsibility falls to the revered shaman Zarlman Two-Moons. Entrusted by Baine Bloodhoof to prepare travelers, Zarlman possesses the keen sight to recognize those walking the path of the ancestors, offering the preliminary rites and sacred preparations necessary to pierce the veil of the physical world.

quest:771.text: Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a foundational spiritual trial undergone by young tauren stepping beyond the Red Cloud Mesa into greater Mulgore. To pierce the veil and receive guidance from ancestral spirits, initiates must gather natural reagents to brew the Water of the Seers under the watchful eye of Zarlman Two-Moons in Bloodhoof Village. Before any vision can be granted, the initiate must demonstrate an intimate understanding of the natural gifts found across Mulgore. Zarlman Two-Moons instructs the seeker to collect well stones found near the sacred communal water wells and ambercorn fallen beneath the roots of Mulgore's ancient trees. These natural elements are not merely physical objects; to the tauren, they hold the latent magic and lifeblood of the Earth Mother, ready to be channeled into ritual use. Once gathered, Zarlman combines the stones and ambercorn into the potent Water of the Seers. When consumed beside the village's tribal flame, this ceremonial draft clears the mind and summons an ethereal guide. Following this manifestation across the plains forms the true heart of the rite, testing the initiate's ability to walk between the physical world and the spiritual whispers of the land.

quest:772.text: Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is the spiritual climax of an ancient trial undertaken by young tauren in Bloodhoof Village. By drinking the sacred Water of the Seers beside the tribal bonfire, initiates summon a spectral guide to lead them toward their destiny. After gathering the necessary ritual herbs and passing the initial trials of faith, an initiate is granted the Water of the Seers by the village shaman, Zarlman Two-Moons. This potent draught must be ingested before the roaring tribal fire at the heart of Bloodhoof Village. When consumed with a focused and respectful mind, the sacred waters expand the drinker's perception beyond physical sight, bridging the veil between the material plane and the spiritual realm. Upon drinking the brew, the flames yield an ethereal apparition: an ancestral ghost wolf. The spirit does not speak or fight, but silently lopes northwest across the rolling plains of Mulgore. A true initiate must heed its quiet path, tracking its journey away from the village and deep into the rocky hills where the hermit Seer Wiserunner awaits in secluded meditation. Reaching Seer Wiserunner at the mouth of his mountain cavern signifies the successful completion of the vision. This journey across the grassy hills tests an initiate's patience, trust in ancestral guidance, and attunement to the Earth Mother. Passing this rite grants the young adventurer the right to undergo the ultimate test of adulthood: the Rite of Wisdom.

quest:773.text: Rite of Wisdom. The Rite of Wisdom is the concluding trial in the traditional Rites of the Earthmother undertaken by young adventurers in Mulgore. After purifying their sight through the Rite of Vision, petitioners travel to the sacred burial grounds of Red Rocks to commune with an Ancestral Spirit and receive the blessing of the dead. Having cleared their perception through the Rite of Vision, young protectors are directed east of Thunder Bluff toward Red Rocks. This ancient burial ground holds the physical remains and lingering spirits of those who fought and died to carve out a peaceful existence in Mulgore.
